.navbar-ct-mini{font-size:114%;margin:0 4em}</style><div class="navbar plainlinks hlist navbar-mini"><ul><li class="nv-view"><a href="/wiki/Template:Catholic_Church_sidebar" title="Template:Catholic <p><b>Pope Francis</b> (<a href="/wiki/Latin_language" class="mw-redirect" title="Latin language">Latin</a>: <i lang="la">Franciscus</i>; <a href="/wiki/Italian_language" title="Italian language">Italian</a>: <i lang="it">Francesco</i>; <a href="/wiki/Spanish_language" title="Spanish language">Spanish</a>: <i lang="es">Francisco</i>; born <b>Jorge Mario Bergoglio</b>,<sup id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3">&#91;b&#93;</a></sup> 17 December 1936) is the head of the <a href="/wiki/Catholic_Church" title="Catholic Church">Catholic Church</a>, the bishop of <a href="/wiki/Rome" title="Rome">Rome</a> and sovereign of the <a href="/wiki/Vatican_City_State" class="mw-redirect" title="Vatican City State">Vatican City State</a>. Francis is the first <a href="/wiki/Pope" title="Pope">pope</a> to be a member of the <a href="/wiki/Society_of_Jesus" class="mw-redirect" title="Society of Jesus">Society of Jesus</a>, the first from the Americas, the first from the <a href="/wiki/Southern_Hemisphere" title="Southern Hemisphere">Southern Hemisphere</a>, and the first pope from outside Europe since <a href="/wiki/Pope_Gregory_III" title="Pope Gregory III">Gregory III</a>, a Syrian who reigned in the 8th century.
</p><p>Born in <a href="/wiki/Buenos_Aires" title="Buenos Aires">Buenos Aires</a>, Argentina, Bergoglio worked for a time as a <a href="/wiki/Bouncer_(doorman)" class="mw-redirect" title="Bouncer (doorman)">bouncer</a> and a <a href="/wiki/Janitor" title="Janitor">janitor</a> as a young man before training to be a chemist and working as a technician in a <a href="/wiki/Food_science" title="Food science">food science</a> laboratory. After recovering from a severe illness, he was inspired to join the <a href="/wiki/Jesuits" title="Jesuits">Society of Jesus</a> (Jesuits) in 1958. He was ordained a <a href="/wiki/Catholic_priest" class="mw-redirect" title="Catholic priest">Catholic priest</a> in 1969, and from 1973 to 1979 was the Jesuit <a href="/wiki/Provincial_superior" title="Provincial superior">provincial superior</a> in Argentina. He became the <a href="/wiki/Archbishop_of_Buenos_Aires" class="mw-redirect" title="Archbishop of Buenos Aires">Archbishop of Buenos Aires</a> in 1998 and was created a <a href="/wiki/Cardinal_(Catholic_Church)" title="Cardinal (Catholic Church)">cardinal</a> in 2001 by <a href="/wiki/Pope_John_Paul_II" title="Pope John Paul II">Pope John Paul II</a>. He led the Argentine Church during the <a href="/wiki/December_2001_riots_in_Argentina" title="December 2001 riots in Argentina">December 2001 riots in Argentina</a>. The administrations of <a href="/wiki/N%C3%A9stor_Kirchner" title="Néstor Kirchner">Néstor Kirchner</a> and <a href="/wiki/Cristina_Fern%C3%A1ndez_de_Kirchner" title="Cristina Fernández de Kirchner">Cristina Fernández de Kirchner</a> considered him to be a political rival. Following the <a href="/wiki/Resignation_of_Pope_Benedict_XVI" title="Resignation of Pope Benedict XVI">resignation of Pope Benedict XVI</a> on 28 February 2013, <a href="/wiki/2013_papal_conclave" title="2013 papal conclave">a papal conclave</a> elected Bergoglio as his successor on 13 March. He chose Francis as his <a href="/wiki/Papal_name" title="Papal name">papal name</a> in honor of <a href="/wiki/Saint_Francis_of_Assisi" class="mw-redirect" title="Saint Francis of Assisi">Saint Francis of Assisi</a>. Throughout his public life, Francis has been noted for his humility, emphasis on God's mercy, international visibility as pope, concern for the poor, and commitment to <a href="/wiki/Pope_Francis:_ecumenism_and_interreligious_dialogue" class="mw-redirect" title="Pope Francis: ecumenism and interreligious dialogue">interreligious dialogue</a>. He is credited with having a less formal approach to the papacy than his predecessors, for instance choosing to reside in the <a href="/wiki/Domus_Sanctae_Marthae" title="Domus Sanctae Marthae">Domus Sanctae Marthae</a> guesthouse rather than in the <a href="/wiki/Papal_apartments" title="Papal apartments">papal apartments</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Apostolic_Palace" title="Apostolic Palace">Apostolic Palace</a> used by previous popes.
</p><p>Francis maintains the views of the church regarding the <a href="/wiki/Ordination_of_women_and_the_Catholic_Church" title="Ordination of women and the Catholic Church">ordination of women as priests</a>, but has initiated dialogue on the possibility of <a href="/wiki/Deaconess" title="Deaconess">deaconesses</a> and has made women full members of <a href="/wiki/Dicasteries" class="mw-redirect" title="Dicasteries">dicasteries</a> in the <a href="/wiki/Roman_Curia" title="Roman Curia">Roman Curia</a>. He maintains that the church should be more open and welcoming for members of the <a href="/wiki/LGBT_community" title="LGBT community">LGBT community</a>. Francis is an outspoken critic of unbridled <a href="/wiki/Capitalism" title="Capitalism">capitalism</a> and <a href="/wiki/Free_market_economics" class="mw-redirect" title="Free market economics">free market economics</a>, <a href="/wiki/Consumerism" title="Consumerism">consumerism</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Overdevelopment" title="Overdevelopment">overdevelopment</a>;<sup id="cite_ref-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-4">&#91;2&#93;</a></sup> he advocates taking action on <a href="/wiki/Climate_change" title="Climate change">climate change</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-5">&#91;3&#93;</a></sup> a focus of his papacy with the promulgation of <i><a href="/wiki/Laudato_si%27" title="Laudato si&#39;">Laudato si'</a></i>. In international diplomacy, he helped to restore <a href="/wiki/United_States%E2%80%93Cuban_Thaw" class="mw-redirect" title="United States–Cuban Thaw">full diplomatic relations between the United States and Cuba</a>, <a href="/wiki/Theology_of_Pope_Francis#Refugees_and_migrants" title="Theology of Pope Francis">supported the cause of refugees</a> during the <a href="/wiki/European_migrant_crisis" class="mw-redirect" title="European migrant crisis">European</a> and <a href="/wiki/Central_American_migrant_caravans" title="Central American migrant caravans">Central American migrant</a> crises, and made a deal with China to define how much influence the nation has in appointing their Catholic bishops. He has faced criticism from theological conservatives on many questions, especially what some interpret as his suggestion in a footnote of <i><a href="/wiki/Amoris_Laetitia" class="mw-redirect" title="Amoris Laetitia">Amoris Laetitia</a></i> that divorced and remarried Catholics may be admitted to receive the <a href="/wiki/Eucharist" title="Eucharist">Eucharist</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Burton2018_6-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Burton2018-6">&#91;4&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<meta property="mw:PageProp/toc" />
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Early_years">Early years</span></h2>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Jorge_Mario_Bergoglio_attended_a_salesian_school_between_1948_and_1949.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/06/Jorge_Mario_Bergoglio_attended_a_salesian_school_between_1948_and_1949.jpg/220px-Jorge_Mario_Bergoglio_attended_a_salesian_school_between_1948_and_1949.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="151" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/06/Jorge_Mario_Bergoglio_attended_a_salesian_school_between_1948_and_1949.jpg/330px-Jorge_Mario_Bergoglio_attended_a_salesian_school_between_1948_and_1949.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/06/Jorge_Mario_Bergoglio_attended_a_salesian_school_between_1948_and_1949.jpg/440px-Jorge_Mario_Bergoglio_attended_a_salesian_school_between_1948_and_1949.jpg 2x" data-file-width="960" data-file-height="657" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Jorge_Mario_Bergoglio_attended_a_salesian_school_between_1948_and_1949.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>Jorge Mario Bergoglio (fourth boy from the left in the third row from the top) at age 12, Salesian College (c. 1948–49)</div></div></div>
<p>Jorge Mario Bergoglio was born on 17 December 1936<sup id="cite_ref-directory_7-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-directory-7">&#91;5&#93;</a></sup> in <a href="/wiki/Flores,_Buenos_Aires" title="Flores, Buenos Aires">Flores</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-Remeseira_8-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Remeseira-8">&#91;6&#93;</a></sup> a <a href="/wiki/Subdivisions_of_Buenos_Aires" title="Subdivisions of Buenos Aires">neighborhood</a> of <a href="/wiki/Buenos_Aires" title="Buenos Aires">Buenos Aires</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-directory_7-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-directory-7">&#91;5&#93;</a></sup> He was the eldest<sup id="cite_ref-Garrido_9-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Garrido-9">&#91;7&#93;</a></sup> of five children of Mario José Bergoglio (1908–1959) and Regina María Sívori (1911–1981). Mario Bergoglio was an <a href="/wiki/Italian_Argentine" class="mw-redirect" title="Italian Argentine">Italian immigrant</a> accountant<sup id="cite_ref-biografia_10-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-biografia-10">&#91;8&#93;</a></sup> born in <a href="/wiki/Portacomaro" title="Portacomaro">Portacomaro</a> (<a href="/wiki/Province_of_Asti" title="Province of Asti">Province of Asti</a>) in Italy's <a href="/wiki/Piedmont" title="Piedmont">Piedmont</a> region. Regina Sívori<sup id="cite_ref-Sivori_11-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Sivori-11">&#91;9&#93;</a></sup> was a housewife born in Buenos Aires to a family of <a href="/wiki/Northern_Italy" title="Northern Italy">northern Italian</a> (Piedmontese-Genoese) origin.<sup id="cite_ref-guardian_12-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-guardian-12">&#91;10&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Donovan_13-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Donovan-13">&#91;11&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Henderson_14-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Henderson-14">&#91;12&#93;</a></sup> Mario José's family left Italy in 1929 to escape the fascist rule of <a href="/wiki/Benito_Mussolini" title="Benito Mussolini">Benito Mussolini</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTERosalesOlivera20135_15-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTERosalesOlivera20135-15">&#91;13&#93;</a></sup> According to María Elena Bergoglio (born 1948), the pope's only living sibling, they did not emigrate for economic reasons.<sup id="cite_ref-fascism_16-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-fascism-16">&#91;14&#93;</a></sup> His other siblings were Oscar Adrián (1938–deceased), Marta Regina (1940–2007), and Alberto Horacio (1942–2010).<sup id="cite_ref-17" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-17">&#91;15&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-18" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-18">&#91;16&#93;</a></sup> Two great-nephews, Antonio and Joseph, died in a traffic collision.<sup id="cite_ref-Tribune_19-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Tribune-19">&#91;17&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-nephews_20-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-nephews-20">&#91;18&#93;</a></sup> His niece, <a href="/wiki/Cristina_Bergoglio" title="Cristina Bergoglio">Cristina Bergoglio</a>, is a painter based in <a href="/wiki/Madrid" title="Madrid">Madrid</a>, Spain.<sup id="cite_ref-21" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-21">&#91;19&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-22" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-22">&#91;20&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In the sixth grade, Bergoglio attended Wilfrid Barón de los Santos Ángeles, a school of the <a href="/wiki/Salesians_of_Don_Bosco" title="Salesians of Don Bosco">Salesians of Don Bosco</a>, in <a href="/wiki/Ramos_Mej%C3%ADa" title="Ramos Mejía">Ramos Mejía</a>, <a href="/wiki/Buenos_Aires_Province" title="Buenos Aires Province">Buenos Aires Province</a>. He attended the technical secondary school Escuela Técnica Industrial N° 27 Hipólito Yrigoyen,<sup id="cite_ref-techniciandegree_23-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-techniciandegree-23">&#91;21&#93;</a></sup> named after <a href="/wiki/Hip%C3%B3lito_Yrigoyen" title="Hipólito Yrigoyen">a past Argentine president</a>, and graduated with a chemical technician's diploma<sup id="cite_ref-directory_7-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-directory-7">&#91;5&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-bio_24-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-bio-24">&#91;22&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-25" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-25">&#91;23&#93;</a></sup> (not a master's degree in chemistry, as some media outlets incorrectly reported).<sup id="cite_ref-26" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-26">&#91;24&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-27" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-27">&#91;25&#93;</a></sup> In that capacity, he spent several years working in the food section of Hickethier-Bachmann Laboratory,<sup id="cite_ref-Clarin_28-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Clarin-28">&#91;26&#93;</a></sup> where he worked under <a href="/wiki/Esther_Ballestrino" title="Esther Ballestrino">Esther Ballestrino</a>. Prior to working as a chemical technician, Bergoglio had also worked as a bar bouncer and as a janitor sweeping floors.<sup id="cite_ref-burke_29-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-burke-29">&#91;27&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Chua_30-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Chua-30">&#91;28&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>When he was 21 years old, he suffered from life-threatening <a href="/wiki/Pneumonia" title="Pneumonia">pneumonia</a> and three <a href="/wiki/Cysts" class="mw-redirect" title="Cysts">cysts</a>. He had part of a lung excised shortly afterwards.<sup id="cite_ref-techniciandegree_23-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-techniciandegree-23">&#91;21&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-reuters_31-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-reuters-31">&#91;29&#93;</a></sup> Bergoglio has been a lifelong supporter of <a href="/wiki/San_Lorenzo_de_Almagro" title="San Lorenzo de Almagro">San Lorenzo de Almagro</a> <a href="/wiki/Association_football" title="Association football">football</a> club.<sup id="cite_ref-Lorenzo_32-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Lorenzo-32">&#91;30&#93;</a></sup> Bergoglio is also a fan of the films of <a href="/wiki/Tita_Merello" title="Tita Merello">Tita Merello</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-aicabio_33-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-aicabio-33">&#91;31&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Neorealism_(art)#Films" title="Neorealism (art)">neorealism</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Tango" title="Tango">tango</a> dancing, with a fondness for the traditional music of Argentina and <a href="/wiki/Uruguay" title="Uruguay">Uruguay</a> known as the <i><a href="/wiki/Milonga_(music)" title="Milonga (music)">milonga</a></i>.<sup id="cite_ref-aicabio_33-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-aicabio-33">&#91;31&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span id="Jesuit_.281958.E2.80.932013.29"></span><span class="mw-headline" id="Jesuit_(1958–2013)">Jesuit (1958–2013)</span></h2>
<p>Bergoglio found his vocation to the priesthood while he was on his way to celebrate the <a href="/wiki/Spring_Day_(Argentina)" class="mw-redirect" title="Spring Day (Argentina)">Spring Day</a>. He passed by a church to go to <a href="/wiki/Sacrament_of_Penance_%26_Reconciliation_(Catholic_Church)" class="mw-redirect" title="Sacrament of Penance &amp; Reconciliation (Catholic Church)">confession</a>, and was inspired by the priest.<sup id="cite_ref-34" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-34">&#91;32&#93;</a></sup> Bergoglio studied at the archdiocesan <a href="/wiki/Seminary" title="Seminary">seminary</a>, <a href="/wiki/Inmaculada_Concepci%C3%B3n_Seminary" title="Inmaculada Concepción Seminary">Inmaculada Concepción Seminary</a>, in <a href="/wiki/Villa_Devoto" title="Villa Devoto">Villa Devoto</a>, Buenos Aires, and, after three years, entered the Society of Jesus as a novice on 11 March 1958.<sup id="cite_ref-aicabio_33-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-aicabio-33">&#91;31&#93;</a></sup> Bergoglio has said that, as a young seminarian, he had a crush on a girl he met and briefly doubted about continuing the religious career.<sup id="cite_ref-celibacy_35-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-celibacy-35">&#91;33&#93;</a></sup> As a Jesuit novice he studied humanities in <a href="/wiki/Santiago" title="Santiago">Santiago</a>, Chile.<sup id="cite_ref-36" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-36">&#91;34&#93;</a></sup> After his novitiate in the Society of Jesus, Bergoglio officially became a Jesuit on 12 March 1960, when he made the religious profession of the initial, perpetual vows of <a href="/wiki/Poverty,_chastity_and_obedience" class="mw-redirect" title="Poverty, chastity and obedience">poverty, chastity and obedience</a> of a member of the order.<sup id="cite_ref-37" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-37">&#91;35&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-RO42_38-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-RO42-38">&#91;36&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In 1960, Bergoglio obtained a <a href="/wiki/Licentiate_(degree)" title="Licentiate (degree)">licentiate</a> in philosophy from the <a href="/wiki/Colegio_M%C3%A1ximo_de_San_Jos%C3%A9" title="Colegio Máximo de San José">Colegio Máximo de San José</a> in <a href="/wiki/San_Miguel,_Buenos_Aires" title="San Miguel, Buenos Aires">San Miguel</a>, Buenos Aires Province. He taught literature and <a href="/wiki/Psychology" title="Psychology">psychology</a> at the <a href="/w/index.php?title=Colegio_de_la_Inmaculada_Concepci%C3%B3n_(Argentina)&amp;action=edit&amp;redlink=1" class="new" title="Colegio de la Inmaculada Concepción (Argentina) (page does not exist)">Colegio de la Inmaculada Concepción</a>, a high school in <a href="/wiki/Santa_Fe,_Argentina" title="Santa Fe, Argentina">Santa Fe</a>, from 1964 to 1965. In 1966, he taught the same courses at the <a href="/wiki/Colegio_del_Salvador_(Argentina)" class="mw-redirect" title="Colegio del Salvador (Argentina)">Colegio del Salvador</a> in Buenos Aires.<sup id="cite_ref-directory_7-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-directory-7">&#91;5&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-39" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-39">&#91;37&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span id="Presbyterate_.281969.E2.80.931992.29"></span><span class="mw-headline" id="Presbyterate_(1969–1992)">Presbyterate (1969–1992)</span></h3>
<p>In 1967 Bergoglio began his theological studies at <a href="/wiki/Facultades_de_Filosof%C3%ADa_y_Teolog%C3%ADa_de_San_Miguel" title="Facultades de Filosofía y Teología de San Miguel">Facultades de Filosofía y Teología de San Miguel</a> and on 13 December 1969 was <a href="/wiki/Holy_Orders" class="mw-redirect" title="Holy Orders">ordained</a> to the priesthood by Archbishop <a href="/wiki/Ram%C3%B3n_Jos%C3%A9_Castellano" title="Ramón José Castellano">Ramón José Castellano</a>. He served as the <a href="/wiki/Master_of_novices" class="mw-redirect" title="Master of novices">master of novices</a> for the province there and became a professor of theology.<sup id="cite_ref-40" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-40">&#91;38&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Bergoglio completed his final stage of spiritual training as a Jesuit, <a href="/wiki/Tertianship" title="Tertianship">tertianship</a>, at <a href="/wiki/Alcal%C3%A1_de_Henares" title="Alcalá de Henares">Alcalá de Henares</a>, Spain, and took final, solemn vows as a Jesuit, including the <a href="/wiki/Fourth_vow" title="Fourth vow">fourth vow</a> of obedience to missioning by the pope, on 22 April 1973.<sup id="cite_ref-RO42_38-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-RO42-38">&#91;36&#93;</a></sup> He was named <a href="/wiki/Provincial_superior" title="Provincial superior">provincial superior</a> of the Society of Jesus in Argentina that July, for a six-year term which ended in 1979.<sup id="cite_ref-directory_7-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-directory-7">&#91;5&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-sjvows_41-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-sjvows-41">&#91;39&#93;</a></sup> In 1973, shortly after being named provincial superior, he had made a <a href="/wiki/Christian_pilgrimage" title="Christian pilgrimage">pilgrimage</a> to Jerusalem but his stay was shortened by the outbreak of the <a href="/wiki/Yom_Kippur_War" title="Yom Kippur War">Yom Kippur War</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-travel_42-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-travel-42">&#91;40&#93;</a></sup> After the completion of his term of office, in 1980 he was named the <a href="/wiki/Rector_(academic)" class="mw-redirect" title="Rector (academic)">rector</a> of the Philosophical and Theological Faculty of San Miguel where he had studied.<sup id="cite_ref-43" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-43">&#91;41&#93;</a></sup> Before taking up this new appointment, he spent the first three months of 1980 in Ireland to learn English, staying at the Jesuit Centre at the <a href="/wiki/Milltown_Institute_of_Theology_and_Philosophy" title="Milltown Institute of Theology and Philosophy">Milltown Institute of Theology and Philosophy</a>, <a href="/wiki/Dublin" title="Dublin">Dublin</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-44" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-44">&#91;42&#93;</a></sup> He served at San Miguel for six years until 1986<sup id="cite_ref-directory_7-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-directory-7">&#91;5&#93;</a></sup> when, at the discretion of Jesuit superior-general <a href="/wiki/Peter_Hans_Kolvenbach" title="Peter Hans Kolvenbach">Peter Hans Kolvenbach</a>, he was replaced by someone more in tune with the worldwide trend in the Society of Jesus toward emphasizing social justice, rather than his emphasis on popular religiosity and direct pastoral work.<sup id="cite_ref-ReferenceA_45-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ReferenceA-45">&#91;43&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>He spent several months at the <a href="/wiki/Sankt_Georgen_Graduate_School_of_Philosophy_and_Theology" title="Sankt Georgen Graduate School of Philosophy and Theology">Sankt Georgen Graduate School of Philosophy and Theology</a> in Frankfurt, Germany, considering possible <a href="/wiki/Dissertation" class="mw-redirect" title="Dissertation">dissertation</a> topics.<sup id="cite_ref-46" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-46">&#91;44&#93;</a></sup> He settled on exploring the work of the German / Italian theologian <a href="/wiki/Romano_Guardini" title="Romano Guardini">Romano Guardini</a>, particularly his study of 'Contrast' published in his 1925 work <i>Der Gegensatz</i>. However, he was to return to Argentina prematurely to serve as a <a href="/wiki/Confessor" title="Confessor">confessor</a> and <a href="/wiki/Spiritual_director" class="mw-redirect" title="Spiritual director">spiritual director</a> to the Jesuit community in <a href="/wiki/C%C3%B3rdoba,_Argentina" title="Córdoba, Argentina">Córdoba</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-litoral_47-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-litoral-47">&#91;45&#93;</a></sup> It was believed that while in Germany, he saw the painting of <a href="/wiki/Mary,_Untier_of_Knots" title="Mary, Untier of Knots">Mary, Untier of Knots</a> in <a href="/wiki/Augsburg" title="Augsburg">Augsburg</a> and brought a copy of the painting to Argentina, but in an interview for the German newsweekly <i>Die Zeit</i> in 2017, Pope Francis stated that he had never been to Augsburg.<sup id="cite_ref-48" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-48">&#91;46&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-51" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-51">&#91;c&#93;</a></sup> As a student at the Salesian school, Bergoglio was mentored by <a href="/wiki/Ukrainian_Greek_Catholic" class="mw-redirect" title="Ukrainian Greek Catholic">Ukrainian Greek Catholic</a> priest <a href="/wiki/Stefan_Czmil" title="Stefan Czmil">Stefan Czmil</a>. Bergoglio often rose hours before his classmates to serve <a href="/wiki/Divine_Liturgy" title="Divine Liturgy">Divine Liturgy</a> for Czmil.<sup id="cite_ref-52" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-52">&#91;49&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-greek_53-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-greek-53">&#91;50&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Bergoglio was asked in 1992 by Jesuit authorities not to reside in Jesuit houses, because of continued tensions with Jesuit leaders and scholars, a sense of Bergoglio's "dissent," views of his Catholic orthodoxy and his opposition to <a href="/wiki/Liberation_theology" title="Liberation theology">theology of liberation</a>, and his work as auxiliary bishop of Buenos Aires.<sup id="cite_ref-ncronline.org_54-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ncronline.org-54">&#91;51&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-55" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-55">&#91;52&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-56" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-56">&#91;53&#93;</a></sup> As a bishop he was no longer subject to his Jesuit superior.<sup id="cite_ref-57" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-57">&#91;54&#93;</a></sup> From then on, he did not visit Jesuit houses and was in "virtual estrangement from the Jesuits" until after his election as pope.<sup id="cite_ref-ReferenceA_45-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ReferenceA-45">&#91;43&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-ncronline.org_54-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ncronline.org-54">&#91;51&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span id="Pre-papal_episcopate_.281992.E2.80.932013.29"></span><span class="mw-headline" id="Pre-papal_episcopate_(1992–2013)">Pre-papal episcopate (1992–2013)</span></h3>
<p>Bergoglio was named Auxiliary Bishop of Buenos Aires in 1992 and <a href="/wiki/Episcopal_ordination" class="mw-redirect" title="Episcopal ordination">consecrated</a> on 27 June 1992 as <a href="/wiki/Auca_(titular_diocese)" class="mw-redirect" title="Auca (titular diocese)">titular bishop of Auca</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-directory_7-6" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-directory-7">&#91;5&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-58" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-58">&#91;55&#93;</a></sup> with Cardinal <a href="/wiki/Antonio_Quarracino" title="Antonio Quarracino">Antonio Quarracino</a>, archbishop of Buenos Aires, serving as principal consecrator.<sup id="cite_ref-aica_59-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-aica-59">&#91;56&#93;</a></sup> He chose as his episcopal motto <i>Miserando atque eligendo</i>.<sup id="cite_ref-60" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-60">&#91;57&#93;</a></sup> It is drawn from <a href="/wiki/Saint_Bede" class="mw-redirect" title="Saint Bede">Saint Bede</a>'s homily on Matthew 9:9–13: "because he saw him through the eyes of mercy and chose him".<sup id="cite_ref-Catholic_News_Service_61-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Catholic_News_Service-61">&#91;58&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>On 3 June 1997, Bergoglio was appointed <a href="/wiki/Coadjutor_archbishop" class="mw-redirect" title="Coadjutor archbishop">coadjutor archbishop</a> of Buenos Aires with right of succession. Upon Quarracino's death on 28 February 1998, Bergoglio became metropolitan archbishop of Buenos Aires. In that role, Bergoglio created new parishes and restructured the archdiocese administrative offices, led pro-life initiatives, and created a commission on divorces.<sup id="cite_ref-directory_7-7" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-directory-7">&#91;5&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-62" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-62">&#91;59&#93;</a></sup> One of Bergoglio's major initiatives as archbishop was to increase the church's presence in the slums of Buenos Aires. Under his leadership, the number of priests assigned to work in the slums doubled.<sup id="cite_ref-63" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-63">&#91;60&#93;</a></sup> This work led to him being called the "Slum Bishop".<sup id="cite_ref-64" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-64">&#91;61&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Early in his time as archbishop of Buenos Aires, Bergoglio sold off the archdiocese's shares in multiple banks and turned its accounts into those of a normal customer in international banks. The shares in banks had led the local church to a propensity towards high spending, and the archdiocese was nearing bankruptcy as a result. As a normal customer of the bank, the church was forced into a higher fiscal discipline.<sup id="cite_ref-65" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-65">&#91;62&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>On 6 November 1998, while remaining archbishop of Buenos Aires, he was named <a href="/wiki/Ordinary_(Catholic_Church)" class="mw-redirect" title="Ordinary (Catholic Church)">ordinary</a> for those <a href="/wiki/Eastern_Rite_Catholic_Churches" class="mw-redirect" title="Eastern Rite Catholic Churches">Eastern Catholics</a> in Argentina who lacked a <a href="/wiki/Prelate" title="Prelate">prelate</a> of their own church.<sup id="cite_ref-aica_59-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-aica-59">&#91;56&#93;</a></sup> Major Archbishop <a href="/wiki/Sviatoslav_Shevchuk" title="Sviatoslav Shevchuk">Sviatoslav Shevchuk</a> said that Bergoglio understands the liturgy, rites, and spirituality of Shevchuk's <a href="/wiki/Ukrainian_Greek_Catholic_Church" title="Ukrainian Greek Catholic Church">Ukrainian Greek Catholic Church</a> and always "took care of our Church in Argentina" as ordinary for Eastern Catholics during his time as archbishop of Buenos Aires.<sup id="cite_ref-greek_53-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-greek-53">&#91;50&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In 2000, Bergoglio was the only church official to reconcile with <a href="/wiki/Jer%C3%B3nimo_Podest%C3%A1" title="Jerónimo Podestá">Jerónimo Podestá</a>, a former bishop who had been suspended as a priest after opposing the <a href="/wiki/Argentine_Revolution" title="Argentine Revolution">Argentine Revolution</a> military dictatorship in 1972. He defended Podestá's wife from Vatican attacks on their marriage.<sup id="cite_ref-66" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-66">&#91;63&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-67" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-67">&#91;64&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-68" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-68">&#91;65&#93;</a></sup> That same year, Bergoglio said the Argentine Catholic Church needed "to put on garments of public penance for the sins committed during the years of the dictatorship" in the 1970s, during the <a href="/wiki/Dirty_War" title="Dirty War">Dirty War</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-69" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-69">&#91;66&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Bergoglio made it his custom to celebrate the <a href="/wiki/Holy_Thursday" class="mw-redirect" title="Holy Thursday">Holy Thursday</a> ritual <a href="/wiki/Maundy_(foot_washing)#Catholic_practice" title="Maundy (foot washing)">washing of feet</a> in places such as jails, hospitals, retirement homes or slums.<sup id="cite_ref-70" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-70">&#91;67&#93;</a></sup> In 2007, just two days after Benedict XVI issued new rules for using the liturgical forms that preceded the Second Vatican Council, Cardinal Bergoglio established a fixed place for a weekly Mass in this <a href="/wiki/Tridentine_Mass" title="Tridentine Mass">extraordinary form</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Roman_Rite" title="Roman Rite">Roman Rite</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-71" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-71">&#91;68&#93;</a></sup> It was celebrated weekly.<sup id="cite_ref-72" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-72">&#91;69&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>On 8 November 2005, Bergoglio was elected president of the <a href="/wiki/Argentine_Episcopal_Conference" class="mw-redirect" title="Argentine Episcopal Conference">Argentine Episcopal Conference</a> for a three-year term (2005–08).<sup id="cite_ref-73" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-73">&#91;70&#93;</a></sup> He was reelected to another three-year term on 11 November 2008.<sup id="cite_ref-74" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-74">&#91;71&#93;</a></sup> He remained a member of that commission's permanent governing body, president of its committee for the <a href="/wiki/Pontifical_Catholic_University_of_Argentina" title="Pontifical Catholic University of Argentina">Pontifical Catholic University of Argentina</a>, and a member of its liturgy committee for the care of shrines.<sup id="cite_ref-aica_59-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-aica-59">&#91;56&#93;</a></sup> While head of the Argentine Catholic bishops' conference, Bergoglio issued a collective apology for his church's failure to protect people from the Junta during the Dirty War.<sup id="cite_ref-75" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-75">&#91;72&#93;</a></sup> When he turned 75 in December 2011, Bergoglio submitted his resignation as archbishop of Buenos Aires to Pope Benedict XVI as required by <a href="/wiki/Canon_law_(Catholic_Church)" class="mw-redirect" title="Canon law (Catholic Church)">canon law</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-travel_42-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-travel-42">&#91;40&#93;</a></sup> Still, as he had no coadjutor archbishop, he stayed in office, waiting for an eventual replacement appointed by the Vatican.<sup id="cite_ref-76" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-76">&#91;73&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span id="Cardinalate_.282001.E2.80.932013.29"></span><span class="mw-headline" id="Cardinalate_(2001–2013)">Cardinalate (2001–2013)</span></h3>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:152px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Cat%C3%A9ch%C3%A8se_18_juin_2008_par_le_cardinal_Bergoglio_-2.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/08/Cat%C3%A9ch%C3%A8se_18_juin_2008_par_le_cardinal_Bergoglio_-2.jpg/150px-Cat%C3%A9ch%C3%A8se_18_juin_2008_par_le_cardinal_Bergoglio_-2.jpg" decoding="async" width="150" height="225" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/08/Cat%C3%A9ch%C3%A8se_18_juin_2008_par_le_cardinal_Bergoglio_-2.jpg/225px-Cat%C3%A9ch%C3%A8se_18_juin_2008_par_le_cardinal_Bergoglio_-2.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/08/Cat%C3%A9ch%C3%A8se_18_juin_2008_par_le_cardinal_Bergoglio_-2.jpg/300px-Cat%C3%A9ch%C3%A8se_18_juin_2008_par_le_cardinal_Bergoglio_-2.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1216" data-file-height="1824" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Cat%C3%A9ch%C3%A8se_18_juin_2008_par_le_cardinal_Bergoglio_-2.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>Bergoglio on 18 June 2008 giving a <a href="/wiki/Catechesis" title="Catechesis">catechesis</a></div></div></div>
<p>At the <a href="/wiki/Papal_consistory" title="Papal consistory">consistory</a> of 21 February 2001, Archbishop Bergoglio was created a <a href="/wiki/Cardinal_(Catholic_Church)" title="Cardinal (Catholic Church)">cardinal</a> by <a href="/wiki/Pope_John_Paul_II" title="Pope John Paul II">Pope John Paul II</a> with the <a href="/wiki/Titular_church" title="Titular church">title</a> of <a href="/wiki/Cardinal_priest" class="mw-redirect" title="Cardinal priest">cardinal priest</a> of <a href="/wiki/San_Roberto_Bellarmino_(church)" class="mw-redirect" title="San Roberto Bellarmino (church)">San Roberto Bellarmino</a>, a church served by Jesuits and named for one; he was formally installed in that church the following 14 October. When he traveled to Rome for the ceremony, he and his sister María Elena visited the village in northern Italy where their father was born.<sup id="cite_ref-fascism_16-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-fascism-16">&#91;14&#93;</a></sup> As cardinal, Bergoglio was appointed to five administrative positions in the <a href="/wiki/Roman_Curia" title="Roman Curia">Roman Curia</a>. He was a member of the <a href="/wiki/Congregation_for_Divine_Worship_and_the_Discipline_of_the_Sacraments" class="mw-redirect" title="Congregation for Divine Worship and the Discipline of the Sacraments">Congregation for Divine Worship and the Discipline of the Sacraments</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Congregation_for_the_Clergy" class="mw-redirect" title="Congregation for the Clergy">Congregation for the Clergy</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Congregation_for_Institutes_of_Consecrated_Life_and_Societies_of_Apostolic_Life" class="mw-redirect" title="Congregation for Institutes of Consecrated Life and Societies of Apostolic Life">Congregation for Institutes of Consecrated Life and Societies of Apostolic Life</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Pontifical_Council_for_the_Family" title="Pontifical Council for the Family">Pontifical Council for the Family</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Pontifical_Commission_for_Latin_America" title="Pontifical Commission for Latin America">Commission for Latin America</a>. Later that year, when Cardinal <a href="/wiki/Edward_Egan" title="Edward Egan">Edward Egan</a> returned to New York following the <a href="/wiki/September_11_attacks" title="September 11 attacks">September 11 attacks</a>, Bergoglio replaced him as relator (recording secretary) in the <a href="/wiki/Synod_of_Bishops_(Catholic)" class="mw-redirect" title="Synod of Bishops (Catholic)">Synod of Bishops</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-77" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-77">&#91;74&#93;</a></sup> and, according to the <i><a href="/wiki/Catholic_Herald" title="Catholic Herald">Catholic Herald</a></i>, created "a favourable impression as a man open to communion and dialogue".<sup id="cite_ref-thunder_78-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-thunder-78">&#91;75&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-79" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-79">&#91;76&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<div class="thumb tleft"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:172px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Card._Jorge_Bergoglio_SJ,_2008.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4d/Card._Jorge_Bergoglio_SJ%2C_2008.jpg/170px-Card._Jorge_Bergoglio_SJ%2C_2008.jpg" decoding="async" width="170" height="202" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4d/Card._Jorge_Bergoglio_SJ%2C_2008.jpg/255px-Card._Jorge_Bergoglio_SJ%2C_2008.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4d/Card._Jorge_Bergoglio_SJ%2C_2008.jpg/340px-Card._Jorge_Bergoglio_SJ%2C_2008.jpg 2x" data-file-width="991" data-file-height="1177" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Card._Jorge_Bergoglio_SJ,_2008.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>Cardinal Jorge Bergoglio in 2008</div></div></div>
<p>Cardinal Bergoglio became known for personal humility, doctrinal conservatism, and a commitment to <a href="/wiki/Social_justice" title="Social justice">social justice</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Allen_80-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Allen-80">&#91;77&#93;</a></sup> A <a href="/wiki/Simple_living" title="Simple living">simple lifestyle</a> contributed to his reputation for humility. He lived in a small apartment, rather than in the elegant bishop's residence in the suburb of <a href="/wiki/Olivos,_Buenos_Aires" title="Olivos, Buenos Aires">Olivos</a>. He took public transportation and cooked his own meals.<sup id="cite_ref-81" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-81">&#91;78&#93;</a></sup> He limited his time in Rome to "lightning visits".<sup id="cite_ref-falasca_82-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-falasca-82">&#91;79&#93;</a></sup> He was known to be devoted to <a href="/wiki/Th%C3%A9r%C3%A8se_of_Lisieux" title="Thérèse of Lisieux">St. Thérèse of Lisieux</a>, and he enclosed a small picture of her in the letters he wrote, calling her "a great missionary saint".<sup id="cite_ref-83" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-83">&#91;80&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>After Pope John Paul II died on 2 April 2005, Bergoglio attended <a href="/wiki/Funeral_of_Pope_John_Paul_II" class="mw-redirect" title="Funeral of Pope John Paul II">his funeral</a> and was considered one of the <i><a href="/wiki/Papabile" title="Papabile">papabile</a></i> for succession to the papacy.<sup id="cite_ref-84" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-84">&#91;81&#93;</a></sup> He participated as a <a href="/wiki/Cardinal_electors_for_the_2005_papal_conclave" class="mw-redirect" title="Cardinal electors for the 2005 papal conclave">cardinal elector</a> in the <a href="/wiki/2005_papal_conclave" title="2005 papal conclave">2005 papal conclave</a> that elected Pope Benedict XVI. In the <i><a href="/wiki/National_Catholic_Reporter" title="National Catholic Reporter">National Catholic Reporter</a></i>, <a href="/wiki/John_L._Allen_Jr." title="John L. Allen Jr.">John L. Allen Jr.</a> reported that Bergoglio was a frontrunner in the 2005 conclave.<sup id="cite_ref-Allen_80-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Allen-80">&#91;77&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-85" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-85">&#91;82&#93;</a></sup> In September 2005, the Italian magazine <i><a href="/wiki/Limes_(magazine)" title="Limes (magazine)">Limes</a></i> published claims that Bergoglio had been the runner-up and main challenger to Cardinal Ratzinger at that conclave and that he had received 40 votes in the third ballot, but fell back to 26 at the fourth and decisive ballot.<sup id="cite_ref-CNN05_86-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-CNN05-86">&#91;83&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-votes2005_87-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-votes2005-87">&#91;84&#93;</a></sup> The claims were based on a diary purportedly belonging to an anonymous cardinal who had been present at the conclave.<sup id="cite_ref-CNN05_86-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-CNN05-86">&#91;83&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Rubin13_88-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Rubin13-88">&#91;85&#93;</a></sup> According to the Italian journalist <a href="/wiki/Andrea_Tornielli" title="Andrea Tornielli">Andrea Tornielli</a>, this number of votes had no precedent for a Latin American <i>papabile</i>.<sup id="cite_ref-Rubin13_88-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Rubin13-88">&#91;85&#93;</a></sup> <i><a href="/wiki/La_Stampa" title="La Stampa">La Stampa</a></i> reported that Bergoglio was in close contention with Ratzinger during the election, until he made an emotional plea that the cardinals should not vote for him.<sup id="cite_ref-tears_89-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-tears-89">&#91;86&#93;</a></sup> According to Tornielli, Bergoglio made this request to prevent the conclave from delaying too much in the election of a pope.<sup id="cite_ref-90" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-90">&#91;87&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>As a cardinal, Bergoglio was associated with <a href="/wiki/Communion_and_Liberation" title="Communion and Liberation">Communion and Liberation</a>, a Catholic evangelical lay movement of the type known as <a href="/wiki/Associations_of_the_faithful" class="mw-redirect" title="Associations of the faithful">associations of the faithful</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Allen_80-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Allen-80">&#91;77&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-91" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-91">&#91;88&#93;</a></sup> He sometimes made appearances at the annual gathering known as the <a href="/wiki/Meeting_for_friendship_among_peoples" class="mw-redirect" title="Meeting for friendship among peoples">Rimini Meeting</a> held during the late summer months in Italy.<sup id="cite_ref-Allen_80-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Allen-80">&#91;77&#93;</a></sup> In 2005, Cardinal Bergoglio authorized the request for <a href="/wiki/Beatification" title="Beatification">beatification</a>—the third step towards <a href="/wiki/Saint" title="Saint">sainthood</a>—for six members of the <a href="/wiki/Pallottines" title="Pallottines">Pallottine</a> community murdered in the <a href="/wiki/San_Patricio_Church_massacre" title="San Patricio Church massacre">San Patricio Church massacre</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-92" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-92">&#91;89&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-CT2005_93-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-CT2005-93">&#91;90&#93;</a></sup> At the same time, Bergoglio ordered an investigation into the murders themselves, which had been widely blamed on the <a href="/wiki/National_Reorganization_Process" title="National Reorganization Process">National Reorganization Process</a>, the military junta that ruled Argentina at the time.<sup id="cite_ref-CT2005_93-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-CT2005-93">&#91;90&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Relations_with_Argentine_governments">Relations with Argentine governments</span></h2>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Dirty_War">Dirty War</span></h3>
<style data-mw-deduplicate="TemplateStyles:r1033289096">.mw-parser-output .hatnote{font-style:italic}.mw-parser-output div.hatnote{padding-left:1.6em;margin-bottom:0.5em}.mw-parser-output .hatnote i{font-style:normal}.mw-parser-output .hatnote+link+.hatnote{margin-top:-0.5em}</style><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Dirty_War" title="Dirty War">Dirty War</a></div>
<p>Bergoglio was the subject of allegations regarding the <a href="/wiki/Argentine_Navy" title="Argentine Navy">Argentine Navy</a>'s kidnapping of two <a href="/wiki/Society_of_Jesus" class="mw-redirect" title="Society of Jesus">Jesuit</a> priests, Orlando Yorio and <a href="/wiki/Franz_Jalics" title="Franz Jalics">Franz Jalics</a>, in May 1976, during Argentina's <a href="/wiki/Dirty_War" title="Dirty War">Dirty War</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-nytimes1_94-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-nytimes1-94">&#91;91&#93;</a></sup> He feared for the priests' safety and had tried to change their work prior to their arrest; however, contrary to reports, he never tried to throw them out of the Jesuit order.<sup id="cite_ref-95" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-95">&#91;92&#93;</a></sup> In 2005, <a href="/wiki/Myriam_Bregman" title="Myriam Bregman">Myriam Bregman</a>, a human rights lawyer, filed a criminal complaint against Bergoglio, as superior in the Society of Jesus of Argentina, accusing him of involvement in the kidnapping.<sup id="cite_ref-latimes1_96-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-latimes1-96">&#91;93&#93;</a></sup> Her complaint did not specify how Bergoglio was involved; Bergoglio's spokesman flatly denied the allegations. The complaint was ultimately dismissed.<sup id="cite_ref-nytimes1_94-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-nytimes1-94">&#91;91&#93;</a></sup> The priests were tortured,<sup id="cite_ref-rubin_97-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-rubin-97">&#91;94&#93;</a></sup> but were found alive five months later, drugged and semi-naked. Yorio accused Bergoglio of effectively handing them over to the death squads by declining to tell the authorities that he endorsed their work. Yorio, who died in 2000, said in a 1999 interview that he believed that Bergoglio did nothing "to free us, in fact just the opposite".<sup id="cite_ref-WAPO_98-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-WAPO-98">&#91;95&#93;</a></sup> Jalics initially refused to discuss the complaint after moving into seclusion in a German monastery.<sup id="cite_ref-99" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-99">&#91;96&#93;</a></sup> However, two days after the election of Francis, Jalics issued a statement confirming the kidnapping and attributing the cause to a former lay colleague who became a guerrilla, was captured, then named Yorio and Jalics when interrogated.<sup id="cite_ref-100" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-100">&#91;97&#93;</a></sup> The following week, Jalics issued a second, clarifying statement: "It is wrong to assert that our capture took place at the initiative of Father Bergoglio (…) the fact is, Orlando Yorio and I were not denounced by Father Bergoglio."<sup id="cite_ref-101" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-101">&#91;98&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-102" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-102">&#91;99&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Bergoglio told his authorized biographer, <a href="/wiki/Sergio_Rubin" title="Sergio Rubin">Sergio Rubin</a>, that after the priests' imprisonment, he worked behind the scenes for their release; Bergoglio's intercession with dictator <a href="/wiki/Jorge_Rafael_Videla" title="Jorge Rafael Videla">Jorge Rafael Videla</a> on their behalf may have saved their lives.<sup id="cite_ref-103" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-103">&#91;100&#93;</a></sup> Bergoglio also told Rubin that he had often sheltered people from the dictatorship on church property, and once gave his own identity papers to a man who looked like him, so he could flee Argentina.<sup id="cite_ref-rubin_97-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-rubin-97">&#91;94&#93;</a></sup> The interview with Rubin, reflected in the biography <i><a href="/wiki/El_jesuita" class="mw-redirect" title="El jesuita">El jesuita</a></i>, is the only time Bergoglio has spoken to the press about those events.<sup id="cite_ref-104" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-104">&#91;101&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Alicia_Oliveira" title="Alicia Oliveira">Alicia Oliveira</a>, a former Argentine judge, has also reported that Bergoglio helped people flee Argentina during the rule of the junta.<sup id="cite_ref-105" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-105">&#91;102&#93;</a></sup> Since Francis became pope, Gonzalo Mosca<sup id="cite_ref-106" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-106">&#91;103&#93;</a></sup> and José Caravias<sup id="cite_ref-107" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-107">&#91;104&#93;</a></sup> have related to journalists accounts of how Bergoglio helped them flee the Argentine dictatorship.
</p><p>Oliveira described the future pope as "anguished" and "very critical of the dictatorship" during the Dirty War.<sup id="cite_ref-108" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-108">&#91;105&#93;</a></sup> Oliveira met with him at the time and urged Bergoglio to speak out—he told her that "he couldn't. That it wasn't an easy thing to do."<sup id="cite_ref-WAPO_98-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-WAPO-98">&#91;95&#93;</a></sup> Artist and human rights activist <a href="/wiki/Adolfo_P%C3%A9rez_Esquivel" title="Adolfo Pérez Esquivel">Adolfo Pérez Esquivel</a>, the 1980 <a href="/wiki/Nobel_Peace_Prize" title="Nobel Peace Prize">Nobel Peace Prize</a> laureate, said: "Perhaps he didn't have the courage of other priests, but he never collaborated with the dictatorship. …Bergoglio was no accomplice of the dictatorship."<sup id="cite_ref-109" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-109">&#91;106&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-110" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-110">&#91;107&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Graciela_Fern%C3%A1ndez_Meijide" title="Graciela Fernández Meijide">Graciela Fernández Meijide</a>, member of the <a href="/wiki/Permanent_Assembly_for_Human_Rights" title="Permanent Assembly for Human Rights">Permanent Assembly for Human Rights</a>, also said that there was no proof linking Bergoglio with the dictatorship. She told the <i><a href="/wiki/Clar%C3%ADn_(Argentine_newspaper)" title="Clarín (Argentine newspaper)">Clarín</a></i> newspaper: "There is no information and Justice couldn't prove it. I was in the <a href="/wiki/Permanent_Assembly_for_Human_Rights" title="Permanent Assembly for Human Rights">APDH</a> during all the dictatorship years and I received hundreds of testimonies. Bergoglio was never mentioned. It was the same in the <a href="/wiki/National_Commission_on_the_Disappearance_of_Persons" title="National Commission on the Disappearance of Persons">CONADEP</a>. Nobody mentioned him as instigator or as anything."<sup id="cite_ref-111" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-111">&#91;108&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Ricardo_Lorenzetti" title="Ricardo Lorenzetti">Ricardo Lorenzetti</a>, President of the Argentine Supreme Court, also has said that Bergoglio is "completely innocent" of the accusations.<sup id="cite_ref-112" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-112">&#91;109&#93;</a></sup> Historian <a href="/wiki/Uki_Go%C3%B1i" title="Uki Goñi">Uki Goñi</a> pointed that, during early 1976, the military junta still had a good image among society, and that the <a href="/wiki/Detention_Centers_in_the_Dirty_War" class="mw-redirect" title="Detention Centers in the Dirty War">scale of the political repression</a> was not known until much later; Bergoglio would have had little reason to suspect that the detention of Yorio and Jalics could end up in their deaths.<sup id="cite_ref-113" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-113">&#91;110&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>When Bergoglio became pope, an alleged photo of him giving the <a href="/wiki/Sacramental_bread" title="Sacramental bread">sacramental bread</a> to dictator Jorge Rafael Videla became popular in social networks. It has also been used by the newspaper <i><a href="/wiki/P%C3%A1gina/12" class="mw-redirect" title="Página/12">Página/12</a></i>.<sup id="cite_ref-114" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-114">&#91;111&#93;</a></sup> The photo was soon proved to be false. It was revealed that the priest, whose face is not visible in the photo, was Carlos Berón de Astrada. The photo was taken at the church "Pequeña Obra de la Divina Providencia Don Orione" in 1990, not during the Dirty War, and after Videla's presidential pardon. The photo was produced by the agency AFP and it was initially published by the <i><a href="/wiki/Cr%C3%B3nica_(newspaper)" title="Crónica (newspaper)">Crónica</a></i> newspaper.<sup id="cite_ref-115" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-115">&#91;112&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span id="Fernando_de_la_R.C3.BAa"></span><span class="mw-headline" id="Fernando_de_la_Rúa">Fernando de la Rúa</span></h3>
<p><a href="/wiki/Fernando_de_la_R%C3%BAa" title="Fernando de la Rúa">Fernando de la Rúa</a> replaced <a href="/wiki/Carlos_Menem" title="Carlos Menem">Carlos Menem</a> as president of Argentina in 1999. As an archbishop, Bergoglio celebrated the annual Mass at the <a href="/wiki/Buenos_Aires_Metropolitan_Cathedral" title="Buenos Aires Metropolitan Cathedral">Buenos Aires Metropolitan Cathedral</a> on the <i><a href="/wiki/First_National_Government" title="First National Government">First National Government</a></i> holiday, 25 May. In 2000, Bergoglio criticized the perceived apathy of society.<sup id="cite_ref-116" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-116">&#91;113&#93;</a></sup> Argentina faced an <a href="/wiki/1998%E2%80%932002_Argentine_great_depression" title="1998–2002 Argentine great depression">economic depression</a> at the time, and the Catholic Church criticized the fiscal austerity of the government, which increased poverty. De la Rúa asked the church to promote a dialogue between the leaders of economic and political sectors to find a solution for the crisis. He claims that he talked with Bergoglio and proposed to take part in the meeting, but Bergoglio would have told him that the meeting was canceled because of a misunderstanding by De la Rúa's assistant, who may have declined the president's assistance. Bishop Jorge Casaretto considers it unlikely, as De la Rúa only made the request in newspaper interviews, but never made a formal request to the church.<sup id="cite_ref-117" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-117">&#91;114&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Justicialist_Party" title="Justicialist Party">Justicialist Party</a> won the <a href="/wiki/Argentine_legislative_election,_2001" class="mw-redirect" title="Argentine legislative election, 2001">2001 elections</a> and got the majority in the Congress, and appointed <a href="/wiki/Ram%C3%B3n_Puerta" title="Ramón Puerta">Ramón Puerta</a> as president of the Senate. As vice president <a href="/wiki/Carlos_%C3%81lvarez_(Argentine_politician)" title="Carlos Álvarez (Argentine politician)">Carlos Álvarez</a> resigned shortly before, this left an opposing party second in the <a href="/wiki/Argentine_order_of_precedence" title="Argentine order of precedence">order of precedence</a>. Bergoglio asked for an interview with Puerta, and had a positive impression of him. Puerta told him that the Justicialist party was not plotting to oust De la Rúa, and promised to help the president promote the laws that may be required.<sup id="cite_ref-118" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-118">&#91;115&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>During police repression of the <a href="/wiki/December_2001_riots_in_Argentina" title="December 2001 riots in Argentina">riots of December 2001</a>, he contacted the Ministry of the Interior and asked that the police distinguish rioters and vandals from peaceful protesters.<sup id="cite_ref-119" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-119">&#91;116&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span id="N.C3.A9stor_and_Cristina_Kirchner"></span><span class="mw-headline" id="Néstor_and_Cristina_Kirchner">Néstor and Cristina Kirchner</span></h3>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Pope_Francis_with_Cristina_Fernandez_de_Kirchner_4.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a1/Pope_Francis_with_Cristina_Fernandez_de_Kirchner_4.jpg/220px-Pope_Francis_with_Cristina_Fernandez_de_Kirchner_4.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="148" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a1/Pope_Francis_with_Cristina_Fernandez_de_Kirchner_4.jpg/330px-Pope_Francis_with_Cristina_Fernandez_de_Kirchner_4.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a1/Pope_Francis_with_Cristina_Fernandez_de_Kirchner_4.jpg/440px-Pope_Francis_with_Cristina_Fernandez_de_Kirchner_4.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2000" data-file-height="1342" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Pope_Francis_with_Cristina_Fernandez_de_Kirchner_4.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>Francis with Argentine president <a href="/wiki/Cristina_Fern%C3%A1ndez_de_Kirchner" title="Cristina Fernández de Kirchner">Cristina Fernández de Kirchner</a>, holding traditional Argentine <a href="/wiki/Mate_(beverage)" class="mw-redirect" title="Mate (beverage)">mate</a> drinkware</div></div></div>
<p>When Bergoglio celebrated Mass at the cathedral for the 2004 <i>First National Government</i> holiday, President <a href="/wiki/N%C3%A9stor_Kirchner" title="Néstor Kirchner">Néstor Kirchner</a> attended and heard Bergoglio request more political dialogue, reject intolerance, and criticize exhibitionism and strident announcements.<sup id="cite_ref-120" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-120">&#91;117&#93;</a></sup> Kirchner celebrated the national day elsewhere the following year and the Mass in the cathedral was suspended.<sup id="cite_ref-121" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-121">&#91;118&#93;</a></sup> In 2006, Bergoglio helped the fellow Jesuit <a href="/wiki/Joaqu%C3%ADn_Pi%C3%B1a" class="mw-redirect" title="Joaquín Piña">Joaquín Piña</a> to win the elections in the <a href="/wiki/Misiones_Province" title="Misiones Province">Misiones Province</a> and prevent an amendment of the local constitution that would allow indefinite re-elections. Kirchner intended to use that project to start similar amendments at other provinces, and eventually to the national constitution.<sup id="cite_ref-122" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-122">&#91;119&#93;</a></sup> Kirchner considered Bergoglio as a political rival to the day he died in October 2010.<sup id="cite_ref-anios_123-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-anios-123">&#91;120&#93;</a></sup> Bergoglio's relations with Kirchner's widow and successor, <a href="/wiki/Cristina_Fern%C3%A1ndez_de_Kirchner" title="Cristina Fernández de Kirchner">Cristina Fernández de Kirchner</a>, have been similarly tense. In 2008, Bergoglio called for national reconciliation during <a href="/wiki/2008_Argentine_government_conflict_with_the_agricultural_sector" class="mw-redirect" title="2008 Argentine government conflict with the agricultural sector">disturbances</a> in the country's agricultural regions, which the government interpreted as a support for anti-government demonstrators.<sup id="cite_ref-anios_123-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-anios-123">&#91;120&#93;</a></sup> The campaign to enact <a href="/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Argentina" title="Same-sex marriage in Argentina">same-sex marriage legislation</a> was a particularly tense period in their relations.<sup id="cite_ref-anios_123-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-anios-123">&#91;120&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>When Bergoglio was elected pope, the initial reactions were mixed. Most of the Argentine society cheered it, but the pro-government newspaper <i><a href="/wiki/P%C3%A1gina/12" class="mw-redirect" title="Página/12">Página/12</a></i> published renewed allegations about the Dirty War, and the president of the <a href="/wiki/National_Library_of_the_Argentine_Republic" class="mw-redirect" title="National Library of the Argentine Republic">National Library</a> described a global conspiracy theory. The president took more than an hour before congratulating the new pope, and only did so in a passing reference within a routine speech. However, due to the pope's popularity in Argentina, Cristina Kirchner made what the political analyst Claudio Fantini called a "<a href="/wiki/Copernican_Revolution_(metaphor)" class="mw-redirect" title="Copernican Revolution (metaphor)">Copernican shift</a>" in her relations with him and fully embraced the Francis phenomenon.<sup id="cite_ref-124" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-124">&#91;121&#93;</a></sup> On the day before his inauguration as pope, Bergoglio, now Francis, had a private meeting with Kirchner. They exchanged gifts and lunched together. This was the new pope's first meeting with a head of state, and there was speculation that the two were mending their relations.<sup id="cite_ref-125" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-125">&#91;122&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-126" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-126">&#91;123&#93;</a></sup> <i>Página/12</i> <a href="/wiki/Self-censorship" title="Self-censorship">removed</a> their controversial articles about Bergoglio, written by <a href="/wiki/Horacio_Verbitsky" title="Horacio Verbitsky">Horacio Verbitsky</a>, from their web page, as a result of this change.<sup id="cite_ref-127" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-127">&#91;124&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span id="Papacy_.282013.E2.80.93present.29"></span><span class="mw-headline" id="Papacy_(2013–present)">Papacy (2013–present)</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Theology_of_Pope_Francis#Vatican_II_revisited" title="Theology of Pope Francis">Theology of Pope Francis §&#160;Vatican II revisited</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Theology_of_Pope_Francis#Church_leadership" title="Theology of Pope Francis">Theology of Pope Francis §&#160;Church leadership</a></div>
<style data-mw-deduplicate="TemplateStyles:r1096954695/mw-parser-output/.tmulti">.mw-parser-output .tmulti .multiimageinner{display:flex;flex-direction:column}.mw-parser-output .tmulti .trow{display:flex;flex-direction:row;clear:left;flex-wrap:wrap;width:100%;box-sizing:border-box}.mw-parser-output .tmulti .tsingle{margin:1px;float:left}.mw-parser-output .tmulti .theader{clear:both;font-weight:bold;text-align:center;align-self:center;background-color:transparent;width:100%}.mw-parser-output .tmulti .thumbcaption{background-color:transparent}.mw-parser-output .tmulti .text-align-left{text-align:left}.mw-parser-output .tmulti .text-align-right{text-align:right}.mw-parser-output .tmulti .text-align-center{text-align:center}@media all and (max-width:720px){.mw-parser-output .tmulti .thumbinner{width:100%!important;box-sizing:border-box;max-width:none!important;align-items:center}.mw-parser-output .tmulti .trow{justify-content:center}.mw-parser-output .tmulti .tsingle{float:none!important;max-width:100%!important;box-sizing:border-box;text-align:center}.mw-parser-output .tmulti .tsingle .thumbcaption{text-align:left}.mw-parser-output .tmulti .trow>.thumbcaption{text-align:center}}</style><div class="thumb tmulti tright"><div class="thumbinner multiimageinner" style="width:271px;max-width:271px"><div class="trow"><div class="theader" style="text-align:center"><a href="/wiki/Coat_of_arms_of_Pope_Francis" title="Coat of arms of Pope Francis">Coat of arms of Pope Francis</a></div></div><div class="trow"><div class="tsingle" style="width:152px;max-width:152px"><div class="thumbimage"><a href="/wiki/File:Coat_of_arms_of_Jorge_Mario_Bergoglio.svg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/65/Coat_of_arms_of_Jorge_Mario_Bergoglio.svg/150px-Coat_of_arms_of_Jorge_Mario_Bergoglio.svg.png" decoding="async" width="150" height="159" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/65/Coat_of_arms_of_Jorge_Mario_Bergoglio.svg/225px-Coat_of_arms_of_Jorge_Mario_Bergoglio.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/65/Coat_of_arms_of_Jorge_Mario_Bergoglio.svg/300px-Coat_of_arms_of_Jorge_Mario_Bergoglio.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="1148" data-file-height="1218" /></a></div><div class="thumbcaption text-align-center">As cardinal</div></div><div class="tsingle" style="width:115px;max-width:115px"><div class="thumbimage"><a href="/wiki/File:Coat_of_arms_of_Franciscus.svg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d7/Coat_of_arms_of_Franciscus.svg/113px-Coat_of_arms_of_Franciscus.svg.png" decoding="async" width="113" height="156" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d7/Coat_of_arms_of_Franciscus.svg/170px-Coat_of_arms_of_Franciscus.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d7/Coat_of_arms_of_Franciscus.svg/226px-Coat_of_arms_of_Franciscus.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="862" data-file-height="1190" /></a></div><div class="thumbcaption text-align-center">As pope</div></div></div><div class="trow" style="display:flex"><div class="thumbcaption">The gold star represents the <a href="/wiki/Virgin_Mary" class="mw-redirect" title="Virgin Mary">Virgin Mary</a>, the grape-like plant—the <a href="/wiki/Spikenard" title="Spikenard">spikenard</a>—is associated with <a href="/wiki/Saint_Joseph" title="Saint Joseph">Saint Joseph</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Holy_Name_of_Jesus" title="Holy Name of Jesus">IHS</a> is the symbol of the Jesuits.<sup id="cite_ref-128" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-128">&#91;125&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-129" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-129">&#91;126&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-NCR_130-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-NCR-130">&#91;127&#93;</a></sup></div></div></div></div>
<p>Elected at 76 years old, Francis was reported to be healthy and his doctors have said his missing lung tissue, removed in his youth, does not significantly affect his health.<sup id="cite_ref-Pope_Francis&#39;s_missing_lung_should_not_be_a_problem,_say_doctors_131-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Pope_Francis&#39;s_missing_lung_should_not_be_a_problem,_say_doctors-131">&#91;128&#93;</a></sup> The only concern would be decreased respiratory reserve if he had a respiratory infection.<sup id="cite_ref-Why_Pope_Francis_Only_Has_One_Lung_132-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Why_Pope_Francis_Only_Has_One_Lung-132">&#91;129&#93;</a></sup> In the past, one attack of <a href="/wiki/Sciatica" title="Sciatica">sciatica</a> in 2007 prevented him from attending a consistory and delayed his return to Argentina for several days.<sup id="cite_ref-falasca_82-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-falasca-82">&#91;79&#93;</a></sup> Francis is the first <a href="/wiki/Jesuit" class="mw-redirect" title="Jesuit">Jesuit</a> pope. This was a significant appointment, because of the sometimes tense relations between the <a href="/wiki/Society_of_Jesus" class="mw-redirect" title="Society of Jesus">Society of Jesus</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Holy_See" title="Holy See">Holy See</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-133" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-133">&#91;130&#93;</a></sup> However, Bergoglio came in second to Cardinal Ratzinger on all the ballots in the 2005 conclave, and at the time appeared as the only other viable candidate.<sup id="cite_ref-134" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-134">&#91;131&#93;</a></sup>
He is also the first from the Americas,<sup id="cite_ref-135" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-135">&#91;132&#93;</a></sup> and the first from the <a href="/wiki/Southern_Hemisphere" title="Southern Hemisphere">Southern Hemisphere</a>. Many media reported him as being the first non-European pope, but he is actually the 11th; the previous was <a href="/wiki/Pope_Gregory_III" title="Pope Gregory III">Gregory III</a> from Syria, who died in 741. Moreover, although Francis was not born in Europe, he is <a href="/wiki/Ethnic_groups_in_Europe" title="Ethnic groups in Europe">ethnically European</a>; his father and both of his mother's parents are from northern Italy.<sup id="cite_ref-136" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-136">&#91;133&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>As pope, his manner is less formal than that of his immediate predecessors: a style that news coverage has referred to as "no frills", noting that it is "his common touch and accessibility that is proving the greatest inspiration."<sup id="cite_ref-nofrills_137-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-nofrills-137">&#91;134&#93;</a></sup> On the night of his election, he took a bus back to his hotel with the cardinals, rather than be driven in the papal car.<sup id="cite_ref-138" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-138">&#91;135&#93;</a></sup> The next day, he visited Cardinal <a href="/wiki/Jorge_Mar%C3%ADa_Mej%C3%ADa" title="Jorge María Mejía">Jorge María Mejía</a> in the hospital and chatted with patients and staff.<sup id="cite_ref-139" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-139">&#91;136&#93;</a></sup> At his first media audience, the Saturday after his election, the pope explained his papal name choice, citing Saint Francis of Assisi as "the man who gives us this spirit of peace, the poor man", and he added "[h]ow I would like a poor Church, and for the poor".<sup id="cite_ref-PapalName_140-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-PapalName-140">&#91;137&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In addition to his <a href="/wiki/Native_language" class="mw-redirect" title="Native language">native</a> Spanish, he speaks fluent Italian (the official language of Vatican City and the "everyday language" of the Holy See) and German. He is also conversant in Latin (the <a href="/wiki/Official_language" title="Official language">official language</a> of the Holy See),<sup id="cite_ref-141" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-141">&#91;138&#93;</a></sup> French,<sup id="cite_ref-142" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-142">&#91;139&#93;</a></sup> Portuguese,<sup id="cite_ref-143" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-143">&#91;140&#93;</a></sup> and English,<sup id="cite_ref-144" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-144">&#91;141&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-languages_145-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-languages-145">&#91;142&#93;</a></sup> and he understands the <a href="/wiki/Piedmontese_language" title="Piedmontese language">Piedmontese language</a> and some <a href="/wiki/Genoese_dialect" title="Genoese dialect">Genoese</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-146" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-146">&#91;143&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Francis chose not to live in the official <a href="/wiki/Papal_apartments" title="Papal apartments">papal residence</a> in the <a href="/wiki/Apostolic_Palace" title="Apostolic Palace">Apostolic Palace</a>, but to remain in the <a href="/wiki/Domus_Sanctae_Marthae" title="Domus Sanctae Marthae">Vatican guest house</a>, in a suite in which he can receive visitors and hold meetings. He is the first pope since <a href="/wiki/Pope_Pius_X" title="Pope Pius X">Pope Pius X</a> to live outside the papal apartments.<sup id="cite_ref-Vatican_guesthouse_147-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Vatican_guesthouse-147">&#91;144&#93;</a></sup> Francis still appears at the window of the Apostolic Palace for the Sunday <a href="/wiki/Angelus" title="Angelus">Angelus</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-guesthouse_148-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-guesthouse-148">&#91;145&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>As a Jesuit pope, he has been "making clear that a fundamental task of the faithful is not so much to follow rules but to discern what God is calling them to do. He is altering the culture of the clergy, steering away from what he has named as “clericalism” (which dwells on priestly status and authority) and toward an ethic of service (Francis says the church’s shepherds must have the “smell of the sheep,” always staying close to the People of God)."<sup id="cite_ref-149" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-149">&#91;146&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Election">Election</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/2013_papal_conclave" title="2013 papal conclave">2013 papal conclave</a> and <a href="/wiki/Papal_inauguration_of_Pope_Francis" title="Papal inauguration of Pope Francis">Papal inauguration of Pope Francis</a></div>
<div class="thumb tleft"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Papa_Francisco_reci%C3%A9n_elegido_2.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/25/Papa_Francisco_reci%C3%A9n_elegido_2.jpg/220px-Papa_Francisco_reci%C3%A9n_elegido_2.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="154" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/25/Papa_Francisco_reci%C3%A9n_elegido_2.jpg/330px-Papa_Francisco_reci%C3%A9n_elegido_2.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/25/Papa_Francisco_reci%C3%A9n_elegido_2.jpg/440px-Papa_Francisco_reci%C3%A9n_elegido_2.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1004" data-file-height="704" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Papa_Francisco_reci%C3%A9n_elegido_2.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>Francis appears in public for the first time as pope, at St. Peter's Basilica balcony, 13 March 2013.</div></div></div>
<p>Bergoglio was elected pope on 13 March 2013,<sup id="cite_ref-directory_7-8" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-directory-7">&#91;5&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-150" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-150">&#91;147&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-151" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-151">&#91;148&#93;</a></sup> the second day of the <a href="/wiki/2013_papal_conclave" title="2013 papal conclave">2013 papal conclave</a>, taking the <a href="/wiki/Papal_name" title="Papal name">papal name</a> Francis.<sup id="cite_ref-directory_7-9" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-directory-7">&#91;5&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-cnbc_152-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-cnbc-152">&#91;149&#93;</a></sup> Francis was elected on the fifth ballot of the conclave.<sup id="cite_ref-153" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-153">&#91;150&#93;</a></sup> The <i><a href="/wiki/Habemus_papam" title="Habemus papam">Habemus papam</a></i> announcement was delivered by the <a href="/wiki/Cardinal_protodeacon" class="mw-redirect" title="Cardinal protodeacon">cardinal protodeacon</a>, <a href="/wiki/Jean-Louis_Tauran" title="Jean-Louis Tauran">Jean-Louis Tauran</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-SuarezPBS_154-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-SuarezPBS-154">&#91;151&#93;</a></sup> Cardinal <a href="/wiki/Christoph_Sch%C3%B6nborn" title="Christoph Schönborn">Christoph Schönborn</a> later said that Bergoglio was elected following two supernatural signs, one in the conclave and hence confidential, and a Latin-American couple of friends of Schönborn who whispered Bergoglio's name in Schönborn's ear; Schönborn commented "if these people say Bergoglio, that's an indication of the Holy Spirit".<sup id="cite_ref-155" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-155">&#91;152&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Instead of accepting his cardinals' congratulations while seated on the <a href="/wiki/Papal_throne" class="mw-redirect" title="Papal throne">papal throne</a>, Francis received them standing, reportedly an immediate sign of a changing approach to formalities at the Vatican.<sup id="cite_ref-NewEuropeHabemus_156-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-NewEuropeHabemus-156">&#91;153&#93;</a></sup> During his first appearance as pontiff on the balcony of <a href="/wiki/Saint_Peter%27s_Basilica" class="mw-redirect" title="Saint Peter&#39;s Basilica">Saint Peter's Basilica</a>, he wore a white <a href="/wiki/Cassock" title="Cassock">cassock</a>, not the red, ermine-trimmed <a href="/wiki/Mozzetta" title="Mozzetta">mozzetta</a><sup id="cite_ref-NewEuropeHabemus_156-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-NewEuropeHabemus-156">&#91;153&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Uebbing_157-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Uebbing-157">&#91;154&#93;</a></sup> used by previous popes.<sup id="cite_ref-158" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-158">&#91;155&#93;</a></sup> He also wore the same iron <a href="/wiki/Pectoral_cross" title="Pectoral cross">pectoral cross</a> that he had worn as archbishop of Buenos Aires, rather than the gold one worn by his predecessors.<sup id="cite_ref-Uebbing_157-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Uebbing-157">&#91;154&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>After being elected and choosing his name, his first act was bestowing the <i><a href="/wiki/Urbi_et_Orbi" title="Urbi et Orbi">Urbi et Orbi</a></i> blessing on thousands of pilgrims gathered in <a href="/wiki/St._Peter%27s_Square" title="St. Peter&#39;s Square">St. Peter's Square</a>. Before blessing the crowd, he asked those in St. Peter's Square to pray for his predecessor, "the bishop emeritus of Rome" Pope Benedict XVI, and for himself as the new "bishop of Rome".<sup id="cite_ref-159" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-159">&#91;156&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Francis held his <a href="/wiki/Papal_inauguration" title="Papal inauguration">papal inauguration</a> on 19 March 2013 in <a href="/wiki/St._Peter%27s_Square" title="St. Peter&#39;s Square">St. Peter's Square</a> in the <a href="/wiki/Vatican_City" title="Vatican City">Vatican</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-directory_7-10" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-directory-7">&#91;5&#93;</a></sup> He celebrated Mass in the presence of various political and religious leaders from around the world.<sup id="cite_ref-160" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-160">&#91;157&#93;</a></sup> In his homily Francis focused on the <a href="/wiki/Solemnity_of_Saint_Joseph" class="mw-redirect" title="Solemnity of Saint Joseph">Solemnity of Saint Joseph</a>, the liturgical day on which the Mass was celebrated.<sup id="cite_ref-161" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-161">&#91;158&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Name">Name</span></h3>
