<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Pope_Francis_among_the_people_at_St._Peter%27s_Square_-_12_May_2013.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/ba/Pope_Francis_among_the_people_at_St._Peter%27s_Square_-_12_May_2013.jpg/220px-Pope_Francis_among_the_people_at_St._Peter%27s_Square_-_12_May_2013.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="165" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/ba/Pope_Francis_among_the_people_at_St._Peter%27s_Square_-_12_May_2013.jpg/330px-Pope_Francis_among_the_people_at_St._Peter%27s_Square_-_12_May_2013.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/ba/Pope_Francis_among_the_people_at_St._Peter%27s_Square_-_12_May_2013.jpg/440px-Pope_Francis_among_the_people_at_St._Peter%27s_Square_-_12_May_2013.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2560" data-file-height="1920" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Pope_Francis_among_the_people_at_St._Peter%27s_Square_-_12_May_2013.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>Francis in <a href="/wiki/St._Peter%27s_Square" title="St. Peter&#39;s Square">St. Peter's Square</a>, two months after his election</div></div></div>
<p>At his first audience on 16 March 2013, Francis told journalists that he had chosen the name in honor of <a href="/wiki/Francis_of_Assisi" title="Francis of Assisi">Saint Francis of Assisi</a>, and had done so because he was especially concerned for the well-being of the poor.<sup id="cite_ref-Pope_Francis_explains_decision_to_take_St_Francis_of_Assisi&#39;s_name_162-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Pope_Francis_explains_decision_to_take_St_Francis_of_Assisi&#39;s_name-162">&#91;159&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-New_Pope_Francis_visits_St._Mary_Major,_collects_suitcases_and_pays_bill_at_hotel_163-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-New_Pope_Francis_visits_St._Mary_Major,_collects_suitcases_and_pays_bill_at_hotel-163">&#91;160&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-164" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-164">&#91;161&#93;</a></sup> He explained that, as it was becoming clear during the conclave voting that he would be elected the new bishop of Rome, the Brazilian Cardinal <a href="/wiki/Cl%C3%A1udio_Hummes" title="Cláudio Hummes">Cláudio Hummes</a> had embraced him and whispered, "Don't forget the poor", which had made Bergoglio think of the saint.<sup id="cite_ref-165" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-165">&#91;162&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-166" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-166">&#91;163&#93;</a></sup> Bergoglio had previously expressed his admiration for St. Francis, explaining that: "He brought to Christianity an idea of poverty against the luxury, pride, vanity of the civil and ecclesiastical powers of the time. He changed history."<sup id="cite_ref-bethune_167-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-bethune-167">&#91;164&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>This is the first time that a pope has been named <i>Francis</i>. On the day of his election, the Vatican clarified that his official papal name was "Francis", not "Francis I", i.e. no <a href="/wiki/Regnal_number" title="Regnal number">regnal number</a> is used for him. A Vatican spokesman said that the name would become Francis I if and when there is a Francis II.<sup id="cite_ref-New_Pope_Francis_visits_St._Mary_Major,_collects_suitcases_and_pays_bill_at_hotel_163-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-New_Pope_Francis_visits_St._Mary_Major,_collects_suitcases_and_pays_bill_at_hotel-163">&#91;160&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Vatican:_It&#39;s_Pope_Francis,_not_Pope_Francis_I_168-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Vatican:_It&#39;s_Pope_Francis,_not_Pope_Francis_I-168">&#91;165&#93;</a></sup> It is the first time since <a href="/wiki/Pope_Lando" title="Pope Lando">Lando</a>'s 913–914 pontificate that a serving pope holds a name not used by a predecessor.<sup id="cite_ref-170" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-170">&#91;d&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Francis also said that some cardinal electors had jokingly suggested to him that he should choose either "Adrian", since <a href="/wiki/Adrian_VI" class="mw-redirect" title="Adrian VI">Adrian VI</a> had been a reformer of the church, or "Clement" to settle the score with <a href="/wiki/Clement_XIV" class="mw-redirect" title="Clement XIV">Clement XIV</a>, who had <a href="/wiki/Suppression_of_the_Society_of_Jesus" title="Suppression of the Society of Jesus">suppressed the Jesuit order</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-PapalName_140-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-PapalName-140">&#91;137&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-171" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-171">&#91;167&#93;</a></sup> In February 2014, it was reported that Bergoglio, had he been elected in 2005, would have chosen the pontifical name of "John XXIV" in honor of <a href="/wiki/John_XXIII" class="mw-redirect" title="John XXIII">John XXIII</a>. It was said that he told Cardinal <a href="/wiki/Francesco_Marchisano" title="Francesco Marchisano">Francesco Marchisano</a>: "John, I would have called myself John, like the Good Pope; I would have been completely inspired by him".<sup id="cite_ref-172" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-172">&#91;168&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Curia">Curia</span></h3>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Francis_Inauguration_fc10.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b5/Francis_Inauguration_fc10.jpg/220px-Francis_Inauguration_fc10.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="165" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b5/Francis_Inauguration_fc10.jpg/330px-Francis_Inauguration_fc10.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b5/Francis_Inauguration_fc10.jpg/440px-Francis_Inauguration_fc10.jpg 2x" data-file-width="4000" data-file-height="3000" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Francis_Inauguration_fc10.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>Inauguration of Francis, 19 March 2013</div></div></div>
<p>On 16 March 2013, Francis asked all those in senior positions of the <a href="/wiki/Roman_Curia" title="Roman Curia">Roman Curia</a> to provisionally continue in office.<sup id="cite_ref-173" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-173">&#91;169&#93;</a></sup> He named <a href="/wiki/Alfred_Xuereb" title="Alfred Xuereb">Alfred Xuereb</a> as his personal secretary.<sup id="cite_ref-174" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-174">&#91;170&#93;</a></sup> On 6 April he named <a href="/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Rodr%C3%ADguez_Carballo" title="José Rodríguez Carballo">José Rodríguez Carballo</a> as secretary for the <a href="/wiki/Congregation_for_Institutes_of_Consecrated_Life_and_Societies_of_Apostolic_Life" class="mw-redirect" title="Congregation for Institutes of Consecrated Life and Societies of Apostolic Life">Congregation for Institutes of Consecrated Life and Societies of Apostolic Life</a>, a position that had been vacant for several months.<sup id="cite_ref-175" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-175">&#91;171&#93;</a></sup> Francis abolished the bonuses paid to Vatican employees upon the election of a new pope, amounting to several million Euros, opting instead to donate the money to charity.<sup id="cite_ref-176" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-176">&#91;172&#93;</a></sup> He also abolished the €25,000 annual bonus paid to the cardinals serving on the Board of Supervisors for the <a href="/wiki/Institute_for_the_Works_of_Religion" title="Institute for the Works of Religion">Vatican bank</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-177" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-177">&#91;173&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>On 13 April 2013, he named eight cardinals to a new <a href="/wiki/Council_of_Cardinal_Advisers" class="mw-redirect" title="Council of Cardinal Advisers">Council of Cardinal Advisers</a> to advise him on revising the organizational structure of the Roman Curia. The group included several known as critics of Vatican operations and only one member of the Curia.<sup id="cite_ref-178" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-178">&#91;174&#93;</a></sup> They are <a href="/wiki/Giuseppe_Bertello" title="Giuseppe Bertello">Giuseppe Bertello</a>, president of the <a href="/wiki/President_of_the_Pontifical_Commission_for_Vatican_City_State" class="mw-redirect" title="President of the Pontifical Commission for Vatican City State">Vatican City State governorate</a>; <a href="/wiki/Francisco_Javier_Errazuriz_Ossa" class="mw-redirect" title="Francisco Javier Errazuriz Ossa">Francisco Javier Errazuriz Ossa</a> from Chile; <a href="/wiki/Oswald_Gracias" title="Oswald Gracias">Oswald Gracias</a> from India; <a href="/wiki/Reinhard_Marx" title="Reinhard Marx">Reinhard Marx</a> from Germany; <a href="/wiki/Laurent_Monsengwo_Pasinya" title="Laurent Monsengwo Pasinya">Laurent Monsengwo Pasinya</a> from the Democratic Republic of the Congo; <a href="/wiki/George_Pell" title="George Pell">George Pell</a> from Australia; <a href="/wiki/Se%C3%A1n_Patrick_O%27Malley" title="Seán Patrick O&#39;Malley">Seán O'Malley</a> from the United States; and <a href="/wiki/%C3%93scar_Rodr%C3%ADguez_Maradiaga" title="Óscar Rodríguez Maradiaga">Óscar Andrés Rodríguez Maradiaga</a> from Honduras. He appointed Bishop <a href="/wiki/Marcello_Semeraro" title="Marcello Semeraro">Marcello Semeraro</a> secretary for the group and scheduled its first meeting for 1–3 October.<sup id="cite_ref-179" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-179">&#91;175&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Early_issues">Early issues</span></h3>
<p>In March 2013, 21 British Catholic <a href="/wiki/House_of_Lords" title="House of Lords">peers</a> and <a href="/wiki/House_of_Commons_of_the_United_Kingdom" title="House of Commons of the United Kingdom">members of Parliament</a> from all <a href="/wiki/Political_parties_in_the_United_Kingdom" class="mw-redirect" title="Political parties in the United Kingdom">parties</a> asked Francis to allow married men in Great Britain to be ordained as priests, keeping celibacy as the rule for bishops. They asked it on the grounds that it would be anomalous that married Anglican priests can be received into the Catholic Church and ordained as priests, by means of either the <a href="/wiki/Pastoral_Provision" title="Pastoral Provision">Pastoral Provision</a> of 20 June 1980 or the 2009 <a href="/wiki/Anglican_ordinariate" class="mw-redirect" title="Anglican ordinariate">Anglican ordinariate</a>, but married Catholic men cannot do the same.<sup id="cite_ref-teahan_180-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-teahan-180">&#91;176&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p><a href="/wiki/Fouad_Twal" title="Fouad Twal">Fouad Twal</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Latin_patriarch_of_Jerusalem" class="mw-redirect" title="Latin patriarch of Jerusalem">Latin patriarch of Jerusalem</a>, included a call in his 2013 Easter homily for the pope to visit <a href="/wiki/Jerusalem" title="Jerusalem">Jerusalem</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-181" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-181">&#91;177&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Louis_Rapha%C3%ABl_I_Sako" title="Louis Raphaël I Sako">Louis Raphael I</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Chaldean_Catholic_Church" title="Chaldean Catholic Church">Chaldean Catholic Patriarch</a>, asked the pope to visit the "embattled Christian community" in Iraq.<sup id="cite_ref-iraq_182-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-iraq-182">&#91;178&#93;</a></sup> In March 2021, Pope Francis went to Iraq on a first-ever papal visit to the diminishing Christian communities of Mesopotamia fallen apart after years of conflict.<sup id="cite_ref-183" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-183">&#91;179&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>On the first <a href="/wiki/Maundy_Thursday" title="Maundy Thursday">Holy Thursday</a> following his election, Francis washed and kissed the feet of ten male and two female juvenile offenders, not all Catholic, aged from 14 to 21, imprisoned at Rome's Casal del Marmo detention facility, telling them <a href="/wiki/Maundy_(foot_washing)" title="Maundy (foot washing)">the ritual of foot washing</a> is a sign that he is at their service.<sup id="cite_ref-muslimfeetwashing_184-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-muslimfeetwashing-184">&#91;180&#93;</a></sup> This was the first time that a pope had included women in this ritual; although he had already done so when he was archbishop.<sup id="cite_ref-muslimfeetwashing_184-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-muslimfeetwashing-184">&#91;180&#93;</a></sup> One of the male and one of the female prisoners were <a href="/wiki/Muslim" class="mw-redirect" title="Muslim">Muslim</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-muslimfeetwashing_184-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-muslimfeetwashing-184">&#91;180&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>On 31 March 2013, Francis used his first <a href="/wiki/Urbi_et_Orbi" title="Urbi et Orbi">Easter homily</a> to make a plea for peace throughout the world, specifically mentioning the Middle East, Africa, and North and South Korea.<sup id="cite_ref-eastersermon_185-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-eastersermon-185">&#91;181&#93;</a></sup> He also spoke out against those who give in to "easy gain" in a world filled with greed, and made a plea for humanity to become a better guardian of creation by protecting the environment.<sup id="cite_ref-eastersermon_185-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-eastersermon-185">&#91;181&#93;</a></sup> He said that "[w]e ask the risen Jesus, who turns death into life, to change hatred into love, vengeance into forgiveness, war into peace."<sup id="cite_ref-risenjesus_186-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-risenjesus-186">&#91;182&#93;</a></sup> Although the Vatican had prepared greetings in 65 languages, Francis chose not to read them.<sup id="cite_ref-languages_145-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-languages-145">&#91;142&#93;</a></sup> According to the Vatican, the pope "at least for now, feels at ease using Italian, the everyday language of the Holy See".<sup id="cite_ref-187" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-187">&#91;183&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:VISITA_PAPA_FRANCISCO_I_(19473235041).jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c4/VISITA_PAPA_FRANCISCO_I_%2819473235041%29.jpg/220px-VISITA_PAPA_FRANCISCO_I_%2819473235041%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="152" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c4/VISITA_PAPA_FRANCISCO_I_%2819473235041%29.jpg/330px-VISITA_PAPA_FRANCISCO_I_%2819473235041%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c4/VISITA_PAPA_FRANCISCO_I_%2819473235041%29.jpg/440px-VISITA_PAPA_FRANCISCO_I_%2819473235041%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="3543" data-file-height="2447" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:VISITA_PAPA_FRANCISCO_I_(19473235041).jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>Thousands welcomed Francis in <a href="/wiki/Guayaquil" title="Guayaquil">Guayaquil</a>, <a href="/wiki/Ecuador" title="Ecuador">Ecuador</a>, 6 July 2015.</div></div></div>
<p>In 2013, Francis initially reaffirmed the <a href="/wiki/Congregation_for_the_Doctrine_of_the_Faith" class="mw-redirect" title="Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith">Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith</a>'s program to <a href="/wiki/Leadership_Conference_of_Women_Religious#Doctrinal_issues" title="Leadership Conference of Women Religious">reform the U.S. Leadership Conference of Women Religious</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-188" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-188">&#91;184&#93;</a></sup> initiated under his predecessor, Pope Benedict XVI. <i><a href="/wiki/The_New_York_Times" title="The New York Times">The New York Times</a></i> reported that the Vatican had formed the opinion in 2012 that the <a href="/wiki/Religious_sister_(Catholic)" class="mw-redirect" title="Religious sister (Catholic)">sisters</a>' group was tinged with feminist influences, focused too much on ending social and economic injustice and not enough on stopping abortion, and permitted speakers at its meetings who questioned church doctrine.<sup id="cite_ref-189" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-189">&#91;185&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-190" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-190">&#91;186&#93;</a></sup> However, in April 2015 the investigation was brought to a close. While the timing of the closure may have anticipated <a href="/wiki/Pope_Francis%27s_visit_to_the_United_States" class="mw-redirect" title="Pope Francis&#39;s visit to the United States">a visit by Francis to the U.S.</a> in September 2015, it was noted that the sisters' emphasis is close to that of Francis.<sup id="cite_ref-191" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-191">&#91;187&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>On 12 May, Francis carried out his first <a href="/wiki/Canonization" title="Canonization">canonizations</a> of candidates approved for sainthood during the reign of Benedict XVI: the first Colombian saint, <a href="/wiki/Laura_of_Saint_Catherine_of_Siena" class="mw-redirect" title="Laura of Saint Catherine of Siena">Laura of Saint Catherine of Siena</a>, the second female Mexican saint, <a href="/wiki/Mar%C3%ADa_Guadalupe_Garc%C3%ADa_Zavala" title="María Guadalupe García Zavala">María Guadalupe García Zavala</a>, both of the 20th century, and the 813 15th-century <a href="/wiki/Martyrs_of_Otranto" title="Martyrs of Otranto">Martyrs of Otranto</a>. He said: "While we venerate the martyrs of Otranto, ask God to support the many Christians who still suffer from violence and give them the courage and fate and respond to evil with goodness."<sup id="cite_ref-auto1_192-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-auto1-192">&#91;188&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Synodal_church">Synodal church</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Theology_of_Pope_Francis#Decentralization" title="Theology of Pope Francis">Theology of Pope Francis §&#160;Decentralization</a></div>
<p>Francis has overseen synods on <a href="/wiki/Third_Extraordinary_General_Assembly_of_the_Synod_of_Bishops" title="Third Extraordinary General Assembly of the Synod of Bishops">the family</a> (2014), on <a href="/wiki/Fifteenth_Ordinary_General_Assembly_of_the_Synod_of_Bishops" title="Fifteenth Ordinary General Assembly of the Synod of Bishops">youth</a> (2018), and on the church in the <a href="/wiki/Amazon_rainforest" title="Amazon rainforest">Amazon region</a> (2019). In 2019 Francis's apostolic constitution <i>Episcopalis communio</i> allowed that the final document of a synod may become magisterial teaching simply with papal approval. The constitution also allowed for laity to contribute input directly to the synod's secretary general.<sup id="cite_ref-sept18_193-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-sept18-193">&#91;189&#93;</a></sup> Some analysts see the creation of a truly synodal church as likely to become the greatest contribution of Francis's papacy.<sup id="cite_ref-194" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-194">&#91;190&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Consultation_with_Catholic_laity">Consultation with Catholic laity</span></h3>
<div class="thumb tleft"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:FrancisQuitoR.png" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0e/FrancisQuitoR.png/220px-FrancisQuitoR.png" decoding="async" width="220" height="242" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0e/FrancisQuitoR.png/330px-FrancisQuitoR.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0e/FrancisQuitoR.png/440px-FrancisQuitoR.png 2x" data-file-width="2009" data-file-height="2209" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:FrancisQuitoR.png" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>Francis in <a href="/wiki/Quito" title="Quito">Quito</a>, Ecuador, 2015</div></div></div>
<p>A February 2014 survey by the <a href="/wiki/World_Values_Survey" title="World Values Survey">World Values Survey</a> cited in <i><a href="/wiki/The_Washington_Post" title="The Washington Post">The Washington Post</a></i> and <i><a href="/wiki/Time_(magazine)" title="Time (magazine)">Time</a></i> shows how the unity Francis had created could be challenged. Although views about Francis personally were favorable, many Catholics disagreed with at least some of his teachings. The survey found that members of the Catholic Church are deeply divided over abortion, artificial contraception, divorce, the ordination of women, and married priests.<sup id="cite_ref-195" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-195">&#91;191&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-196" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-196">&#91;192&#93;</a></sup> In the same month Francis asked parishes to provide answers to an official questionnaire<sup id="cite_ref-197" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-197">&#91;193&#93;</a></sup> described as a "much broader consultation than just a survey"<sup id="cite_ref-bbc27060172_198-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-bbc27060172-198">&#91;194&#93;</a></sup> regarding opinions among the laity. He continued to assert <a href="/wiki/Catholic_theology" title="Catholic theology">Catholic doctrine</a>, in less dramatic tone than his recent predecessors, who maintained that the Catholic Church is not a democracy of popular opinion.<sup id="cite_ref-Clement_199-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Clement-199">&#91;195&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p><a href="/wiki/Linda_Woodhead" title="Linda Woodhead">Linda Woodhead</a> of <a href="/wiki/Lancaster_University" title="Lancaster University">Lancaster University</a> wrote of the survey Francis initiated, "it's not a survey in any sense that a social scientist would recognize." Woodhead said that many ordinary Catholics would have difficulty understanding theological <a href="/wiki/Jargon" title="Jargon">jargon</a> there. Nonetheless, she suspected the survey might be influential.<sup id="cite_ref-200" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-200">&#91;196&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Catholic_Church_in_England_and_Wales" title="Catholic Church in England and Wales">Catholic Church in England and Wales</a> as of April&#160;2014<sup class="plainlinks noexcerpt noprint asof-tag update" style="display:none;"><a class="external text" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pope_Francis&amp;action=edit">&#91;update&#93;</a></sup> had refused to publish results of this survey; a church spokesman said a senior Vatican official had expressly asked for summaries to remain confidential, and that orders had come from the pope that the information should not be made public until after October. This disappointed many reformers who hoped the laity would be more involved in decision-making. Some other Catholic churches, for example in <a href="/wiki/Catholic_Church_in_Germany" title="Catholic Church in Germany">Germany</a> and <a href="/wiki/Catholic_Church_in_Austria" title="Catholic Church in Austria">Austria</a>, published summaries of the responses to the survey, which showed a wide gap between church teaching and the behavior of ordinary Catholics.<sup id="cite_ref-bbc27060172_198-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-bbc27060172-198">&#91;194&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In a column he wrote for the Vatican's semi-official newspaper <i><a href="/wiki/L%27Osservatore_Romano" title="L&#39;Osservatore Romano">L'Osservatore Romano</a></i>, the then-Prefect of the <a href="/wiki/Supreme_Tribunal_of_the_Apostolic_Signatura" class="mw-redirect" title="Supreme Tribunal of the Apostolic Signatura">Supreme Tribunal of the Apostolic Signatura</a>, American cardinal <a href="/wiki/Raymond_Leo_Burke" title="Raymond Leo Burke">Raymond Leo Burke</a>, who has a long-standing reputation as one of the church's most vocal conservative hard-liners, said that Francis opposed both abortion and <a href="/wiki/Gay_marriage" class="mw-redirect" title="Gay marriage">gay marriage</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-201" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-201">&#91;197&#93;</a></sup> The Vatican's chief spokesman, Father <a href="/wiki/Federico_Lombardi" title="Federico Lombardi">Federico Lombardi</a>, also noted in the Vatican press office during the 2014 consistory meetings that Francis and Cardinal <a href="/wiki/Walter_Kasper" title="Walter Kasper">Walter Kasper</a> would not change or redefine any dogmas pertaining to church theology on doctrinal matters.<sup id="cite_ref-202" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-202">&#91;198&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Institute_for_the_Works_of_Religion">Institute for the Works of Religion</span></h3>
<p>In the first months of Francis's papacy, the <a href="/wiki/Institute_for_the_Works_of_Religion" title="Institute for the Works of Religion">Institute for the Works of Religion</a>, informally known as the Vatican Bank, said that it would become more transparent in its financial dealings<sup id="cite_ref-203" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-203">&#91;199&#93;</a></sup> There had long been allegations of corruption and <a href="/wiki/Money_laundering" title="Money laundering">money laundering</a> connected with the bank.<sup id="cite_ref-bank1_204-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-bank1-204">&#91;200&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-bank2_205-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-bank2-205">&#91;201&#93;</a></sup> Francis appointed a commission to advise him about reform of the Bank,<sup id="cite_ref-bank1_204-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-bank1-204">&#91;200&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-bank2_205-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-bank2-205">&#91;201&#93;</a></sup> and the finance consulting firm <a href="/wiki/Promontory_Financial_Group" title="Promontory Financial Group">Promontory Financial Group</a> was assigned to carry out a comprehensive investigation of all customer contacts of the bank on these facts.<sup id="cite_ref-206" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-206">&#91;202&#93;</a></sup> Because of this affair the <a href="/wiki/Devil%27s_advocate#Origin_and_history" title="Devil&#39;s advocate">Promoter of Justice</a> at the <a href="/wiki/Law_of_Vatican_City" title="Law of Vatican City">Vatican Tribunal</a> applied a <a href="/wiki/Letter_rogatory" class="mw-redirect" title="Letter rogatory">letter rogatory</a> for the first time in the history of the Republic of Italy at the beginning of August 2013.<sup id="cite_ref-207" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-207">&#91;203&#93;</a></sup> In January 2014, Francis replaced four of the five cardinal overseers of the Vatican Bank, who had been confirmed in their positions in the final days of Benedict XVI's papacy.<sup id="cite_ref-208" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-208">&#91;204&#93;</a></sup> Lay experts and clerics were looking into how the bank was run. <a href="/wiki/Ernst_von_Freyberg" title="Ernst von Freyberg">Ernst von Freyberg</a> was put in charge. <a href="/wiki/Moneyval" title="Moneyval">Moneyval</a> feels more reform is needed, and Francis may be willing to close the bank if the reforms prove too difficult.<sup id="cite_ref-Jones_209-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Jones-209">&#91;205&#93;</a></sup> There is uncertainty how far reforms can succeed.<sup id="cite_ref-210" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-210">&#91;206&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Papal_documents">Papal documents</span></h3>
<p>On 29 June 2013, Francis published the <a href="/wiki/Encyclical" title="Encyclical">encyclical</a> <i><a href="/wiki/Lumen_fidei" title="Lumen fidei">Lumen fidei</a></i>, which was largely the work of Benedict XVI but awaiting a final draft at his retirement.<sup id="cite_ref-211" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-211">&#91;207&#93;</a></sup> On 24 November 2013, Francis published his first major letter as pope, the <a href="/wiki/Apostolic_exhortation" title="Apostolic exhortation">apostolic exhortation</a> <i><a href="/wiki/Evangelii_gaudium" title="Evangelii gaudium">Evangelii gaudium</a></i>,<sup id="cite_ref-212" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-212">&#91;208&#93;</a></sup> which he described as the programmatic of his papacy.<sup id="cite_ref-ReferenceB_213-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ReferenceB-213">&#91;209&#93;</a></sup> On 18 June 2015, he published his first own, original encyclical <i><a href="/wiki/Laudato_si%27" title="Laudato si&#39;">Laudato si'</a></i> concerning care for the planet.<sup id="cite_ref-214" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-214">&#91;210&#93;</a></sup> On 8 April 2016, Francis published his second apostolic exhortation, <i><a href="/wiki/Amoris_laetitia" title="Amoris laetitia">Amoris laetitia</a></i>,<sup id="cite_ref-Amoris_laetitia_215-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Amoris_laetitia-215">&#91;211&#93;</a></sup> remarking on love within the family. Controversy arose at the end of 2016 when four cardinals formally asked Francis for clarifications, particularly on the issue of giving communion to divorced and civilly remarried Catholics.<sup id="cite_ref-216" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-216">&#91;212&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>His <a href="/wiki/Motu_proprio" title="Motu proprio"><i>motu proprios</i></a> include <i>Ai nostri tempi</i> and <i>De concordia inter codices</i>. Francis issued another titled <i><a href="/wiki/Maiorem_hac_dilectionem" title="Maiorem hac dilectionem">Maiorem hac dilectionem</a></i> which created a new path towards canonization for certain causes.
</p><p>He established two new Secretariats (top-level departments) in the Roman Curia: the <a href="/wiki/Secretariat_for_the_Economy" title="Secretariat for the Economy">Secretariat for the Economy</a>, and the <a href="/wiki/Secretariat_for_Communications" class="mw-redirect" title="Secretariat for Communications">Secretariat for Communications</a>. He <a href="/wiki/Matrimonial_nullity_trial_reforms_of_Pope_Francis" title="Matrimonial nullity trial reforms of Pope Francis">simplified</a> the process for declaring <a href="/wiki/Declaration_of_nullity" title="Declaration of nullity">matrimonial nullity</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-trials_217-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-trials-217">&#91;213&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>On 8 December 2017, Francis signed a new apostolic constitution on ecclesiastical universities and faculties <i><a href="/wiki/Veritatis_gaudium" title="Veritatis gaudium">Veritatis gaudium</a></i>, published 29 January 2018.<sup id="cite_ref-218" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-218">&#91;214&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>A further Apostolic Exhortation, <i><a href="/wiki/Gaudete_et_exsultate" title="Gaudete et exsultate">Gaudete et exsultate</a></i> (<i>Rejoice and be glad</i>), was published on 19 March 2018, dealing with "the <a href="/wiki/Universal_call_to_holiness" title="Universal call to holiness">call to holiness</a> in today's world" for all persons. He counters contemporary versions of the <a href="/wiki/Gnosticism" title="Gnosticism">gnostic</a> and <a href="/wiki/Pelagianism" title="Pelagianism">Pelagian</a> <a href="/wiki/Heresy_in_Christianity" title="Heresy in Christianity">heresies</a> and describes how Jesus' beatitudes call people to "go against the flow".<sup id="cite_ref-219" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-219">&#91;215&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In February 2019, Francis acknowledged that priests and bishops were sexually abusing <a href="/wiki/Religious_sister_(Catholic)" class="mw-redirect" title="Religious sister (Catholic)">religious sisters</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-220" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-220">&#91;216&#93;</a></sup> He addressed this and the <a href="/wiki/Clergy_sex_abuse_scandal" class="mw-redirect" title="Clergy sex abuse scandal">clergy sex abuse scandal</a> by convening a summit on clergy sexual abuse in Rome 21–24 February 2019.<sup id="cite_ref-221" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-221">&#91;217&#93;</a></sup> As a follow-up to that summit, on 9 May 2019 Francis <a href="/wiki/Promulgated" class="mw-redirect" title="Promulgated">promulgated</a> the <i><a href="/wiki/Motu_proprio" title="Motu proprio">motu proprio</a></i> <i><a href="/wiki/Vos_estis_lux_mundi" title="Vos estis lux mundi">Vos estis lux mundi</a></i> which specified responsibilities, including reporting directly to the <a href="/wiki/Holy_See" title="Holy See">Holy See</a> on bishops and on one's superior, while simultaneously involving another bishop in the <a href="/wiki/Archdiocese" class="mw-redirect" title="Archdiocese">archdiocese</a> of the accused bishop.<sup id="cite_ref-222" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-222">&#91;218&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>On 30 September 2020, he published the apostolic letter <i><a href="/wiki/Scripturae_sacrae_affectus" class="mw-redirect" title="Scripturae sacrae affectus">Scripturae sacrae affectus</a></i> to celebrate the 16th centenary of the death of <a href="/wiki/Jerome" title="Jerome">Jerome</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-223" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-223">&#91;219&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-224" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-224">&#91;220&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>On 4 October 2020 on the feast of St. Francis of Assisi, Francis published the encyclical <i><a href="/wiki/Fratelli_tutti" title="Fratelli tutti">Fratelli tutti</a></i> on fraternity and social friendship, using St. Francis's own words to describe our universal brotherhood and sisterhood.<sup id="cite_ref-:11_225-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:11-225">&#91;221&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>On 8 December 2020 on the Feast of the <a href="/wiki/Immaculate_Conception" title="Immaculate Conception">Immaculate Conception</a>, Pope Francis published the <a href="/wiki/Apostolic_letter" class="mw-redirect" title="Apostolic letter">apostolic letter</a> <i>Patris corde</i> ("With a Father's Heart").<sup id="cite_ref-226" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-226">&#91;222&#93;</a></sup> To mark the occasion, the Pope proclaimed a "Year of Saint Joseph" from 8 December 2020, to 8 December 2021 on the 150th Anniversary of the Proclamation of <a href="/wiki/Saint_Joseph" title="Saint Joseph">Saint Joseph</a> as <a href="/wiki/Patron" class="mw-redirect" title="Patron">Patron</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Catholic_Church" title="Catholic Church">Universal Church</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-227" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-227">&#91;223&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>On 1 June 2021, Francis published the apostolic constitution <i><a href="/wiki/Pascite_gregem_Dei" title="Pascite gregem Dei">Pascite gregem Dei</a></i>.<sup id="cite_ref-228" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-228">&#91;224&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Pope Francis issued the <i>motu proprio</i> <i><a href="/wiki/Traditionis_custodes" title="Traditionis custodes">Traditionis custodes</a></i> on 16 July 2021. The document abrogated the permissions for the celebration of the <a href="/wiki/Tridentine_Mass" title="Tridentine Mass">Tridentine Mass</a> previously established by Benedict XVI in the 2007 <i><a href="/wiki/Summorum_Pontificum" title="Summorum Pontificum">Summorum Pontificum</a></i>, with <i>Traditionis custodes</i> instituting increased restrictions on the use of the 1962 <a href="/wiki/Roman_Missal" title="Roman Missal">Roman Missal</a>. Pope Francis stated in a letter accompanying the <i>motu proprio</i> that emphasizing the <a href="/wiki/Mass_of_Paul_VI" title="Mass of Paul VI">Mass of Paul VI</a> would bring "unity I intend to re-establish throughout the Church of the Roman Rite."<sup id="cite_ref-229" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-229">&#91;225&#93;</a></sup> On 11 February, Pope Francis met with two priests from the <a href="/wiki/Priestly_Fraternity_of_Saint_Peter" title="Priestly Fraternity of Saint Peter">Priestly Fraternity of Saint Peter</a> (FSSP) and reassured them that <i>Traditionis Custodes</i> did not affect their community and gave them permission, in writing, to use all the liturgical books of 1962. He also implied that <i>Traditionis Custodes</i> did not apply to all traditional Catholic communities, not just the FSSP.<sup id="cite_ref-230" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-230">&#91;226&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Ecumenism_and_interreligious_dialogue">Ecumenism and interreligious dialogue</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Pope_Francis:_ecumenism_and_interreligious_dialogue" class="mw-redirect" title="Pope Francis: ecumenism and interreligious dialogue">Pope Francis: ecumenism and interreligious dialogue</a></div>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Stamps_of_Azerbaijan,_2016-1283s.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/92/Stamps_of_Azerbaijan%2C_2016-1283s.jpg/220px-Stamps_of_Azerbaijan%2C_2016-1283s.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="183" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/92/Stamps_of_Azerbaijan%2C_2016-1283s.jpg/330px-Stamps_of_Azerbaijan%2C_2016-1283s.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/92/Stamps_of_Azerbaijan%2C_2016-1283s.jpg/440px-Stamps_of_Azerbaijan%2C_2016-1283s.jpg 2x" data-file-width="960" data-file-height="799" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Stamps_of_Azerbaijan,_2016-1283s.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>The stamp is dedicated to the pastoral visit of Francis to <a href="/wiki/Azerbaijan" title="Azerbaijan">Azerbaijan</a> on 2 October 2016.</div></div></div>
<p>Pope Francis continued in the tradition of the <a href="/wiki/Second_Vatican_Council" title="Second Vatican Council">Second Vatican Council</a> and of the papacies since the Council in promoting <a href="/wiki/Ecumenism" title="Ecumenism">ecumenism</a> with other <a href="/wiki/Christian_denominations" class="mw-redirect" title="Christian denominations">Christian denominations</a>, as well as encouraging dialogue with leaders of other religions; he has also supported peace with those claiming no religious belief.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Clerical_titles">Clerical titles</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Theology_of_Pope_Francis#Clericalism" title="Theology of Pope Francis">Theology of Pope Francis §&#160;Clericalism</a></div>
<p>In January 2014, Francis said that he would appoint fewer <a href="/wiki/Monsignor" title="Monsignor">monsignors</a> and only assign those honored to the lowest of the three surviving ranks of monsignor, <a href="/wiki/Chaplain_of_His_Holiness" title="Chaplain of His Holiness">chaplain of His Holiness</a>. It would be awarded only to <a href="/wiki/Diocesan_priest" class="mw-redirect" title="Diocesan priest">diocesan priests</a> at least 65 years old. During his 15 years as archbishop of Buenos Aires, Francis never sought the title for any of his priests. It is believed he associates it with clerical careerism and hierarchy, though he did not apply this restriction to clergy working in the Roman Curia or diplomatic corps, where careerism is an even greater concern.<sup id="cite_ref-231" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-231">&#91;227&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Canonizations_and_beatifications">Canonizations and beatifications</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/List_of_saints_canonized_by_Pope_Francis" title="List of saints canonized by Pope Francis">List of saints canonized by Pope Francis</a>, <a href="/wiki/List_of_people_beatified_by_Pope_Francis" title="List of people beatified by Pope Francis">List of people beatified by Pope Francis</a>, and <a href="/wiki/List_of_people_declared_venerable_by_Pope_Francis" title="List of people declared venerable by Pope Francis">List of people declared venerable by Pope Francis</a></div>
<p>Francis presided over the first canonizations of his pontificate on 12 May 2013 in which he canonized the <a href="/wiki/Martyrs_of_Otranto" title="Martyrs of Otranto">Martyrs of Otranto</a>. Antonio Primaldo and his 812 companions who had been <a href="/wiki/Ottoman_invasion_of_Otranto" title="Ottoman invasion of Otranto">executed by the Ottomans</a> in 1480,<sup id="cite_ref-232" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-232">&#91;228&#93;</a></sup> as well as the <a href="/wiki/Religious_sister_(Catholic)" class="mw-redirect" title="Religious sister (Catholic)">religious sisters</a> <a href="/wiki/Laura_Montoya" title="Laura Montoya">Laura of St. Catherine of Siena</a> and <a href="/wiki/Mar%C3%ADa_Guadalupe_Garc%C3%ADa_Zavala" title="María Guadalupe García Zavala">María Guadalupe García Zavala</a> – in this first canonization he surpassed the record of Pope John Paul II in canonizing the most saints in a pontificate.<sup id="cite_ref-auto1_192-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-auto1-192">&#91;188&#93;</a></sup> Francis approved the <a href="/wiki/Equipollent_canonization" class="mw-redirect" title="Equipollent canonization">equipollent canonization</a> of <a href="/wiki/Angela_of_Foligno" title="Angela of Foligno">Angela of Foligno</a> the following 9 October and then the Jesuit <a href="/wiki/Peter_Faber" title="Peter Faber">Peter Faber</a> the following 17 December.<sup id="cite_ref-233" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-233">&#91;229&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-234" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-234">&#91;230&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The pope approved further equipollent canonizations on 3 April 2014 for the Jesuit <a href="/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_de_Anchieta" class="mw-redirect" title="José de Anchieta">José de Anchieta</a> as well as the <a href="/wiki/Ursulines" title="Ursulines">Ursuline</a> nun <a href="/wiki/Marie_of_the_Incarnation_(Ursuline)" title="Marie of the Incarnation (Ursuline)">Marie of the Incarnation</a> and bishop <a href="/wiki/Fran%C3%A7ois_de_Laval" title="François de Laval">François de Laval</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-235" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-235">&#91;231&#93;</a></sup> Francis canonized his two predecessors John XXIII and John Paul II on 27 April 2014 and canonized six additional saints the following 23 November.<sup id="cite_ref-236" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-236">&#91;232&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-237" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-237">&#91;233&#93;</a></sup> The pope canonized <a href="/wiki/Joseph_Vaz" title="Joseph Vaz">Joseph Vaz</a> on his visit to Sri Lanka on 14 January 2015 and canonized a further four saints on the following 17 May; he canonized Junípero Serra on 23 September while visiting the United States and then canonized four saints on 18 October including the <a href="/wiki/Louis_Martin_and_Marie-Az%C3%A9lie_Gu%C3%A9rin" title="Louis Martin and Marie-Azélie Guérin">first married couple</a> to be named as saints.<sup id="cite_ref-238" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-238">&#91;234&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-239" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-239">&#91;235&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-240" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-240">&#91;236&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-241" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-241">&#91;237&#93;</a></sup> Francis canonized <a href="/wiki/Elisabeth_Hesselblad" class="mw-redirect" title="Elisabeth Hesselblad">Maria Elisabeth Hesselblad</a> and <a href="/wiki/Stanislaus_Papczy%C5%84ski" title="Stanislaus Papczyński">Stanislaus Papczyński</a> on 5 June 2016 and then canonized <a href="/wiki/Teresa_of_Calcutta" class="mw-redirect" title="Teresa of Calcutta">Teresa of Calcutta</a> on 4 September; he canonized seven additional saints on 16 October.<sup id="cite_ref-242" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-242">&#91;238&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-243" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-243">&#91;239&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-244" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-244">&#91;240&#93;</a></sup> The pope canonized the two child visionaries <a href="/wiki/Francisco_and_Jacinta_Marto" title="Francisco and Jacinta Marto">Francisco and Jacinta Marto</a> during his visit to Fátima in mid-2017 and canonized 35 additional saints on 15 October.<sup id="cite_ref-245" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-245">&#91;241&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-246" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-246">&#91;242&#93;</a></sup> Francis recognized seven saints on 14 October 2018, chief among them, his predecessor Pope Paul VI and <a href="/wiki/%C3%93scar_Romero" title="Óscar Romero">Óscar Romero</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-247" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-247">&#91;243&#93;</a></sup> Francis later confirmed the equipollent canonization for <a href="/wiki/Bartholomew_of_Braga" title="Bartholomew of Braga">Bartholomew of Braga</a> in mid-2019.<sup id="cite_ref-248" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-248">&#91;244&#93;</a></sup> On 13 October 2019, Francis canonized five new saints, including Cardinal <a href="/wiki/John_Henry_Newman" title="John Henry Newman">John Henry Newman</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-249" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-249">&#91;245&#93;</a></sup> The pope confirmed the equipollent canonization for <a href="/wiki/Margaret_of_Castello" title="Margaret of Castello">Margherita della Metola</a> on 24 April 2021.<sup id="cite_ref-250" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-250">&#91;246&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The pope has also continued the practice of having beatifications celebrated in the place of the individual's origin though has presided over beatifications himself on three occasions: for <a href="/wiki/Korean_Martyrs" title="Korean Martyrs">Paul Yun Ji-Chung and 123 companions</a> on 16 August 2014, his predecessor Pope Paul VI on 19 October 2014, and two Colombian martyrs on 8 September 2017.<sup id="cite_ref-251" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-251">&#91;247&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-252" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-252">&#91;248&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-253" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-253">&#91;249&#93;</a></sup> The pope has approved beatifications for a range of men and women including the likes of <a href="/wiki/%C3%81lvaro_del_Portillo" title="Álvaro del Portillo">Álvaro del Portillo</a> of <a href="/wiki/Opus_Dei" title="Opus Dei">Opus Dei</a> (27 September 2014), the martyred archbishop Óscar Romero (23 May 2015), the prominent Polish cardinal <a href="/wiki/Stefan_Wyszy%C5%84ski" title="Stefan Wyszyński">Stefan Wyszyński</a> (12 September 2021), and several large groups of <a href="/wiki/Martyrs_of_the_Spanish_Civil_War" title="Martyrs of the Spanish Civil War">Spanish martyrs</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-254" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-254">&#91;250&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Francis also confirmed his predecessor <a href="/wiki/Pope_John_Paul_I" title="Pope John Paul I">John Paul I</a> to be <a href="/wiki/Venerable" class="mw-redirect" title="Venerable">Venerable</a> on 8 November 2017.<sup id="cite_ref-255" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-255">&#91;251&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Doctors_of_the_Church">Doctors of the Church</span></h3>
<p>On 21 February 2015, Francis signed a decree naming <a href="/wiki/Gregory_of_Narek" title="Gregory of Narek">Saint Gregory of Narek</a> as the 36th <a href="/wiki/Doctor_of_the_Church" title="Doctor of the Church">Doctor of the Church</a>; he formally conferred the title upon the saint at a ceremony held in Saint Peter's Basilica on 12 April 2015 with delegations from the <a href="/wiki/Armenian_Catholic_Church" title="Armenian Catholic Church">Armenian Catholic Church</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Armenian_Apostolic_Church" title="Armenian Apostolic Church">Armenian Apostolic Church</a> present.<sup id="cite_ref-256" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-256">&#91;252&#93;</a></sup> On 20 January 2022, Francis provided his approval to the suggestion to name <a href="/wiki/Irenaeus" title="Irenaeus">Saint Irenaeus of Lyon</a> as the 37th Doctor of the Church, formally conferring the title upon him, along with the supplementary title <i>Doctor unitatis</i> ("Doctor of Unity") in a decree issued on 21 January.<sup id="cite_ref-257" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-257">&#91;253&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Consistories">Consistories</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Cardinals_created_by_Francis" title="Cardinals created by Francis">Cardinals created by Francis</a></div>
<p>At the first <a href="/wiki/Papal_consistory" title="Papal consistory">consistory</a> of his papacy, held on 22 February 2014, Francis created 19 new cardinals. At the time of their elevation to that rank, 16 of these new cardinals were under eighty years of age and thus eligible to vote in a <a href="/wiki/Papal_conclave" title="Papal conclave">papal conclave</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-258" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-258">&#91;254&#93;</a></sup> The new appointees included prelates from South America, Africa, and Asia, including appointees in some of the world's poorest countries, such as <a href="/wiki/Chibly_Langlois" title="Chibly Langlois">Chibly Langlois</a> from <a href="/wiki/Haiti" title="Haiti">Haiti</a> and <a href="/wiki/Philippe_Ou%C3%A9draogo_(bishop)" class="mw-redirect" title="Philippe Ouédraogo (bishop)">Philippe Nakellentuba Ouedraogo</a> from <a href="/wiki/Burkina_Faso" title="Burkina Faso">Burkina Faso</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Reuters_259-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Reuters-259">&#91;255&#93;</a></sup> The consistory was a rare occasion in which Francis and his predecessor, <a href="/wiki/Benedict_XVI" class="mw-redirect" title="Benedict XVI">Benedict XVI</a>, appeared together in public.<sup id="cite_ref-Reuters_259-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Reuters-259">&#91;255&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Benedict XVI also attended the second consistory on 14 February 2015, at which Francis elevated 20 new cardinals, with 15 under the age of eighty and five over the age of eighty. The pope continued his practice of appointing cardinals from the peripheries, such as <a href="/wiki/Charles_Maung_Bo" title="Charles Maung Bo">Charles Maung Bo</a> of <a href="/wiki/Myanmar" title="Myanmar">Myanmar</a> and <a href="/wiki/Soane_Patita_Paini_Mafi" title="Soane Patita Paini Mafi">Soane Patita Paini Mafi</a> of <a href="/wiki/Tonga" title="Tonga">Tonga</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-260" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-260">&#91;256&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Francis presided over the third consistory of his papacy on 19 November 2016, elevating 17 new cardinals. Of that total number at the time of their elevation, 13 were under the age of eighty and four were over the age of eighty. Francis continued his previous practice of elevating cardinals from the peripheries with an emphasis again on Asia and Africa, such as <a href="/wiki/Patrick_D%27Rozario" title="Patrick D&#39;Rozario">Patrick D'Rozario</a> from Bangladesh and <a href="/wiki/Dieudonn%C3%A9_Nzapalainga" title="Dieudonné Nzapalainga">Dieudonné Nzapalainga</a> from the <a href="/wiki/Central_African_Republic" title="Central African Republic">Central African Republic</a>, while also naming the first three American cardinals of his papacy and only one Curial appointment.<sup id="cite_ref-261" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-261">&#91;257&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The pope presided over a fourth consistory for the elevation of five new cardinals on the afternoon of 28 June 2017. Each of the five were under the age of eighty, and were thus eligible to vote in a papal conclave. This consistory was noteworthy for the fact that, with the pope continuing the trend of elevating cardinals from a diverse range of areas, no cardinals elevated are of the Roman Curia, and one was a mere auxiliary bishop.<sup id="cite_ref-262" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-262">&#91;258&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Francis presided over his fifth consistory for the elevation of 14 new cardinals on 28 June 2018. The first eleven were under the age of eighty, and therefore, were eligible to vote in a future papal conclave while the last three were over the age of eighty, and thus, ineligible to vote in a papal conclave.<sup id="cite_ref-263" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-263">&#91;259&#93;</a></sup> The pope continued the practice of naming the <a href="/wiki/Vicar_of_Rome" class="mw-redirect" title="Vicar of Rome">Vicar of Rome</a> and a curial prefect as cardinals, while naming his substitute for the Secretariat of State in anticipation of his transferral to a curial department. The pope also continued his practice of bestowing the red hat on those from peripheries such as Madagascar, Pakistan, and Iraq, and like in 2016, created a priest as a cardinal. The consistory was also noteworthy for the fact that Francis named the papal almoner <a href="/wiki/Konrad_Krajewski" title="Konrad Krajewski">Konrad Krajewski</a> as a cardinal, marking the consistory the first occasion where the almoner was made a cardinal. Francis himself later said that he wanted the office of almoner to receive the red hat going forward as it was an important arm of the Vatican.<sup id="cite_ref-264" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-264">&#91;260&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>On 1 September 2019, following his weekly Sunday Angelus address, Francis unexpectedly announced the appointment of 13 new cardinals. Of these, 10 appointees were under the age of 80 and would therefore become <a href="/wiki/Cardinal_electors" class="mw-redirect" title="Cardinal electors">cardinal electors</a>, besides three over 80. The new cardinals were formally installed at the consistory celebrated on 5 October 2019.<sup id="cite_ref-R0901_265-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-R0901-265">&#91;261&#93;</a></sup> Most of the new cardinals come from the peripheries of the church and developing countries. Two new appointees were from Muslim majority countries (<a href="/wiki/Morocco" title="Morocco">Morocco</a> and <a href="/wiki/Indonesia" title="Indonesia">Indonesia</a>), while two others were known for their work on refugee and migration issues.<sup id="cite_ref-266" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-266">&#91;262&#93;</a></sup> This action took the number of <a href="/wiki/Cardinal_electors" class="mw-redirect" title="Cardinal electors">cardinal electors</a> appointed by Francis to the <a href="/wiki/College_of_Cardinals" title="College of Cardinals">College of Cardinals</a> to about 70 out of nearly 130.<sup id="cite_ref-R0901_265-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-R0901-265">&#91;261&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Francis created thirteen new cardinals on 28 November 2020; nine appointees were under the age of 80, therefore, could vote in a future papal conclave.<sup id="cite_ref-25October2020_267-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-25October2020-267">&#91;263&#93;</a></sup> The pope also nominated four cardinals over the age of 80. Most of these new appointees continued the trend that Francis adhered to, appointing the first cardinals to represent <a href="/wiki/Brunei" title="Brunei">Brunei</a> and <a href="/wiki/Rwanda" title="Rwanda">Rwanda</a>. Francis also nominated the first <a href="/wiki/African_American" class="mw-redirect" title="African American">African American</a> cardinal (<a href="/wiki/Wilton_Daniel_Gregory" title="Wilton Daniel Gregory">Gregory</a>), while naming the first <a href="/wiki/Conventual_Franciscan" class="mw-redirect" title="Conventual Franciscan">Conventual Franciscan</a> (<a href="/wiki/Mauro_Gambetti" title="Mauro Gambetti">Gambetti</a>) in almost 160 years, and the first from Siena (<a href="/wiki/Augusto_Paolo_Lojudice" title="Augusto Paolo Lojudice">Lojudice</a>) since 1801.<sup id="cite_ref-268" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-268">&#91;264&#93;</a></sup> Three of his appointees were only priests upon their nomination, therefore, two (Gambetti and <a href="/wiki/Enrico_Feroci" title="Enrico Feroci">Feroci</a>) received their <a href="/wiki/Episcopal_consecration" class="mw-redirect" title="Episcopal consecration">episcopal consecration</a>, while one (<a href="/wiki/Raniero_Cantalamessa" title="Raniero Cantalamessa">Cantalamessa</a>) was granted a papal dispensation from it.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Year_of_Mercy">Year of Mercy</span></h3>
<div class="thumb tleft"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:192px;"><a href="/wiki/File:A_Szent%C3%A9v_kapuj%C3%A1nak_megnyit%C3%A1sa_2015_-_Opening_of_the_Holy_Door_2015_4.jpeg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/03/A_Szent%C3%A9v_kapuj%C3%A1nak_megnyit%C3%A1sa_2015_-_Opening_of_the_Holy_Door_2015_4.jpeg/190px-A_Szent%C3%A9v_kapuj%C3%A1nak_megnyit%C3%A1sa_2015_-_Opening_of_the_Holy_Door_2015_4.jpeg" decoding="async" width="190" height="192" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/03/A_Szent%C3%A9v_kapuj%C3%A1nak_megnyit%C3%A1sa_2015_-_Opening_of_the_Holy_Door_2015_4.jpeg/285px-A_Szent%C3%A9v_kapuj%C3%A1nak_megnyit%C3%A1sa_2015_-_Opening_of_the_Holy_Door_2015_4.jpeg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/03/A_Szent%C3%A9v_kapuj%C3%A1nak_megnyit%C3%A1sa_2015_-_Opening_of_the_Holy_Door_2015_4.jpeg/380px-A_Szent%C3%A9v_kapuj%C3%A1nak_megnyit%C3%A1sa_2015_-_Opening_of_the_Holy_Door_2015_4.jpeg 2x" data-file-width="431" data-file-height="435" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:A_Szent%C3%A9v_kapuj%C3%A1nak_megnyit%C3%A1sa_2015_-_Opening_of_the_Holy_Door_2015_4.jpeg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>Francis opens the <a href="/wiki/Holy_door" title="Holy door">Holy Door</a>, marking the beginning of the <a href="/wiki/Extraordinary_Jubilee_of_Mercy" title="Extraordinary Jubilee of Mercy">Extraordinary Jubilee of Mercy</a>.</div></div></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Extraordinary_Jubilee_of_Mercy" title="Extraordinary Jubilee of Mercy">Extraordinary Jubilee of Mercy</a></div>
<p>With his April 2015 <a href="/wiki/Papal_bull" title="Papal bull">papal bull</a> of indiction, <i>Misericordiae Vultus</i> (<a href="/wiki/Latin" title="Latin">Latin</a>: "The Face of <a href="/wiki/Mercy" title="Mercy">Mercy</a>"), Francis inaugurated a Special <a href="/wiki/Jubilee_(Christianity)" class="mw-redirect" title="Jubilee (Christianity)">Jubilee Year</a> of Mercy, to run from 8 December 2015, <a href="/wiki/Solemnity" title="Solemnity">Solemnity</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Immaculate_Conception" title="Immaculate Conception">Immaculate Conception</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Blessed_Virgin_Mary" class="mw-redirect" title="Blessed Virgin Mary">Blessed Virgin Mary</a>, to the last Sunday before <a href="/wiki/Advent" title="Advent">Advent</a> and the Solemnity of the <a href="/wiki/Feast_of_Christ_the_King" title="Feast of Christ the King">Feast of Christ the King</a> of the Universe on 20 November 2016.
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Holy_Door" class="mw-redirect" title="Holy Door">Holy Doors</a> of the major basilicas of Rome (including the Great Door of St. Peter's) were opened, and special "Doors of Mercy" were opened at cathedrals and other major churches around the world, where the faithful can earn indulgences by fulfilling the usual conditions of prayer for the pope's intentions, confession, and detachment from sin, and communion.<sup id="cite_ref-opening_269-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-opening-269">&#91;265&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-270" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-270">&#91;266&#93;</a></sup> During Lent of that year, special 24-hour penance services will be celebrated, and during the year, special qualified and experienced priests called "Missionaries of Mercy" will be available in every diocese to forgive even severe, special-case sins normally reserved to the Holy See's <a href="/wiki/Apostolic_Penitentiary" title="Apostolic Penitentiary">Apostolic Penitentiary</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Misericordiae_271-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Misericordiae-271">&#91;267&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-time_272-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-time-272">&#91;268&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Francis established the <a href="/wiki/World_Day_of_the_Poor" title="World Day of the Poor">World Day of the Poor</a> in his Apostolic Letter, <i>Misericordia et Misera</i>, issued on 20 November 2016 to celebrate the end of the Extraordinary Jubilee of Mercy.<sup id="cite_ref-273" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-273">&#91;269&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-274" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-274">&#91;270&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="COVID-19_pandemic">COVID-19 pandemic</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Vatican_City" title="COVID-19 pandemic in Vatican City">COVID-19 pandemic in Vatican City</a></div>
<p>During the <a href="/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic" title="COVID-19 pandemic">COVID-19 pandemic</a>, Francis canceled his regular <a href="/wiki/Papal_audience" class="mw-redirect" title="Papal audience">general audiences</a> at <a href="/wiki/St._Peter%27s_Square" title="St. Peter&#39;s Square">St. Peter's Square</a> to prevent crowds from gathering and spreading the virus, which <a href="/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Italy" title="COVID-19 pandemic in Italy">seriously affected Italy</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-275" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-275">&#91;271&#93;</a></sup> He encouraged priests to visit patients and health workers;<sup id="cite_ref-276" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-276">&#91;272&#93;</a></sup> urged the faithful not to forget the poor during the time of crisis;<sup id="cite_ref-277" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-277">&#91;273&#93;</a></sup> offered prayers for people with  the virus in China;<sup id="cite_ref-278" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-278">&#91;274&#93;</a></sup> and invoked the Blessed Virgin Mary under her title <a href="/wiki/Salus_Populi_Romani" title="Salus Populi Romani">Salus Populi Romani</a>, as the <a href="/wiki/Diocese_of_Rome" title="Diocese of Rome">Diocese of Rome</a> observed a period of prayer and fasting in recognition of the victims.<sup id="cite_ref-279" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-279">&#91;275&#93;</a></sup> The pontiff reacted with displeasure on 13 March 2020, at the news that the Vicar General had closed all churches in the Diocese of Rome. Despite <a href="/wiki/2020_Italy_coronavirus_lockdown" class="mw-redirect" title="2020 Italy coronavirus lockdown">Italy being under a quarantine lockdown</a>, Francis pleaded "not to leave the ... people alone" and worked to partially reverse the closures.
</p><p>On 20 March 2020, Francis asked the <a href="/wiki/Dicastery_for_Promoting_Integral_Human_Development" title="Dicastery for Promoting Integral Human Development">Dicastery for Promoting Integral Human Development (DPIHD)</a> to create a <a href="/wiki/Vatican_COVID-19_Commission" title="Vatican COVID-19 Commission">Vatican COVID-19 Commission</a> to express the church's concern for the crisis generated by the COVID-19 pandemic, and propose responses to the potential socio-economic challenges deriving from it.<sup id="cite_ref-280" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-280">&#91;276&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-281" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-281">&#91;277&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>On 27 March, Francis gave an extraordinary benediction <i><a href="/wiki/Urbi_et_Orbi" title="Urbi et Orbi">Urbi et Orbi</a></i>.<sup id="cite_ref-282" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-282">&#91;278&#93;</a></sup> In his homily on <a href="/wiki/Calming_the_storm" title="Calming the storm">calming the storm</a> in the <a href="/wiki/Gospel_of_Mark" title="Gospel of Mark">Gospel of Mark</a>, Francis described the setting: "Dense darkness has thickened on our squares, streets and cities; it looks over our lives filling everything with a deafening silence and a desolate void that paralyzes everything in its passage: you can feel it in the air, you can feel it in your gestures. ...In the face of suffering, where the true development of our peoples is measured, we discover and experience the priestly prayer of Jesus: 'may all be one'."<sup id="cite_ref-283" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-283">&#91;279&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Francis maintains getting <a href="/wiki/COVID_vaccination" class="mw-redirect" title="COVID vaccination">COVID vaccination</a> is a moral obligation. Francis stated that people had a responsibility to look after themselves, "and this translates into respect for the health of those around us. Health care is a moral obligation", he stated.<sup id="cite_ref-284" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-284">&#91;280&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In response to the <a href="/wiki/Economic_impact_of_the_COVID-19_pandemic" title="Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic">economic harm</a> created by the COVID-19 pandemic, Francis stated that now is the time to consider implementing a <a href="/wiki/Universal_basic_income" title="Universal basic income">universal basic wage</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-285" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-285">&#91;281&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Russo-Ukrainian_War">Russo-Ukrainian War</span></h3>
<p>Following the <a href="/wiki/2022_Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine" title="2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine">February 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine</a> and escalation of the <a href="/wiki/Russo-Ukrainian_War" title="Russo-Ukrainian War">Russo-Ukrainian War</a>, Francis visited the Russian embassy in Rome in what was described as an "unprecedented move."<sup id="cite_ref-286" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-286">&#91;282&#93;</a></sup> Francis called Ukrainian president <a href="/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy" title="Volodymyr Zelenskyy">Volodymyr Zelenskyy</a>, stating his "sorrow" as the Vatican worked to find "room for negotiation."<sup id="cite_ref-287" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-287">&#91;283&#93;</a></sup> As the invasion began, the <a href="/wiki/Major_archbishop" title="Major archbishop">major archbishop</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Ukrainian_Greek_Catholic_Church" title="Ukrainian Greek Catholic Church">Ukrainian Greek Catholic Church</a> <a href="/wiki/Sviatoslav_Shevchuk" title="Sviatoslav Shevchuk">Sviatoslav Shevchuk</a> cancelled a trip to visit Francis in Florence.<sup id="cite_ref-288" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-288">&#91;284&#93;</a></sup> On 25 February, the day after the invasion began, Francis would assure Shevchuk via a phone call that "he would do everything he can to help end the Ukraine conflict."<sup id="cite_ref-289" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-289">&#91;285&#93;</a></sup> During the 27 February Angelus address, Francis called for peace, saying, "Silence the weapons!"<sup id="cite_ref-290" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-290">&#91;286&#93;</a></sup> Francis also sent two high-ranking cardinals with aid to Ukraine at the beginning of March.<sup id="cite_ref-291" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-291">&#91;287&#93;</a></sup> These special envoys were the papal almsgiver, Cardinal <a href="/wiki/Konrad_Krajewski" title="Konrad Krajewski">Konrad Krajewski</a>, and Cardinal <a href="/wiki/Michael_Czerny" title="Michael Czerny">Michael Czerny</a>, who is head of the papal office that deals with migration, charity, justice and peace. This mission, which involved several trips,<sup id="cite_ref-292" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-292">&#91;288&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-293" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-293">&#91;289&#93;</a></sup> was considered a highly unusual move of Vatican diplomacy.<sup id="cite_ref-294" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-294">&#91;290&#93;</a></sup> Pope Francis consecrated both Russia and Ukraine on 25 March 2022 (see <a href="/wiki/Consecration_of_Russia" class="mw-redirect" title="Consecration of Russia">consecration of Russia</a>).<sup id="cite_ref-295" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-295">&#91;291&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In mid-May 2022, Francis described Russia's invasion of Ukraine as "perhaps somehow either provoked or not prevented[.]”<sup id="cite_ref-296" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-296">&#91;292&#93;</a></sup> Francis explained that this observation did not mean he was "pro-Putin": "“It would be simplistic and wrong to say such a thing. I am simply against reducing complexity to the distinction between good guys and bad guys, without reasoning about roots and interests, which are very complex.”<sup id="cite_ref-297" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-297">&#91;293&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>On 24 August 2022, Pope Francis described the killing of <a href="/wiki/Darya_Dugina" title="Darya Dugina">Darya Dugina</a> as a case of innocents paying for the <a href="/wiki/Russo-Ukrainian_War" title="Russo-Ukrainian War">Russo-Ukrainian War</a>. On the same day, the Ukraine's envoy to the <a href="/wiki/Holy_See" title="Holy See">Holy See</a> protested against such a description of the killing, saying that Dugina was "one of ideologists of (Russian) imperialism" and therefore not an innocent victim.<sup id="cite_ref-298" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-298">&#91;294&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In September 2022, Francis pointed out that Ukraine has a lawful right to defend itself, and that dialogue with the aggressor is necessary even when it stinks and later said that Ukrainians were noble people who were victims of savageness, monstrosities and torture.<sup id="cite_ref-299" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-299">&#91;295&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-300" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-300">&#91;296&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>On 2 October 2022, Francis directly addressed Putin and Zelenskyy, making an impassioned appeal to Putin to halt the "spiral of violence and death", saying that <a href="/wiki/Nuclear_threats_during_the_2022_Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine" title="Nuclear threats during the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine">a nuclear escalation</a> would bring "uncontrollable global consequences". Addressing Ukrainian president Zelenskyy, Pope Francis asked him to be open about "serious peace proposals" at the same time that Francis recognized that Ukraine had suffered an "aggression" and that he "pained about the suffering of the Ukrainian people".<sup id="cite_ref-301" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-301">&#91;297&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In November 2022, Francis granted an interview to Christian magazine <a href="/wiki/America_(magazine)" title="America (magazine)"><i>America</i></a>. During the interview, Francis stated that generally, the <a href="/wiki/Chechens" title="Chechens">Chechens</a> and <a href="/wiki/Buryats" title="Buryats">Buryats</a> minorities were "perhaps the cruellest of Russia [but] not of Russian tradition". These remarks were strongly condemned by Russia's foreign ministry spokesperson <a href="/wiki/Maria_Zakharova" title="Maria Zakharova">Maria Zakharova</a>, who expressed that the comments were "no longer <a href="/wiki/Russophobia" class="mw-redirect" title="Russophobia">Russophobia</a>, [they] are a perversion on a level I can’t even name". Others remarked that his statement was "racist".<sup id="cite_ref-302" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-302">&#91;298&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Role_of_women">Role of women</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Women_in_the_Catholic_Church" title="Women in the Catholic Church">Women in the Catholic Church</a></div>
<p>On 11 January 2021, Francis <a href="/wiki/Spiritus_Domini_(Pope_Francis)" title="Spiritus Domini (Pope Francis)">allowed</a> bishops to institute women to the ministries of <a href="/wiki/Acolyte" title="Acolyte">acolyte</a> and <a href="/wiki/Reader_(liturgy)" title="Reader (liturgy)">lector</a>. While these instituted ministries were previously reserved to men, Catholic women already carry out these duties without institution in most of the world. Francis wrote that these <a href="/wiki/Christian_ministry" title="Christian ministry">ministries</a> are fundamentally distinct from those reserved to <a href="/wiki/Holy_orders_in_the_Catholic_Church" title="Holy orders in the Catholic Church">ordained clergy</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-303" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-303">&#91;299&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:15_304-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:15-304">&#91;300&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-305" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-305">&#91;301&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In February 2021, Francis announced back-to-back appointments of women to take positions that were only held by men in the past. He appointed <a href="/wiki/France" title="France">France</a>'s member of the <a href="/wiki/Congregation_of_Xavi%C3%A8res" title="Congregation of Xavières">Xaviere Missionary Sisters</a>, <a href="/wiki/Nathalie_Becquart" title="Nathalie Becquart">Nathalie Becquart</a> as the first co-undersecretary of the <a href="/wiki/Synod_of_Bishops_in_the_Catholic_Church" title="Synod of Bishops in the Catholic Church">Synod of Bishops</a>. Besides, an Italian magistrate, Catia Summaria also became the first woman Promoter of Justice in the Vatican's Court of Appeals.<sup id="cite_ref-306" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-306">&#91;302&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Financial_corruption">Financial corruption</span></h3>
<p>Francis was mandated by electing cardinals to sort out Vatican finances following scandals during the papacies of Pope Benedict and Pope John Paul II. He stated he is determined to end corruption in the Catholic Church but is not very optimistic due to it being a human problem dating back centuries.<sup id="cite_ref-307" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-307">&#91;303&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Canadian_indigenous_residential_schools">Canadian indigenous residential schools</span></h3>
<p>On 24 July 2022, Francis began an apostolic journey to <a href="/wiki/Catholic_Church_in_Canada" title="Catholic Church in Canada">Canada</a>, expressing his sorrow, indignation, and shame over the church's abuse of <a href="/wiki/Indigenous_peoples_in_Canada" title="Indigenous peoples in Canada">Canadian indigenous</a> children in <a href="/wiki/Canadian_Indian_residential_school_system" title="Canadian Indian residential school system">residential schools</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-:14_308-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:14-308">&#91;304&#93;</a></sup> He apologized for the church's role in "projects of cultural destruction" and forced <a href="/wiki/Cultural_assimilation_of_indigenous_peoples" class="mw-redirect" title="Cultural assimilation of indigenous peoples">assimilation</a> which culminated in the abusive system of residential schools.<sup id="cite_ref-:14_308-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:14-308">&#91;304&#93;</a></sup> Francis promised a serious investigation into the history of abuse.<sup id="cite_ref-:14_308-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:14-308">&#91;304&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Theological_emphases">Theological emphases</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Theology_of_Pope_Francis" title="Theology of Pope Francis">Theology of Pope Francis</a></div>
<p>In <i>Evangelii gaudium</i> Francis revealed what would be the emphases of his pontificate: a missionary impulse among all Catholics, sharing the faith more actively, avoiding worldliness and more visibly living the gospel of God's mercy, and helping the poor and working for <a href="/wiki/Catholic_social_teaching" title="Catholic social teaching">social justice</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-309" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-309">&#91;305&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Evangelization">Evangelization</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Theology_of_Pope_Francis#The_Church&#39;s_mission" title="Theology of Pope Francis">Theology of Pope Francis §&#160;The Church's mission</a></div>
<p>From his first major letter <i><a href="/wiki/Evangelii_gaudium" title="Evangelii gaudium">Evangelii gaudium</a></i> (<i>Joy to the World</i>), Francis called for "a missionary and pastoral conversion" whereby the laity would fully share in the missionary task of the church.<sup id="cite_ref-ReferenceB_213-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ReferenceB-213">&#91;209&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-310" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-310">&#91;306&#93;</a></sup> Then in his letter on the call of all to the same holiness, <i><a href="/wiki/Gaudete_et_exsultate" title="Gaudete et exsultate">Gaudete et exsultate</a></i>, Francis describes holiness as "an impulse to evangelize and to leave a mark in this world".<sup id="cite_ref-311" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-311">&#91;307&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Church_governance"><span class="anchor" id="Ordination_of_women"></span><span class="anchor" id="Clergy"></span>Church governance</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Theology_of_Pope_Francis#Church_governance" title="Theology of Pope Francis">Theology of Pope Francis §&#160;Church governance</a></div>
