<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:261px;"><a href="/wiki/File:D%C3%BCsseldorf_Rosenmontag_2014_IMG_1350_(12915484354).jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5e/D%C3%BCsseldorf_Rosenmontag_2014_IMG_1350_%2812915484354%29.jpg/259px-D%C3%BCsseldorf_Rosenmontag_2014_IMG_1350_%2812915484354%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="259" height="173" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5e/D%C3%BCsseldorf_Rosenmontag_2014_IMG_1350_%2812915484354%29.jpg/389px-D%C3%BCsseldorf_Rosenmontag_2014_IMG_1350_%2812915484354%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5e/D%C3%BCsseldorf_Rosenmontag_2014_IMG_1350_%2812915484354%29.jpg/518px-D%C3%BCsseldorf_Rosenmontag_2014_IMG_1350_%2812915484354%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2592" data-file-height="1728" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:D%C3%BCsseldorf_Rosenmontag_2014_IMG_1350_(12915484354).jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>A Carnival float of Francis and Germany's prelate <a href="/wiki/Franz-Peter_Tebartz-van_Elst" title="Franz-Peter Tebartz-van Elst">Franz-Peter Tebartz-van Elst</a>, Düsseldorf, 2014</div></div></div><p>Francis called for decentralization of governance away from Rome, and for a synodal manner of decision making in dialogue with the people.<sup id="cite_ref-312" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-312">&#91;308&#93;</a></sup> He strongly opposed <a href="/wiki/Theology_of_Pope_Francis#Clericalism" title="Theology of Pope Francis">clericalism</a><sup id="cite_ref-313" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-313">&#91;309&#93;</a></sup> and made <a href="/wiki/Theology_of_Pope_Francis#Important_role_of_women" title="Theology of Pope Francis">women</a> full members of the church's dicasteries in Rome.<sup id="cite_ref-314" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-314">&#91;310&#93;</a></sup>
</p><h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Environment">Environment</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Theology_of_Pope_Francis#Environmentalism" title="Theology of Pope Francis">Theology of Pope Francis §&#160;Environmentalism</a></div><p>Francis's naming of himself after <a href="/wiki/Francis_of_Assisi" title="Francis of Assisi">Francis of Assisi</a> was an early indication of how he shared Francis's care for all of creation. This was followed in May 2015 with his major <a href="/wiki/Encyclical" title="Encyclical">encyclical</a> on the environment, <i><a href="/wiki/Laudato_si%27" title="Laudato si&#39;">Laudato si'</a></i> (<i>Praise be to you</i>).<sup id="cite_ref-315" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-315">&#91;311&#93;</a></sup>
</p><h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Option_for_the_poor"><span class="anchor" id="Poverty"></span><span class="anchor" id="Liberation_theology"></span>Option for the poor</span></h3>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Pope_Francis_at_Vargihna.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a1/Pope_Francis_at_Vargihna.jpg/220px-Pope_Francis_at_Vargihna.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="146" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a1/Pope_Francis_at_Vargihna.jpg/330px-Pope_Francis_at_Vargihna.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a1/Pope_Francis_at_Vargihna.jpg/440px-Pope_Francis_at_Vargihna.jpg 2x" data-file-width="800" data-file-height="532" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Pope_Francis_at_Vargihna.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>Francis visits a <a href="/wiki/Favela" title="Favela">favela</a> in Brazil during <a href="/wiki/World_Youth_Day_2013" title="World Youth Day 2013">World Youth Day 2013</a>.</div></div></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Theology_of_Pope_Francis#Option_for_the_poor" title="Theology of Pope Francis">Theology of Pope Francis §&#160;Option for the poor</a>, <a href="/wiki/Theology_of_Pope_Francis#Capitalism" title="Theology of Pope Francis">Theology of Pope Francis §&#160;Capitalism</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Theology_of_Pope_Francis#Liberation_Theology" title="Theology of Pope Francis">Theology of Pope Francis §&#160;Liberation Theology</a></div>
<p>Francis has highly extolled "popular movements", which demonstrate the "strength of us", serve as a remedy to the "culture of the self", and are based on solidarity with the poor and the common good.<sup id="cite_ref-316" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-316">&#91;312&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Morality"><span class="anchor" id="Abortion"></span><span class="anchor" id="Contraception_and_family_planning"></span><span class="anchor" id="Capital_punishment_and_life_imprisonment"></span>Morality</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Theology_of_Pope_Francis#Morality_as_a_vehicle_of_God&#39;s_mercy" title="Theology of Pope Francis">Theology of Pope Francis §&#160;Morality as a vehicle of God's mercy</a>, <a href="/wiki/Theology_of_Pope_Francis#Sexual_morality_as_Good_News" title="Theology of Pope Francis">Theology of Pope Francis §&#160;Sexual morality as Good News</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Pope_Francis_and_LGBT_topics" title="Pope Francis and LGBT topics">Pope Francis and LGBT topics</a></div><p>Cardinal <a href="/wiki/Walter_Kasper" title="Walter Kasper">Walter Kasper</a> has called mercy "the key word of his pontificate."<sup id="cite_ref-:02_317-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:02-317">&#91;313&#93;</a></sup><sup class="reference nowrap"><span title="Page / location: 31–32">&#58;&#8202;31–32&#8202;</span></sup> His papal motto <i>Miserando atque eligendo</i> ("by having mercy and by choosing") contains a central theme of his papacy, God's mercy,<sup id="cite_ref-web.archive.org2_318-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-web.archive.org2-318">&#91;314&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-319" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-319">&#91;315&#93;</a></sup> While maintaining the Catholic Church's traditional teaching against abortion, Francis, has referred to the "obsession" of some Catholics with a few issues like "abortion, gay marriage and the use of contraceptive methods" which "do not show the heart of the message of Jesus Christ."<sup id="cite_ref-320" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-320">&#91;316&#93;</a></sup>
</p><h3><span class="mw-headline" id="LGBT">LGBT</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Pope_Francis_and_LGBT_topics" title="Pope Francis and LGBT topics">Pope Francis and LGBT topics</a></div>
<p>In June 2013, Francis suggested that "if a person is gay and seeks God and has good will, who am I to judge?"<sup id="cite_ref-321" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-321">&#91;317&#93;</a></sup> Later, in 2015, he declared that "the family is threatened by growing efforts on the part of some to redefine the very institution of marriage."<sup id="cite_ref-:12_322-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:12-322">&#91;318&#93;</a></sup> He has also suggested that same-sex marriage "disfigures God's plan for creation."<sup id="cite_ref-:12_322-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:12-322">&#91;318&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Francis endorsed the <a href="/wiki/2015_Slovak_same-sex_marriage_referendum" title="2015 Slovak same-sex marriage referendum">2015 Slovak same-sex marriage referendum</a> which would have banned same-sex marriage and same-sex adoptions in the country.<sup id="cite_ref-323" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-323">&#91;319&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-apbigstoryfeb_324-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-apbigstoryfeb-324">&#91;320&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-325" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-325">&#91;321&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>
He stated that he supports <a href="/wiki/Civil_union" title="Civil union">legally recognising same-sex civil unions</a> in a statement from an interview published in October 2020;<sup id="cite_ref-:5_326-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:5-326">&#91;322&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:8_327-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:8-327">&#91;323&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:9_328-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:9-328">&#91;324&#93;</a></sup> this passage was from an interview from 2019, but this passage had been cut from public releases at the time.<sup id="cite_ref-329" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-329">&#91;325&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-330" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-330">&#91;326&#93;</a></sup> The statement was also interpreted as supportive of <a href="/wiki/LGBT_adoption" class="mw-redirect" title="LGBT adoption">LGBT adoption</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-:9_328-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:9-328">&#91;324&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:10_331-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:10-331">&#91;327&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-332" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-332">&#91;328&#93;</a></sup><style data-mw-deduplicate="TemplateStyles:r996844942">.mw-parser-output .templatequote{overflow:hidden;margin:1em 0;padding:0 40px}.mw-parser-output .templatequote .templatequotecite{line-height:1.5em;text-align:left;padding-left:1.6em;margin-top:0}</style></p><blockquote class="templatequote"><p>What we have to create is a <a href="/wiki/Civil_union" title="Civil union">civil union</a> law. That way they are legally covered. They're children of God and have a right to a family. Nobody should be thrown out or be made miserable because of it.
</p></blockquote>
<p>However, Vatican later clarified that his comments were taken out of context with two comments to two different questions at different times spliced together in a very misleading way.<sup id="cite_ref-auto_333-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-auto-333">&#91;329&#93;</a></sup> Francis has never officially pronounced support for gay civil unions.<sup id="cite_ref-auto_333-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-auto-333">&#91;329&#93;</a></sup> 
</p><p>In January 2022, Francis said during a weekly audience that parents of gay children should offer support to their children instead of condemning them.<sup id="cite_ref-334" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-334">&#91;330&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In an interview with <a href="/wiki/Associated_Press" title="Associated Press">Associated Press</a>, Pope Francis said laws that criminalized homosexuality were unjust and that Catholic bishops should welcome LGBTQ people into the church rather than marginalize them, stating "we are all children of God".<sup id="cite_ref-335" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-335">&#91;331&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Religious_persecution">Religious persecution</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Further information: <a href="/wiki/Persecution_of_Christians_by_ISIL" class="mw-redirect" title="Persecution of Christians by ISIL">Persecution of Christians by ISIL</a></div>
<p>Francis supported the use of force to stop Islamic militants from attacking religious minorities in Iraq.<sup id="cite_ref-336" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-336">&#91;332&#93;</a></sup> In January 2018, Francis met with a group of <a href="/wiki/Yazidi_people" class="mw-redirect" title="Yazidi people">Yazidi</a> refugees in Europe and expressed his support for their right to freely profess their own faith without limitations. In the meeting, he also urged the international community "not to remain a silent and unresponsive spectator in the face of [your] tragedy."<sup id="cite_ref-337" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-337">&#91;333&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Controversies">Controversies</span></h2>
<p>Since 2016, criticism against Francis by theological conservatives has intensified.<sup id="cite_ref-:0_338-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:0-338">&#91;334&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:1_339-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:1-339">&#91;335&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:2_340-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:2-340">&#91;336&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:3_341-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:3-341">&#91;337&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:4_342-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:4-342">&#91;338&#93;</a></sup> One commentator has described the conservative resistance against Francis as "unique in its visibility" in recent church history.<sup id="cite_ref-343" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-343">&#91;339&#93;</a></sup> Some have explained the level of disagreement as due to his going beyond theoretical principles to pastoral discernment.<sup id="cite_ref-344" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-344">&#91;340&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Sexual_abuse_response">Sexual abuse response</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Catholic_Church_sexual_abuse_cases" title="Catholic Church sexual abuse cases">Catholic Church sexual abuse cases</a></div>
<p>As cardinal, in 2010 Bergoglio commissioned a study which concluded that Father <a href="/wiki/Julio_C%C3%A9sar_Grassi" title="Julio César Grassi">Julio César Grassi</a>, a priest convicted of child sexual abuse, was innocent, that his victims were lying, and that the case against him never should have gone to trial.<sup id="cite_ref-study_345-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-study-345">&#91;341&#93;</a></sup> Despite the study, the <a href="/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_Argentina" title="Supreme Court of Argentina">Supreme Court of Argentina</a> upheld the conviction and 15-year prison sentence against Grassi in March 2017.<sup id="cite_ref-study_345-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-study-345">&#91;341&#93;</a></sup> Francis has admitted that the church "arrived late" in dealing with sexual abuse cases.<sup id="cite_ref-346" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-346">&#91;342&#93;</a></sup> During his papacy, a number of abuse survivors have expressed disappointment in Francis's response to sex abuse in the church,<sup id="cite_ref-347" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-347">&#91;343&#93;</a></sup> while others have praised him for his actions.<sup id="cite_ref-348" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-348">&#91;344&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In 2015, Francis was criticized for supporting Chilean bishop <a href="/wiki/Juan_Barros" class="mw-redirect" title="Juan Barros">Juan Barros</a>, who was accused of covering up sex crimes committed against minors.<sup id="cite_ref-349" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-349">&#91;345&#93;</a></sup> In 2018, Francis acknowledged he had made "grave errors" in judgment about Barros, apologized to the victims and launched a Vatican investigation that resulted in the resignation of Barros and two other Chilean bishops.<sup id="cite_ref-350" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-350">&#91;346&#93;</a></sup> In 2018, Archbishop <a href="/wiki/Carlo_Maria_Vigan%C3%B2" title="Carlo Maria Viganò">Carlo Maria Viganò</a> published an open letter denouncing Francis's handling of sexual abuse allegations against <a href="/wiki/Theodore_McCarrick" title="Theodore McCarrick">Theodore McCarrick</a>, accusing him of knowing about allegations that McCarrick had committed sexual abuse and failing to take action. Viganò called on the Pope to resign.<sup id="cite_ref-351" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-351">&#91;347&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In November 2021, Francis thanked journalists for their work uncovering child sexual abuse scandals in the church, thanking journalist also for "helping us not to sweep it under the carpet, and for the voice you have given to the abuse victims."<sup id="cite_ref-352" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-352">&#91;348&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In November 2022, French Cardinal <a href="/wiki/Jean-Pierre_Ricard" title="Jean-Pierre Ricard">Jean-Pierre Ricard</a> admitted to having sexually abused a 14-year-old girl in the 1980s in <a href="/wiki/Marseille" title="Marseille">Marseille</a>. Ricard, who was named as Cardinal by Francis, said that he committed "reprehensible" acts with the girl while he was a priest. French authorities opened an investigation into the case while Francis commented that now that "everything is clearer [...] more cases like this shouldn't surprise [anyone]", and added condemnation for sexual abuse as "against priestly nature, and also against social nature".<sup id="cite_ref-353" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-353">&#91;349&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-354" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-354">&#91;350&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Theological_disagreements">Theological disagreements</span></h3>
<h4><span class="mw-headline" id="Amoris_laetitia_and_the_communion_to_the_divorced_and_civilly_remarried"><i>Amoris laetitia</i> and the communion to the divorced and civilly remarried</span></h4>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Amoris_laetitia" title="Amoris laetitia">Amoris laetitia</a></div>
<p>On a theological level, controversy arose after the publication of the apostolic exhortation <i><a href="/wiki/Amoris_laetitia" title="Amoris laetitia">Amoris laetitia</a></i>, especially regarding whether the exhortation had changed the <a href="/wiki/Catholic_Church" title="Catholic Church">Catholic Church</a>'s sacramental discipline concerning access to the <a href="/wiki/Sacrament_of_Penance" title="Sacrament of Penance">sacraments of Penance</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Eucharist_in_the_Catholic_Church" title="Eucharist in the Catholic Church">Eucharist</a> for divorced couples who have <a href="/wiki/Civil_marriage" title="Civil marriage">civilly remarried</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Oullet_355-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Oullet-355">&#91;351&#93;</a></sup> Francis had written that "It is important that the divorced who have entered a new union should be made to feel part of the Church." He called not for "a new set of general rules, canonical in nature and applicable to all cases," but "a responsible personal and pastoral discernment of particular cases." He went on to say: "It is true that general rules set forth a good which can never be disregarded or neglected, but in their formulation they cannot provide absolutely for all particular situations."<sup id="cite_ref-Carroll_356-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Carroll-356">&#91;352&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Four cardinals (<a href="/wiki/Raymond_Leo_Burke" title="Raymond Leo Burke">Raymond Leo Burke</a>, <a href="/wiki/Carlo_Caffarra" title="Carlo Caffarra">Carlo Caffarra</a>, <a href="/wiki/Walter_Brandm%C3%BCller" title="Walter Brandmüller">Walter Brandmüller</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Joachim_Meisner" title="Joachim Meisner">Joachim Meisner</a>) formally asked Francis for clarifications, particularly on the issue of giving communion to divorced and civilly remarried Catholics.<sup id="cite_ref-357" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-357">&#91;353&#93;</a></sup> They submitted five "dubia" (doubts), and requested a yes or no answer. Francis has not publicly replied.<sup id="cite_ref-358" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-358">&#91;354&#93;</a></sup> The exhortation has been implemented in different ways by various bishops around the world.<sup id="cite_ref-359" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-359">&#91;355&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Cardinal <a href="/wiki/Gerhard_Ludwig_M%C3%BCller" title="Gerhard Ludwig Müller">Gerhard Müller</a>, former prefect of the <a href="/wiki/Congregation_for_the_Doctrine_of_the_Faith" class="mw-redirect" title="Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith">Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith</a>, maintained that <i>Amoris Laetitia</i> should only be interpreted in line with previous doctrine. Therefore, according to Cardinal Müller, divorced and civilly remarried can have access to the Sacraments of Reconciliation and the Eucharist only if they take on the duty of living in complete continence.<sup id="cite_ref-360" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-360">&#91;356&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-361" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-361">&#91;357&#93;</a></sup> Francis subsequently announced that <a href="/wiki/Dicastery" title="Dicastery">dicastery</a> prefects would be appointed for a single five-year term, and replaced Müller at the end of his term in 2017 with <a href="/wiki/Luis_Ladaria_Ferrer" title="Luis Ladaria Ferrer">Luis Ladaria Ferrer</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-362" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-362">&#91;358&#93;</a></sup> Cardinal <a href="/wiki/Carlo_Caffarra" title="Carlo Caffarra">Carlo Caffarra</a>, one of the authors of the dubia, maintains that after <i>Amoris laetitia</i> "only a blind man could deny there's great confusion, uncertainty and insecurity in the Church."<sup id="cite_ref-363" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-363">&#91;359&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In July 2017 a group of conservative clergy, academics and laymen signed a document labeled as a "<a href="/wiki/Correctio_filialis_de_haeresibus_propagatis" title="Correctio filialis de haeresibus propagatis">Filial Correction</a>" of Francis.<sup id="cite_ref-cnn_364-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-cnn-364">&#91;360&#93;</a></sup> The 25-page document, which was made public in September after it received no reply, criticized the pope for promoting what it described as seven heretical propositions through various words, actions and omissions during his pontificate.<sup id="cite_ref-Correctio_filialis_de_haeresibus_propagatis_365-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Correctio_filialis_de_haeresibus_propagatis-365">&#91;361&#93;</a></sup> Capuchin Father <a href="/wiki/Thomas_Weinandy" title="Thomas Weinandy">Thomas Weinandy</a>, ex-doctrine chief of US Bishops, wrote a letter to Francis on 31 July 2017, which he subsequently made public, in which he charged that Francis is fostering "chronic confusion", "demeaning" the importance of doctrine, appointing bishops who "scandalize" believers with dubious "teaching and pastoral practice", giving prelates who object the impression they will be "marginalized or worse" if they speak out, and causing faithful Catholics to "lose confidence in their supreme shepherd".<sup id="cite_ref-366" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-366">&#91;362&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>A defense of <i>Amoris Laetitia</i> came from philosopher Rocco Butiglione who accused its critics of "ethical objectivism." He said that the critics cannot deny that "there are mitigating circumstances in which a mortal sin (a sin that would otherwise be mortal) becomes a lighter sin, a venial sin. There are therefore some cases in which remarried divorcees can (through their confessor and after an adequate spiritual discernment) be considered in God's grace and therefore deserving of receiving the sacraments."<sup id="cite_ref-367" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-367">&#91;363&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h4><span class="mw-headline" id="Document_on_Human_Fraternity">Document on Human Fraternity</span></h4>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Document_on_Human_Fraternity" title="Document on Human Fraternity">Document on Human Fraternity</a></div>
<p>The <i><a href="/wiki/Document_on_Human_Fraternity" title="Document on Human Fraternity">Document on Human Fraternity</a> for World Peace and Living Together</i> is a joint statement signed by Francis and <a href="/wiki/Sheikh" title="Sheikh">Sheikh</a> <a href="/wiki/Ahmed_el-Tayeb" title="Ahmed el-Tayeb">Ahmed el-Tayeb</a>, <a href="/wiki/Grand_Imam_of_Al-Azhar" class="mw-redirect" title="Grand Imam of Al-Azhar">Grand Imam of Al-Azhar</a>, on 4 February 2019 in <a href="/wiki/Abu_Dhabi" title="Abu Dhabi">Abu Dhabi</a>, <a href="/wiki/United_Arab_Emirates" title="United Arab Emirates">United Arab Emirates</a>. This joint statement is concerned with how different faiths can live peaceably in the same world and areas and later inspired the <a href="/wiki/International_Day_of_Human_Fraternity" title="International Day of Human Fraternity">International Day of Human Fraternity</a>, as acknowledged by the UN Secretary-General, <a href="/wiki/Ant%C3%B3nio_Guterres" title="António Guterres">António Guterres</a>, in different occasions.<sup id="cite_ref-first-ever_368-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-first-ever-368">&#91;364&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-369" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-369">&#91;365&#93;</a></sup> Criticisms focused particularly on the passage about God's will with regard to the diversity of religions, claiming that the "pluralism and the diversity of religions, colour, sex, race and language are willed by God in His wisdom, through which He created human beings".<sup id="cite_ref-370" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-370">&#91;366&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:6_371-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:6-371">&#91;367&#93;</a></sup> Catholic theologian Chad Pecknold wrote that this sentence was "puzzling, and potentially problematic".<sup id="cite_ref-:7_372-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:7-372">&#91;368&#93;</a></sup> Some Catholic observers tried to understand it as an allusion to the "permissive will" of God, allowing evil on earth.<sup id="cite_ref-:6_371-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:6-371">&#91;367&#93;</a></sup> Pecknold wrote that the diversity of religions might also be "evidence of our natural desire to know God".<sup id="cite_ref-:7_372-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:7-372">&#91;368&#93;</a></sup> Pope Francis clarified to Bishop <a href="/wiki/Athanasius_Schneider" title="Athanasius Schneider">Athanasius Schneider</a>, as per Bp Schneider, that the Pope was referring to "the permissive will of God."<sup id="cite_ref-373" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-373">&#91;369&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h4><span class="mw-headline" id="Traditionis_custodes_and_the_restriction_of_the_Tridentine_Mass"><i>Traditionis custodes</i> and the restriction of the Tridentine Mass</span></h4>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Traditionis_custodes" title="Traditionis custodes">Traditionis custodes</a></div>
<p>In July 2021, Francis issued, <i><a href="/wiki/Motu_proprio" title="Motu proprio">motu proprio</a></i>, the <a href="/wiki/Apostolic_letter" class="mw-redirect" title="Apostolic letter">apostolic letter</a> titled <i><a href="/wiki/Traditionis_custodes" title="Traditionis custodes">Traditionis custodes</a></i>, which reversed the decision of his immediate predecessor Benedict XVI in <i><a href="/wiki/Summorum_Pontificum" title="Summorum Pontificum">Summorum Pontificum</a></i> and imposed new restrictions on the use of the <a href="/wiki/Tridentine_Mass" title="Tridentine Mass">Traditional Latin Mass</a>. The letter returned to the bishops the power to grant or suppress the Latin Mass in their particular dioceses, and requires newly ordained priests to first request permission before performing the old rite, among other changes.<sup id="cite_ref-374" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-374">&#91;370&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-375" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-375">&#91;371&#93;</a></sup> <i>Traditionis Custodes</i>, which Pope Francis published and came into immediate effect on July 16, has been criticized by prelates such as Cardinals <a href="/wiki/Raymond_Leo_Burke" title="Raymond Leo Burke">Raymond Burke</a>, <a href="/wiki/Gerhard_Ludwig_M%C3%BCller" title="Gerhard Ludwig Müller">Gerhard Müller</a> and <a href="/wiki/Joseph_Zen" title="Joseph Zen">Joseph Zen</a>, as well as many lay faithful who attend the traditional Latin Mass, also called Extraordinary Form of the <a href="/wiki/Roman_Rite" title="Roman Rite">Roman Rite</a>. The most general criticism is that the restrictions are unnecessary, needlessly harsh, and implemented in an unjustifiably swift fashion."<sup id="cite_ref-376" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-376">&#91;372&#93;</a></sup> The <i>motu proprio</i> was later confirmed by Francis through the <a href="/wiki/Apostolic_Letter" class="mw-redirect" title="Apostolic Letter">apostolic letter</a> <i>Desiderio desideravi</i>.<sup id="cite_ref-377" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-377">&#91;373&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="International_policy">International policy</span></h3>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:172px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Raul-castro-papa-francisco.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/58/Raul-castro-papa-francisco.jpg/170px-Raul-castro-papa-francisco.jpg" decoding="async" width="170" height="192" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/58/Raul-castro-papa-francisco.jpg/255px-Raul-castro-papa-francisco.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/58/Raul-castro-papa-francisco.jpg/340px-Raul-castro-papa-francisco.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2178" data-file-height="2457" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Raul-castro-papa-francisco.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>Francis with <a href="/wiki/Cuba" title="Cuba">Cuban</a> leader <a href="/wiki/Ra%C3%BAl_Castro" title="Raúl Castro">Raúl Castro</a> in September 2015</div></div></div>
<p>Francis has regularly been accused by conservatives of having a "soft spot" for leftist populist movements.<sup id="cite_ref-378" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-378">&#91;374&#93;</a></sup> After Francis's visit to <a href="/wiki/Cuba" title="Cuba">Cuba</a> in 2015, Catholic Yale historian <a href="/wiki/Carlos_Eire" title="Carlos Eire">Carlos Eire</a> said Francis had a "<a href="/wiki/Option_for_the_poor" title="Option for the poor">preferential option</a> for the oppressors" in Cuba.<sup id="cite_ref-379" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-379">&#91;375&#93;</a></sup> Nevertheless, Francis remained hostile to <a href="/wiki/Right-wing_populism" title="Right-wing populism">right-wing populism</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-380" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-380">&#91;376&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Francis has supported the Vatican-China agreement, intended to normalize the situation of <a href="/wiki/Catholic_Church_in_China" title="Catholic Church in China">China's Catholics</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-381" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-381">&#91;377&#93;</a></sup> which was criticized by Cardinal <a href="/wiki/Joseph_Zen" title="Joseph Zen">Joseph Zen</a> as a step towards the "annihilation" of the Catholic Church in China.<sup id="cite_ref-382" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-382">&#91;378&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-383" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-383">&#91;379&#93;</a></sup> U.S. Secretary of State <a href="/wiki/Mike_Pompeo" title="Mike Pompeo">Mike Pompeo</a> said cooperating with the <a href="/wiki/Chinese_Communist_Party" title="Chinese Communist Party">Chinese Communist Party</a> puts the pope's moral authority at risk.<sup id="cite_ref-384" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-384">&#91;380&#93;</a></sup> In September 2020, Pompeo urged Francis to stand against <a href="/wiki/Human_rights_in_China" title="Human rights in China">China's human rights violations</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-385" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-385">&#91;381&#93;</a></sup> In November, Francis named China's <a href="/wiki/Uyghurs" title="Uyghurs">Uyghur</a> minority among a list of the world's persecuted peoples. He wrote: "I think often of persecuted peoples: the <a href="/wiki/Rohingya_people" title="Rohingya people">Rohingya</a> [Muslims in Myanmar], the poor Uighurs, the Yazidi—what ISIS did to them was truly cruel—or Christians in Egypt and Pakistan killed by bombs that went off while they prayed in church." <a href="/wiki/Zhao_Lijian" title="Zhao Lijian">Zhao Lijian</a>, the spokesman of the Foreign Ministry of China, said Francis's remarks had "no factual basis at all".<sup id="cite_ref-386" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-386">&#91;382&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<div class="thumb tleft"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Donald_Trump_Pope_Francis_Melania_Trump_in_2017.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/21/Donald_Trump_Pope_Francis_Melania_Trump_in_2017.jpg/220px-Donald_Trump_Pope_Francis_Melania_Trump_in_2017.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/21/Donald_Trump_Pope_Francis_Melania_Trump_in_2017.jpg/330px-Donald_Trump_Pope_Francis_Melania_Trump_in_2017.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/21/Donald_Trump_Pope_Francis_Melania_Trump_in_2017.jpg/440px-Donald_Trump_Pope_Francis_Melania_Trump_in_2017.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1200" data-file-height="800" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Donald_Trump_Pope_Francis_Melania_Trump_in_2017.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>Francis with U.S. President Donald Trump and First Lady <a href="/wiki/Melania_Trump" title="Melania Trump">Melania</a> in 2017</div></div></div>
<p>Since 2016, Francis has also been contrasted with US President <a href="/wiki/Donald_Trump" title="Donald Trump">Donald Trump</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-387" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-387">&#91;383&#93;</a></sup> elected that year, with some conservative critics drawing comparisons between the two.<sup id="cite_ref-388" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-388">&#91;384&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-389" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-389">&#91;385&#93;</a></sup> During the <a href="/wiki/2016_United_States_presidential_election" title="2016 United States presidential election">2016 United States presidential election</a>, Francis said of Trump, "A person who only thinks about building walls, wherever they may be, and not building bridges, is not Christian. That is not the gospel." Trump responded, "For a religious leader to question a person's faith is disgraceful."<sup id="cite_ref-390" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-390">&#91;386&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Federico_Lombardi" title="Federico Lombardi">Federico Lombardi</a> said that Francis's comments were not "a personal attack, nor an indication of who to vote for".<sup id="cite_ref-391" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-391">&#91;387&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In response to criticism from <a href="/wiki/Episcopal_Conference_of_Venezuela" title="Episcopal Conference of Venezuela">Venezuela's bishops</a>, President <a href="/wiki/Nicol%C3%A1s_Maduro" title="Nicolás Maduro">Nicolás Maduro</a> said in 2017 that he had the support of Francis.<sup id="cite_ref-392" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-392">&#91;388&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-393" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-393">&#91;389&#93;</a></sup> Francis met with the country's bishops in June 2017, and the Venezuelan bishops' conference president stated, "There is no distance between the episcopal conference and the Holy See."<sup id="cite_ref-394" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-394">&#91;390&#93;</a></sup> In January 2019, 20 former presidents in Latin America wrote a letter to Francis criticizing his Christmas address regarding the ongoing <a href="/wiki/Crisis_in_Venezuela" title="Crisis in Venezuela">Venezuelan crisis</a> for being too simplistic and for not acknowledging what they believed to be the causes of the suffering of the victims of the crisis.<sup id="cite_ref-395" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-395">&#91;391&#93;</a></sup> Francis has sought peace in the crisis without picking a side.<sup id="cite_ref-396" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-396">&#91;392&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In 2019, during the <a href="/wiki/2019%E2%80%932020_Hong_Kong_protests" title="2019–2020 Hong Kong protests">Hong Kong protests</a>, Francis was criticized by Catholic clergy in Hong Kong, with Cardinal <a href="/wiki/Joseph_Zen" title="Joseph Zen">Joseph Zen</a> criticizing him for not taking a stand against China and instead being quoted as saying "I would like to go to China. I love China". Francis compared the protests in Hong Kong to those seen <a href="/wiki/2019%E2%80%932021_Chilean_protests" class="mw-redirect" title="2019–2021 Chilean protests">in Chile</a> and in France.<sup id="cite_ref-397" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-397">&#91;393&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="International_diplomatic_role">International diplomatic role</span></h2>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Pope_Francis_Travels.svg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0d/Pope_Francis_Travels.svg/220px-Pope_Francis_Travels.svg.png" decoding="async" width="220" height="113" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0d/Pope_Francis_Travels.svg/330px-Pope_Francis_Travels.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0d/Pope_Francis_Travels.svg/440px-Pope_Francis_Travels.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="1151" data-file-height="591" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Pope_Francis_Travels.svg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>Map indicating <a href="/wiki/List_of_pastoral_visits_of_Pope_Francis_outside_Italy" class="mw-redirect" title="List of pastoral visits of Pope Francis outside Italy">countries visited by Francis as pope</a></div></div></div>
<p>Francis played a key role in the talks toward restoring <a href="/wiki/Cuban_Thaw" class="mw-redirect" title="Cuban Thaw">full diplomatic relations between the U.S. and Cuba</a>. The restoration was jointly announced by U.S. President <a href="/wiki/Barack_Obama" title="Barack Obama">Barack Obama</a> and Cuban President <a href="/wiki/Ra%C3%BAl_Castro" title="Raúl Castro">Raúl Castro</a> on 17 December 2014. The headline in the <i><a href="/wiki/Los_Angeles_Times" title="Los Angeles Times">Los Angeles Times</a></i> on 19 December was "Bridge to Cuba via Vatican," with the further lead "In a rare and crucial role, Francis helped keep U.S. talks with Havana on track and guided final deal."<sup id="cite_ref-Bridge_to_Cuba_398-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Bridge_to_Cuba-398">&#91;394&#93;</a></sup> The pope, along with the <a href="/wiki/Government_of_Canada" title="Government of Canada">Government of Canada</a>, was a behind-the-scenes broker of the agreement, taking the role following President Obama's request during his visit to the pope in March 2014.<sup id="cite_ref-399" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-399">&#91;395&#93;</a></sup> The success of the negotiations was credited to Francis because "as a religious leader with the confidence of both sides, he was able to convince the Obama and Castro administrations that the other side would live up to the deal".<sup id="cite_ref-Bridge_to_Cuba_398-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Bridge_to_Cuba-398">&#91;394&#93;</a></sup> En route to the United States for a visit in September 2015, the pope stopped in Cuba. "The plan comes amid a breakthrough for which Francis has received much credit."<sup id="cite_ref-Wilkinson,_Pope_will_visit_Cuba._400-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Wilkinson,_Pope_will_visit_Cuba.-400">&#91;396&#93;</a></sup> The Cuba visit "seals that accomplishment, in which he served as a bridge between two erstwhile enemies".<sup id="cite_ref-Wilkinson,_Pope_will_visit_Cuba._400-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Wilkinson,_Pope_will_visit_Cuba.-400">&#91;396&#93;</a></sup> According to one expert on religion in Latin America, Mario Paredes, the pope's visit to Cuba was consistent with his aim to promote an understanding of the role of the Cuban Revolution and that of the Catholic Church. When Francis was archbishop of Buenos Aires, he authored a text entitled "Dialogues Between John Paul II and Fidel Castro".<sup id="cite_ref-Wilkinson,_Pope_will_visit_Cuba._400-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Wilkinson,_Pope_will_visit_Cuba.-400">&#91;396&#93;</a></sup> John Paul was the first pope to visit Cuba. In May 2015, Francis met with Cuban leader Raúl Castro. After the meeting in <a href="/wiki/Vatican_City" title="Vatican City">Vatican City</a> on 10 May 2015, Castro said that he was considering returning to the <a href="/wiki/Catholic_Church" title="Catholic Church">Catholic Church</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Catholic_Cuba_401-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Catholic_Cuba-401">&#91;397&#93;</a></sup> He said in a televised news conference, "I read all the speeches of the pope, his commentaries, and if the pope continues this way, I will go back to praying and go back to the [Catholic] church. I am not joking."<sup id="cite_ref-NYT11MAY2015A4_402-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-NYT11MAY2015A4-402">&#91;398&#93;</a></sup> Castro said that, when the pope came, "I promise to go to all his Masses and with satisfaction".<sup id="cite_ref-NYT11MAY2015A4_402-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-NYT11MAY2015A4-402">&#91;398&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:President_Barack_Obama_with_Pope_Francis_at_the_Vatican,_March_27,_2014.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/23/President_Barack_Obama_with_Pope_Francis_at_the_Vatican%2C_March_27%2C_2014.jpg/220px-President_Barack_Obama_with_Pope_Francis_at_the_Vatican%2C_March_27%2C_2014.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/23/President_Barack_Obama_with_Pope_Francis_at_the_Vatican%2C_March_27%2C_2014.jpg/330px-President_Barack_Obama_with_Pope_Francis_at_the_Vatican%2C_March_27%2C_2014.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/23/President_Barack_Obama_with_Pope_Francis_at_the_Vatican%2C_March_27%2C_2014.jpg/440px-President_Barack_Obama_with_Pope_Francis_at_the_Vatican%2C_March_27%2C_2014.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1500" data-file-height="1000" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:President_Barack_Obama_with_Pope_Francis_at_the_Vatican,_March_27,_2014.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>Francis with U.S. President <a href="/wiki/Barack_Obama" title="Barack Obama">Barack Obama</a>, 27 March 2014</div></div></div>
<p>In May 2014, his visit to the <a href="/wiki/State_of_Israel" class="mw-redirect" title="State of Israel">State of Israel</a>, where he delivered 13 speeches, was heavily publicized.<sup id="cite_ref-403" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-403">&#91;399&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Protests_Against_Pope_Francis_Visit_to_Israel_2014" class="mw-redirect" title="Protests Against Pope Francis Visit to Israel 2014">Protests against his visit</a> resulted in an alleged arson attempt at the <a href="/wiki/Dormition_Abbey" class="mw-redirect" title="Dormition Abbey">Dormition Abbey</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-404" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-404">&#91;400&#93;</a></sup> The cave under the <a href="/wiki/Church_of_the_Nativity" title="Church of the Nativity">Church of the Nativity</a> caught fire the night after his visit.<sup id="cite_ref-405" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-405">&#91;401&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>
In May 2015, Francis welcomed Palestinian president <a href="/wiki/Mahmoud_Abbas" title="Mahmoud Abbas">Mahmoud Abbas</a> to the Vatican. Several media outlets reported that Francis praised Abbas as "an angel of peace", though his actual words were the following: "The angel of peace destroys the evil spirit of war. I thought about you: may you be an angel of peace."<sup id="cite_ref-406" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-406">&#91;402&#93;</a></sup> The Vatican signed a treaty recognizing the <a href="/wiki/State_of_Palestine" title="State of Palestine">state of Palestine</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-407" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-407">&#91;403&#93;</a></sup> The Vatican issued statements concerning the hope that the peace talks could resume between Israel and Palestine. Abbas' visit was on the occasion of the canonization of two Palestinian nuns.<sup id="cite_ref-408" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-408">&#91;404&#93;</a></sup> </p><div class="thumb tleft"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Vladimir_Putin_with_Franciscus_(2015-06-10)_1.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a9/Vladimir_Putin_with_Franciscus_%282015-06-10%29_1.jpg/220px-Vladimir_Putin_with_Franciscus_%282015-06-10%29_1.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="136" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a9/Vladimir_Putin_with_Franciscus_%282015-06-10%29_1.jpg/330px-Vladimir_Putin_with_Franciscus_%282015-06-10%29_1.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a9/Vladimir_Putin_with_Franciscus_%282015-06-10%29_1.jpg/440px-Vladimir_Putin_with_Franciscus_%282015-06-10%29_1.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1880" data-file-height="1160" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Vladimir_Putin_with_Franciscus_(2015-06-10)_1.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>Francis shaking hands with Russian Foreign Minister <a href="/wiki/Sergey_Lavrov" title="Sergey Lavrov">Sergey Lavrov</a>, in front of Russian President <a href="/wiki/Vladimir_Putin" title="Vladimir Putin">Vladimir Putin</a>, 10 June 2015</div></div></div>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Pope_Francis_in_Sarajevo_06_(cropped).JPG" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/98/Pope_Francis_in_Sarajevo_06_%28cropped%29.JPG/220px-Pope_Francis_in_Sarajevo_06_%28cropped%29.JPG" decoding="async" width="220" height="137" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/98/Pope_Francis_in_Sarajevo_06_%28cropped%29.JPG/330px-Pope_Francis_in_Sarajevo_06_%28cropped%29.JPG 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/98/Pope_Francis_in_Sarajevo_06_%28cropped%29.JPG/440px-Pope_Francis_in_Sarajevo_06_%28cropped%29.JPG 2x" data-file-width="4000" data-file-height="2494" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Pope_Francis_in_Sarajevo_06_(cropped).JPG" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>Crowd at the <a href="/wiki/Ko%C5%A1evo_City_Stadium" title="Koševo City Stadium">Koševo City Stadium</a> in <a href="/wiki/Sarajevo" title="Sarajevo">Sarajevo</a>, celebrating a mass with Francis, June 2015</div></div></div>
<p>On 6 June 2015, Francis visited <a href="/wiki/Sarajevo" title="Sarajevo">Sarajevo</a>, the capital city of <a href="/wiki/Bosnia_and_Herzegovina" title="Bosnia and Herzegovina">Bosnia and Herzegovina</a>. He urged peace during his time in the religiously diverse city, known as the "Jerusalem of Europe".<sup id="cite_ref-409" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-409">&#91;405&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>On 25 September 2015, Francis addressed the United Nations in New York City.<sup id="cite_ref-Times_2015_410-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Times_2015-410">&#91;406&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>On 16 April 2016, he visited, together with <a href="/wiki/Bartholomew_I_of_Constantinople" title="Bartholomew I of Constantinople">Ecumenical Patriarch Bartholomew</a> and <a href="/wiki/Ieronymos_II_of_Athens" title="Ieronymos II of Athens">Archbishop Ieronimos II of Athens</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Moria_Refugee_Camp" class="mw-redirect" title="Moria Refugee Camp">Moria Refugee Camp</a> on the Greek island of <a href="/wiki/Lesbos" title="Lesbos">Lesbos</a>, to call the attention of the world to the refugee issue. There the three Christian leaders signed a joint declaration.<sup id="cite_ref-411" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-411">&#91;407&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In January 2017, Francis demanded the resignation of <a href="/wiki/Matthew_Festing" title="Matthew Festing">Matthew Festing</a>, the 79th <a href="/wiki/List_of_Princes_and_Grand_Masters_of_the_Sovereign_Military_Order_of_Malta" class="mw-redirect" title="List of Princes and Grand Masters of the Sovereign Military Order of Malta">Prince and Grand Master</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Sovereign_Military_Order_of_Malta" title="Sovereign Military Order of Malta">Sovereign Military Order of Malta</a>. The Pope's demand came as a response to Festing and Cardinal <a href="/wiki/Raymond_Leo_Burke" title="Raymond Leo Burke">Raymond Leo Burke</a> firing Baron <a href="/wiki/Albrecht_von_Boeselager" title="Albrecht von Boeselager">Albrecht von Boeselager</a> from his position in the Order of Malta. The Order, in May 2017, appointed a new leader in the person of Fra' Giacomo Dalla Torre del Tempio di Sanguinetto.<sup id="cite_ref-412" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-412">&#91;408&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>
On 24 May 2017, Francis met with U.S. President <a href="/wiki/Donald_Trump" title="Donald Trump">Donald Trump</a> in Vatican City, where they discussed the contributions of <a href="/wiki/Catholic_Church_in_the_United_States" title="Catholic Church in the United States">Catholics</a> to the United States and to the world. They discussed issues of mutual concern, including how religious communities can combat human suffering in crisis regions, such as <a href="/wiki/Syria" title="Syria">Syria</a>, <a href="/wiki/Libya" title="Libya">Libya</a>, and <a href="/wiki/ISIS" class="mw-redirect" title="ISIS">ISIS</a>-controlled territory. They also discussed <a href="/wiki/Terrorism" title="Terrorism">terrorism</a> and the radicalization of young people. The <a href="/wiki/Cardinal_Secretary_of_State" title="Cardinal Secretary of State">Vatican's secretary of state</a>, <a href="/wiki/Pietro_Parolin" title="Pietro Parolin">Pietro Parolin</a>, raised the issue of <a href="/wiki/Climate_change" title="Climate change">climate change</a> and encouraged Trump to remain in the <a href="/wiki/Paris_Agreement" title="Paris Agreement">Paris Agreement</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-413" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-413">&#91;409&#93;</a></sup> At the 2017 <a href="/wiki/World_Food_Day" title="World Food Day">World Food Day</a> ceremony, Francis reiterated that "we see the consequences [of climate change] every day" and that we "know how the problems are to be faced ... [t]hanks to scientific knowledge." He said that "the international community has drawn up the necessary legal instruments, such as the Paris Agreement, from which however some are withdrawing. There is a re-emergence of the nonchalance towards the delicate balances of ecosystems, the presumption of being able to manipulate and control the planet's limited resources, and greed for profit."<sup id="cite_ref-Vatican_FAO_20171016_414-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Vatican_FAO_20171016-414">&#91;410&#93;</a></sup> </p><div class="thumb tleft"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Wizyta_w_Watykanie_(42556254741).jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/52/Wizyta_w_Watykanie_%2842556254741%29.jpg/220px-Wizyta_w_Watykanie_%2842556254741%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/52/Wizyta_w_Watykanie_%2842556254741%29.jpg/330px-Wizyta_w_Watykanie_%2842556254741%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/52/Wizyta_w_Watykanie_%2842556254741%29.jpg/440px-Wizyta_w_Watykanie_%2842556254741%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1000" data-file-height="667" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Wizyta_w_Watykanie_(42556254741).jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>Francis with Polish Prime Minister <a href="/wiki/Mateusz_Morawiecki" title="Mateusz Morawiecki">Mateusz Morawiecki</a> and his family, Vatican City, June 2018</div></div></div>
<p>Francis <a href="/wiki/Pope_Francis%27s_visit_to_Ireland" class="mw-redirect" title="Pope Francis&#39;s visit to Ireland">visited Ireland in 2018</a>, in what was the first papal tour of the country since John Paul II's historic trip in 1979.<sup id="cite_ref-415" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-415">&#91;411&#93;</a></sup> While in Ireland he apologized for abuses by clergy in the United States and Ireland.<sup id="cite_ref-416" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-416">&#91;412&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Pope_Francis_visit_Bethlehem.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c0/Pope_Francis_visit_Bethlehem.jpg/220px-Pope_Francis_visit_Bethlehem.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c0/Pope_Francis_visit_Bethlehem.jpg/330px-Pope_Francis_visit_Bethlehem.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c0/Pope_Francis_visit_Bethlehem.jpg/440px-Pope_Francis_visit_Bethlehem.jpg 2x" data-file-width="5472" data-file-height="3648" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Pope_Francis_visit_Bethlehem.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>Francis in <a href="/wiki/Bethlehem" title="Bethlehem">Bethlehem</a>, <a href="/wiki/State_of_Palestine" title="State of Palestine">Palestine</a>, 25 May 2014</div></div></div>
<p>In February 2019, Francis visited <a href="/wiki/Abu_Dhabi" title="Abu Dhabi">Abu Dhabi</a>, <a href="/wiki/United_Arab_Emirates" title="United Arab Emirates">United Arab Emirates</a>, on the invitation of <a href="/wiki/Mohammed_bin_Zayed_Al_Nahyan" class="mw-redirect" title="Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan">Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan</a>. Francis became the first pope to hold a papal Mass on the Arabian Peninsula, with more than 120,000 attendees in the <a href="/wiki/Zayed_Sports_City_Stadium" title="Zayed Sports City Stadium">Zayed Sports City Stadium</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-417" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-417">&#91;413&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Francis made the plight of refugees and migrants "a core component of his pastoral work", and has defended their rights in <a href="/wiki/Theology_of_Pope_Francis#Refugees_and_migrants" title="Theology of Pope Francis">dialogue both with Europe and with the United States</a>. He went on to place a statue in <a href="/wiki/St._Peter%27s_Square" title="St. Peter&#39;s Square">St. Peter's Square</a> to bring attention to the Christian imperative involved in their situation (Hebrews 13:2).<sup id="cite_ref-418" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-418">&#91;414&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-419" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-419">&#91;415&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-420" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-420">&#91;416&#93;</a></sup> In line with this policy, Francis has criticised <a href="/wiki/Neo-nationalism" title="Neo-nationalism">neo-nationalists</a> and <a href="/wiki/Populism" title="Populism">populists</a> who reject the acceptance of refugees.<sup id="cite_ref-421" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-421">&#91;417&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-422" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-422">&#91;418&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In March 2021, Pope Francis held a <a href="/wiki/Pope_Francis%27s_visit_to_Iraq" class="mw-redirect" title="Pope Francis&#39;s visit to Iraq">historic meeting</a> with <a href="/wiki/Iraq" title="Iraq">Iraq</a>'s top <a href="/wiki/Shi%27ite" class="mw-redirect" title="Shi&#39;ite">Shi'ite</a> cleric, <a href="/wiki/Grand_Ayatollah_Ali_al-Sistani" class="mw-redirect" title="Grand Ayatollah Ali al-Sistani">Grand Ayatollah Ali al-Sistani</a>, and visited the birthplace of the <a href="/wiki/Abraham_in_Islam" title="Abraham in Islam">Prophet Abraham</a>, Ur. Giving a message of peaceful coexistence, he and the Iraqi cleric urged the <a href="/wiki/Islam" title="Islam">Muslim</a> and <a href="/wiki/Christianity" title="Christianity">Christian</a> communities to work together in unity for peace.<sup id="cite_ref-423" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-423">&#91;419&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-424" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-424">&#91;420&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>On 9 May 2021, Francis called for peace between <a href="/wiki/Israel" title="Israel">Israel</a> and Palestinians and an end to <a href="/wiki/2021_Israel%E2%80%93Palestine_crisis" title="2021 Israel–Palestine crisis">clashes in Jerusalem</a> during his <a href="/wiki/Regina_caeli" title="Regina caeli">Regina caeli</a> address.<sup id="cite_ref-425" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-425">&#91;421&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-426" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-426">&#91;422&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Following the <a href="/wiki/2021_Taliban_offensive" title="2021 Taliban offensive">Taliban takeover of Afghanistan and withdrawal of U.S. forces from the country</a>, Francis said that the withdrawal of troops was "legitimate" but said that the process of evacuations was "not thought through" and criticized the war for having failed at nation-building. He also stated that the Vatican is in talks with the Taliban through Cardinal <a href="/wiki/Pietro_Parolin" title="Pietro Parolin">Pietro Parolin</a> to discourage the Taliban on taking reprisal measures against civilians.<sup id="cite_ref-427" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-427">&#91;423&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-428" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-428">&#91;424&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>On 1 September 2021, Francis publicly defended the dialogue with <a href="/wiki/China" title="China">China</a> on the appointment of new bishops. Francis stated that uneasy dialogue was better than no dialogue at all, and emphasized in improving strained ties with the Chinese government.<sup id="cite_ref-429" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-429">&#91;425&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>On <a href="/wiki/All_Souls%27_Day" title="All Souls&#39; Day">All Souls' Day</a>, on 1 November 2021, Francis visited a war cemetery in Rome and paid tribute to fallen soldiers during the <a href="/wiki/Battle_of_Anzio" title="Battle of Anzio">Battle of Anzio</a> in World War II as well as at the <a href="/wiki/Piave_River" class="mw-redirect" title="Piave River">Piave River</a>, in Italy, during World War I. Francis also praised military casualties for "fighting for their homeland and values." and called for global peace.<sup id="cite_ref-430" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-430">&#91;426&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-431" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-431">&#91;427&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>On 16 April 2022, <a href="/wiki/Ivan_Fedorov_(politician)" title="Ivan Fedorov (politician)">Ivan Fedorov</a> attended Easter services in the Vatican with the Pope. <a href="/wiki/Maria_Mezentseva" title="Maria Mezentseva">Maria Mezentseva</a>, Olena Khomenko, and Rusem Umerov were also in attendance.
</p><p>Pope Francis said: "In this darkness of war, in the cruelty, we are all praying for you and with you this night. We are praying for all the suffering. We can only give you our company", our prayer, further stating "the biggest thing you can receive "Christ is risen," He said "Christ is risen" in Ukrainian."<sup id="cite_ref-432" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-432">&#91;428&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>On 25 July 2022, at the Powwow ceremonial grounds on the Cree Nation reservation in Edmonton, Canada, the Pope expressed "deep sorrow" at the Cemetery. "I humbly beg forgiveness for the evil committed by so many Christians against the Indigenous peoples", Francis said.<sup id="cite_ref-433" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-433">&#91;429&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Four chiefs escorted the pontiff to the site near the former Ermineskin Indian Residential School, and presented him with a feathered headdress after he spoke, making him an honorary leader of the community.<sup id="cite_ref-434" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-434">&#91;430&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Public_image">Public image</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/List_of_places_and_things_named_after_Pope_Francis" title="List of places and things named after Pope Francis">List of places and things named after Pope Francis</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1066479718"/><table class="infobox" style="width: 210px; float: right; clear: right; margin:0 0 1.5em 1.5em"><tbody><tr><th colspan="2" class="infobox-above" style="font-size:115%">External video</th></tr><tr><td colspan="2" class="infobox-image"><a href="/wiki/File:Pope_Francis_(27056871831)_(cropped).jpg" class="image"><img alt="Pope Francis (27056871831) (cropped).jpg" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ee/Pope_Francis_%2827056871831%29_%28cropped%29.jpg/210px-Pope_Francis_%2827056871831%29_%28cropped%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="210" height="293" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ee/Pope_Francis_%2827056871831%29_%28cropped%29.jpg/315px-Pope_Francis_%2827056871831%29_%28cropped%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/ee/Pope_Francis_%2827056871831%29_%28cropped%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="393" data-file-height="549" /></a></td></tr><tr><td colspan="2" class="infobox-full-data" style="text-align: left"><img alt="video icon" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg/16px-Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg.png" decoding="async" width="16" height="16" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg/24px-Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg/32px-Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="128" data-file-height="128" /> <a rel="nofollow" class="external text" href="https://www.ted.com/talks/pope_francis_why_the_only_future_worth_building_includes_everyone?language=en#t-62701">Why the only future worth building includes everyone</a>, <a href="/wiki/TED_(conference)" title="TED (conference)">TED talks</a>, April 2017, 17:51, in Italian with subtitles in 22 languages</td></tr></tbody></table>
<p>Popular <a href="/wiki/Mainstream_media" title="Mainstream media">mainstream media</a> frequently portray Francis either as a <a href="/wiki/Progressivism" title="Progressivism">progressive</a> papal reformer or with <a href="/wiki/Social_liberalism" title="Social liberalism">liberal</a>, moderate values.<sup id="cite_ref-435" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-435">&#91;431&#93;</a></sup> The Vatican has claimed that Western news outlets often seek to portray his message with a less-doctrinal tone of papacy, in hopes of extrapolating his words to convey a more merciful and tolerant message.<sup id="cite_ref-Achanging_436-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Achanging-436">&#91;432&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-437" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-437">&#91;433&#93;</a></sup> In the news media, both faithful and non-believers often refer to a "honeymoon" phase in which the pope has changed the tone on Catholic doctrines and supposedly initiated <a href="/wiki/Ecclesiastical" title="Ecclesiastical">ecclesiastical</a> reform in the Vatican.<sup id="cite_ref-438" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-438">&#91;434&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-439" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-439">&#91;435&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-440" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-440">&#91;436&#93;</a></sup> Media systems differ, too, not only in their coverage of Francis's stances but also in how individual events are portrayed. His 2015 trip to Cuba is a prime example. During this trip, American-based AP and British-based Reuters highlighted the religious aspect of the pope's journey while Prensa Latina, the official state media agency, depicted it as a diplomatic visit. American and British media were also more likely during this trip to show Francis interacting with regular Cubans compared to the official Cuban media, which showed Francis interacting with elites most often.<sup id="cite_ref-441" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-441">&#91;437&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In December 2013, both <i><a href="/wiki/Time_Magazine" class="mw-redirect" title="Time Magazine">Time</a></i> and <i><a href="/wiki/The_Advocate_(LGBT_magazine)" class="mw-redirect" title="The Advocate (LGBT magazine)">The Advocate</a></i> magazines named the Pontiff as their "Person of the Year" in praise and hopes of reforming the <a href="/wiki/Roman_Curia" title="Roman Curia">Roman Curia</a> while hoping to change the Catholic Church's doctrine on various controversial issues. In addition, <i>Esquire</i> magazine named him as the "Best-dressed man" for 2013 for his simpler vestments often in tune with a modern simplistic design on sartorial fashion.<sup id="cite_ref-442" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-442">&#91;438&#93;</a></sup> <i><a href="/wiki/Rolling_Stone" title="Rolling Stone">Rolling Stone</a></i> magazine followed in January 2014 by making the Pontiff their featured front cover.<sup id="cite_ref-443" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-443">&#91;439&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-444" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-444">&#91;440&#93;</a></sup> <i><a href="/wiki/Fortune_(magazine)" title="Fortune (magazine)">Fortune</a></i> magazine also ranked Francis as number one in their list of 50 greatest leaders.<sup id="cite_ref-445" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-445">&#91;441&#93;</a></sup> On 5 November 2014, he was ranked by <i><a href="/wiki/Forbes" title="Forbes">Forbes</a></i> as the fourth <a href="/wiki/Forbes_list_of_The_World%27s_Most_Powerful_People" class="mw-redirect" title="Forbes list of The World&#39;s Most Powerful People">most powerful person in the world</a> and was the only non-political figure in the top ranking.<sup id="cite_ref-446" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-446">&#91;442&#93;</a></sup> In December 2016, Francis again made <i>Forbes</i><span class="nowrap" style="padding-left:0.1em;">&#39;</span>s list of "The World's Most Powerful People", ranking fifth.<sup id="cite_ref-447" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-447">&#91;443&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In March 2013, a new song was dedicated to Francis and released in Brazilian Portuguese, European Portuguese, and Italian, titled <i>Come Puoi</i> ("How You Can").<sup id="cite_ref-nofrills_137-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-nofrills-137">&#91;134&#93;</a></sup> Also in March, Pablo Buera, the mayor of <a href="/wiki/La_Plata" title="La Plata">La Plata</a>, Argentina, announced that the city had renamed a section of a street leading up to a local cathedral <i>Papa Francisco</i>.<sup id="cite_ref-street_448-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-street-448">&#91;444&#93;</a></sup> There are already efforts to name other streets after him, as well as a school where he studied as a child.<sup id="cite_ref-street_448-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-street-448">&#91;444&#93;</a></sup> A proposal to create a commemorative coin as a tribute to Francis was made in Argentina's lower house on 28 November 2013. On the coins it would read, "Tribute from the Argentine People to Pope Francis." beneath his face.<sup id="cite_ref-449" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-449">&#91;445&#93;</a></sup> As of May 2013, sales of papal souvenirs, a sign of popularity, were up.<sup id="cite_ref-NYT52513_450-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-NYT52513-450">&#91;446&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Francis presided over his first joint public wedding ceremony in a Nuptial Mass for 20 couples from the Archdiocese of Rome on 14 September 2014, just a few weeks before the start of the 5–19 October Extraordinary <a href="/wiki/Synod_of_Bishops_(Catholic)" class="mw-redirect" title="Synod of Bishops (Catholic)">Synod of Bishops</a> on the Family.<sup id="cite_ref-451" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-451">&#91;447&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-453" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-453">&#91;e&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>On 19 March 2016, Francis became the first pope to create an <a href="/wiki/Instagram" title="Instagram">Instagram</a> account.<sup id="cite_ref-454" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-454">&#91;449&#93;</a></sup> He broke records after having gained over one million followers in under twelve hours of the account being up.<sup id="cite_ref-455" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-455">&#91;450&#93;</a></sup> In 2019 Francis held a conference on the World Day of Social Communications highlighting the pros and cons of social media and urging users to use it as a source that liberates rather than enslaves.<sup id="cite_ref-456" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-456">&#91;451&#93;</a></sup> On 26 November 2020 Francis became the first pope to write an op-ed for <i>The New York Times</i>, addressing issues such as the coronavirus and the need for global solidarity.<sup id="cite_ref-457" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-457">&#91;452&#93;</a></sup> The Pontiff also used his op-ed to strongly critique those protesting COVID-19 restrictions.<sup id="cite_ref-458" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-458">&#91;453&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In August 2021, rumors of a possible resignation arose due to health issues,<sup id="cite_ref-459" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-459">&#91;454&#93;</a></sup> but he dismissed those rumors in early September 2021, saying that he is "living a normal life."<sup id="cite_ref-460" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-460">&#91;455&#93;</a></sup> In June 2022, the Pope's health was an issue again when he had to cancel his trips to the Democratic Republic of the Congo and South Sudan. The Vatican said that the decision was at the request of the doctors treating his knee, in order to not jeopardize the results of the therapy.<sup id="cite_ref-461" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-461">&#91;456&#93;</a></sup> In an interview with <a href="/wiki/Reuters" title="Reuters">Reuters</a> in July 2022, Francis denied rumours about his resignation, saying "[it] never entered my mind. For the moment no, for the moment, no. Really!", but said that he would resign if his health made it impossible for him to run the church.<sup id="cite_ref-462" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-462">&#91;457&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Distinctions">Distinctions</span></h2>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Titles_and_styles">Titles and styles</span></h3>
<p>The official form of address of the pope in English is <i>His Holiness Pope Francis</i>; in Latin, <i>Franciscus, Episcopus Romae</i>. <i>Holy Father</i> is among the other <a href="/wiki/His_holiness#Catholic_church" class="mw-redirect" title="His holiness">honorifics</a> used for popes.<sup id="cite_ref-463" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-463">&#91;458&#93;</a></sup>
</p>

<li><a href="/wiki/Ennio_Morricone" title="Ennio Morricone">Ennio Morricone</a> composed a Mass setting (<i>Missa Papae Francisci</i>) named after the pope, for the occasion of the 200th anniversary of the restoration of the Jesuit order. The performance aired on <a href="/wiki/Rai_5" title="Rai 5">Rai 5</a> and was attended by former Italian President <a href="/wiki/Giorgio_Napolitano" title="Giorgio Napolitano">Giorgio Napolitano</a> and other dignitaries.<sup id="cite_ref-476" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-476">&#91;471&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-477" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-477">&#91;472&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-478" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-478">&#91;473&#93;</a></sup></li>

First performance: Capella Mariana 4 October 2015.<sup id="cite_ref-479" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-479">&#91;474&#93;</a></sup></li></ul>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Appreciation">Appreciation</span></h3>
<p>In the <a href="/wiki/Oratorio" title="Oratorio">oratorio</a> <a href="/wiki/Laudato_si%27_(oratorio)" title="Laudato si&#39; (oratorio)">Laudato si'</a> by <a href="/wiki/Peter_Reulein" title="Peter Reulein">Peter Reulein</a> (music) written on a <a href="/wiki/Libretto" title="Libretto">libretto</a> by <a href="/wiki/Helmut_Schlegel" title="Helmut Schlegel">Helmut Schlegel</a> <a href="/wiki/Order_of_Friars_Minor" title="Order of Friars Minor">OFM</a>, the figure of Francis appears next to <a href="/wiki/Mary,_mother_of_Jesus" title="Mary, mother of Jesus">Mary</a>, <a href="/wiki/Francis_of_Assisi" title="Francis of Assisi">Francis of Assisi</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Clare_of_Assisi" title="Clare of Assisi">Clare of Assisi</a>. In the oratorio, Pope Franziskus suggests a bridge from the crucifixion scene on <a href="/wiki/Calvary" title="Calvary">Golgotha</a> to the suffering of the present. He emphasizes the female talent and the importance of the charism of women for church and society. The texts of the <a href="/wiki/Encyclical" title="Encyclical">encyclicals</a> <i><a href="/wiki/Laudato_si%27" title="Laudato si&#39;">Laudato si'</a></i> and <i><a href="/wiki/Evangelii_gaudium" title="Evangelii gaudium">Evangelii gaudium</a></i> were used. The motto of the <a href="/wiki/Extraordinary_Jubilee_of_Mercy" title="Extraordinary Jubilee of Mercy">Extraordinary Jubilee of Mercy</a> also plays a central role.<sup id="cite_ref-Laudato_si-score_480-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Laudato_si-score-480">&#91;475&#93;</a></sup> The oratorio was premiered on 6 November 2016 in the <a href="/wiki/Limburg_Cathedral" title="Limburg Cathedral">Limburg Cathedral</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Laudato_si-Liebfrauen_481-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Laudato_si-Liebfrauen-481">&#91;476&#93;</a></sup>
</p>

<dl><dt>Notes</dt>
<dd>Pope Francis's initial <a href="/wiki/Grant_of_arms" title="Grant of arms">grant of arms</a> by the <a href="/wiki/Holy_See" title="Holy See">Holy See</a> was as <a href="/wiki/Roman_Catholic_Archdiocese_of_Buenos_Aires" title="Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Buenos Aires">Archbishop of Buenos Aires</a>, when he was <a href="/wiki/Cardinal_Bergoglio" class="mw-redirect" title="Cardinal Bergoglio">Cardinal Bergoglio</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-NCR_130-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-NCR-130">&#91;127&#93;</a></sup> in which the depiction of the Star and Spikenard were <a href="/wiki/Tincture_(heraldry)" title="Tincture (heraldry)">tinctured</a> <a href="/wiki/Argent" title="Argent">Argent</a>.<br />Following his election as <a href="/wiki/Pontiff" title="Pontiff">Pontiff</a> these are now tinctured <a href="/wiki/Or_(heraldry)" title="Or (heraldry)">Or</a>. The first version of <a href="/wiki/His_Holiness" class="mw-redirect" title="His Holiness">His Holiness</a>' arms released by the <a href="/wiki/Vatican_Press_Office" class="mw-redirect" title="Vatican Press Office">Vatican Press Office</a> depicted a five-pointed Star from Bergoglio's archiepiscopal version, but upon election as Pope his <a href="/wiki/Coat_of_arms" title="Coat of arms">coat of arms</a> assumed an eight-pointed star with the representation of the spikenard also being suitably differenced.</dd>

<dt>Symbolism</dt>
<dd>(On the shield) <i>Jesuit emblem</i>: In reference to Francis being a <a href="/wiki/Jesuit" class="mw-redirect" title="Jesuit">Jesuit</a>, the uppermost charge on the shield is the emblem of the <a href="/wiki/Society_of_Jesus" class="mw-redirect" title="Society of Jesus">Society of Jesus</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-OR_483-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-OR-483">&#91;478&#93;</a></sup> This <a href="/wiki/Charge_(heraldry)" title="Charge (heraldry)">charge</a> displays a radiating sun within which is the <a href="/wiki/Monogram" title="Monogram">monogram</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Holy_Name_of_Jesus" title="Holy Name of Jesus">Holy Name of Jesus</a> in red, with a red cross surmounting the <a href="/wiki/Christogram" title="Christogram">H</a> and three black nails below the <a href="/wiki/H" title="H">H</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-OR_483-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-OR-483">&#91;478&#93;</a></sup> <i>Eight-pointed star</i>: a long-standing symbol of the <a href="/wiki/Virgin_Mary" class="mw-redirect" title="Virgin Mary">Virgin Mary</a>. <i><a href="/wiki/Spikenard" title="Spikenard">Spikenard</a></i> alias nard: this flower represents <a href="/wiki/Saint_Joseph" title="Saint Joseph">Saint Joseph</a>; in <a href="/wiki/Hispanic" title="Hispanic">Hispanic</a> iconographic tradition St Joseph is often depicted holding a branch of spikenard.<sup id="cite_ref-VIS_484-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-VIS-484">&#91;479&#93;</a></sup></dd></dl>

<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Writings">Writings</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Pope_Francis_bibliography" title="Pope Francis bibliography">Pope Francis bibliography</a></div>
