<p>Pope Francis has written a variety of books, encyclicals, and other writings.
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Music_album">Music album</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Wake_Up!_(Pope_Francis_album)" title="Wake Up! (Pope Francis album)">Wake Up! (Pope Francis album)</a></div>
<p><i><a href="/wiki/Wake_Up!_(Pope_Francis_album)" title="Wake Up! (Pope Francis album)">Wake Up!</a></i> was released on 27 November 2015 by the label Believe Digital and contains speeches by Francis and accompanying music, including rock music.<sup id="cite_ref-485" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-485">&#91;480&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-486" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-486">&#91;481&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-487" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-487">&#91;482&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Films">Films</span></h2>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Documentary_film">Documentary film</span></h3>
<p>By 2015, there were two biographical films about Francis: <i><a href="/wiki/Call_Me_Francesco" class="mw-redirect" title="Call Me Francesco">Call Me Francesco</a></i> (Italy, 2015), starring <a href="/wiki/Rodrigo_de_la_Serna" title="Rodrigo de la Serna">Rodrigo de la Serna</a>, and <i><a href="/wiki/Francis:_Pray_for_me" class="mw-redirect" title="Francis: Pray for me">Francis: Pray for me</a></i> (Argentina, 2015), starring <a href="/wiki/Dar%C3%ADo_Grandinetti" title="Darío Grandinetti">Darío Grandinetti</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-488" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-488">&#91;483&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p><i><a href="/wiki/Pope_Francis:_A_Man_of_His_Word" title="Pope Francis: A Man of His Word">Pope Francis: A Man of His Word</a></i> is a documentary film with Swiss-Italian-French-German co-production, co-written and directed by <a href="/wiki/Wim_Wenders" title="Wim Wenders">Wim Wenders</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-489" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-489">&#91;484&#93;</a></sup> It premiered at the <a href="/wiki/2018_Cannes_Film_Festival" title="2018 Cannes Film Festival">2018 Cannes Film Festival</a> and was released in the United States on 18 May 2018.<sup id="cite_ref-490" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-490">&#91;485&#93;</a></sup> It includes extensive sections of interviews as well as stock footage from archives.<sup id="cite_ref-491" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-491">&#91;486&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>On 21 October 2020, the documentary <i><a href="/wiki/Francesco_(2020_film)" title="Francesco (2020 film)">Francesco</a></i> directed by film producer <a href="/wiki/Evgeny_Afineevsky" title="Evgeny Afineevsky">Evgeny Afineevsky</a> premiered.<sup id="cite_ref-:03_492-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:03-492">&#91;487&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:13_493-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:13-493">&#91;488&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>On 4 October 2022, the documentary <i><a href="/wiki/The_Letter:_A_Message_for_our_Earth" title="The Letter: A Message for our Earth">The Letter: A Message for our Earth</a></i> premiered on YouTube Originals, directed by Nicolas Brown and produced by Off The Fence in partnership with <a href="/wiki/Laudato_Si%27_Movement" title="Laudato Si&#39; Movement">Laudato Si' Movement</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-494" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-494">&#91;489&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Portrayal_in_film">Portrayal in film</span></h3>
<p>Francis is played by <a href="/wiki/Jonathan_Pryce" title="Jonathan Pryce">Jonathan Pryce</a> in the <a href="/wiki/Biographical_film" title="Biographical film">biographical</a> <a href="/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television)" title="Drama (film and television)">drama</a> film <i><a href="/wiki/The_Two_Popes" title="The Two Popes">The Two Popes</a></i> (2019), costarring with <a href="/wiki/Anthony_Hopkins" title="Anthony Hopkins">Anthony Hopkins</a> who plays <a href="/wiki/Pope_Benedict_XVI" title="Pope Benedict XVI">Pope Benedict XVI</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-495" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-495">&#91;490&#93;</a></sup>
</p>

<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Notes">Notes</span></h2>
<style data-mw-deduplicate="TemplateStyles:r1011085734">.mw-parser-output .reflist{font-size:90%;margin-bottom:0.5em;list-style-type:decimal}.mw-parser-output .reflist .references{font-size:100%;margin-bottom:0;list-style-type:inherit}.mw-parser-output .reflist-columns-2{column-width:30em}.mw-parser-output .reflist-columns-3{column-width:25em}.mw-parser-output .reflist-columns{margin-top:0.3em}.mw-parser-output .reflist-columns ol{margin-top:0}.mw-parser-output .reflist-columns li{page-break-inside:avoid;break-inside:avoid-column}.mw-parser-output .reflist-upper-alpha{list-style-type:upper-alpha}.mw-parser-output .reflist-upper-roman{list-style-type:upper-roman}.mw-parser-output .reflist-lower-alpha{list-style-type:lower-alpha}.mw-parser-output .reflist-lower-greek{list-style-type:lower-greek}.mw-parser-output .reflist-lower-roman{list-style-type:lower-roman}</style><div class="reflist reflist-lower-alpha">
<div class="mw-references-wrap"><ol class="references">
<li id="cite_note-2"><span class="mw-cite-backlink"><b><a href="#cite_ref-2">^</a></b></span> <span class="reference-text">Press reports have provided a variety of translations for the phrase. According to <a href="/wiki/Vatican_Radio" title="Vatican Radio">Vatican Radio</a>: "Pope Francis has chosen the motto <i>Miserando atque eligendo</i>, meaning lowly but chosen; literally in Latin by having mercy, by choosing him. The motto is one Francis used as bishop. It is taken from the homilies of the <a href="/wiki/Bede" title="Bede">Venerable Bede</a> on <a href="/wiki/Gospel_of_Matthew" title="Gospel of Matthew">Saint Matthew's Gospel</a> relating to his vocation: 'Jesus saw the tax collector and by having mercy chose him as an apostle saying to him: Follow me.<span style="padding-right:.15em;">'</span>"<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1">&#91;1&#93;</a></sup></span>
</li>
<li id="cite_note-3"><span class="mw-cite-backlink"><b><a href="#cite_ref-3">^</a></b></span> <span class="reference-text">Pronunciation: <small></small><span title="Representation in the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA)" class="IPA" lang="es-Latn-fonipa"><a href="/wiki/Help:IPA/Spanish" title="Help:IPA/Spanish">[ˈxoɾxe ˈmaɾjo βeɾˈɣoɣljo]</a></span> (Spanish); <small></small><span title="Representation in the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA)" class="IPA" lang="it-Latn-fonipa"><a href="/wiki/Help:IPA/Italian" title="Help:IPA/Italian">[berˈɡɔʎʎo]</a></span> (Italian)</span>
</li>
<li id="cite_note-51"><span class="mw-cite-backlink"><b><a href="#cite_ref-51">^</a></b></span> <span class="reference-text">This devotion has since spread to Brazil; it "attracts people with small problems."<sup id="cite_ref-49" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-49">&#91;47&#93;</a></sup> Bergoglio had an image of Mary Untier of Knots inscribed on a chalice he presented to Pope Benedict XVI in 2005.<sup id="cite_ref-50" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-50">&#91;48&#93;</a></sup></span>
</li>
<li id="cite_note-170"><span class="mw-cite-backlink"><b><a href="#cite_ref-170">^</a></b></span> <span class="reference-text"><a href="/wiki/John_Paul_I" class="mw-redirect" title="John Paul I">John Paul I</a>, elected in 1978, took a new combination of already used names, in honor of his two immediate predecessors, <a href="/wiki/John_XXIII" class="mw-redirect" title="John XXIII">John XXIII</a> and <a href="/wiki/Paul_VI" class="mw-redirect" title="Paul VI">Paul VI</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-169" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-169">&#91;166&#93;</a></sup> </span>
</li>
<li id="cite_note-453"><span class="mw-cite-backlink"><b><a href="#cite_ref-453">^</a></b></span> <span class="reference-text"><a href="/wiki/Pope_Emeritus_Benedict_XVI" class="mw-redirect" title="Pope Emeritus Benedict XVI">Pope Emeritus Benedict XVI</a> did not do this during his eight-year reign from 2005 to 2013; his predecessor, <a href="/wiki/Pope_John_Paul_II" title="Pope John Paul II">Pope John Paul II</a>, married a group of couples from all over the world in 2000, as part of the Jubilee for Families, and before that in 1994 during the church's Year of the Family, as well as presiding over a number of private marriages as pope.<sup id="cite_ref-452" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-452">&#91;448&#93;</a></sup></span>
</li>
</ol></div></div>
